Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\hanruzhou\.claude\skills\dotfiles-windows

# dotfiles-windows

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)

## Orientation
- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).

## Shell layout (pwsh)
- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).

## Packages
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.

## copilot-proxy
- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `codex-copilot`,
  `codex-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`, `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`),
  `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
  Automatic selection excludes policy-disabled, picker-hidden and embedding-only
  entries. Claude `--auto` is Claude-first; Codex is OpenAI-first; both share the
  named OpenAI order Sol > Terra > 5.5 > 5.4 > 5.3 Codex > Luna > mini.
- The shim retries only the same buffered request/model, emits SSE keepalives for
  silent streams, and has a stall watchdog; it never performs request-time
  cross-model failover. Timing knobs: `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS`,
  `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS`, `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS`.
- `copilot-here` writes only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The
  pinned copilot-api is installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`
  (never `bunx` at launch); `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls
  whether Node fetches the GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide:
  `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.

## Editors / terminal / tv
- VSCode & Cursor settings + keybindings are deep-merged into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`
  by `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20_editor_overlays.ps1.tmpl` (sources under `editors/`).
- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),
  and WezTerm (`~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`, pwsh as default shell) are managed too.
  Television channels live under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (`tv <name>`).

## What's enabled on THIS machine
- role: **workstation**
- Coding agents: true · Agent sounds: peon · SpecStory build (PR #191): true · GUI apps: true · WSL2 (Docker backend): true · WSL Ubuntu: true · Utility apps: true · Gaming: true
- Extra runtimes: true · Media: true · LLM: true · Tunnel: true · IaC: true · OpenSSH: true · herdr: true · Clink(cmd): true · try: true · translate: true · Rime/Weasel: true
- China mirrors: true · Backup mode: smart · Vim mode: true · Managed machine: true

## just recipes
`just --list`: `apply`/`diff`/`update`, `upgrade-scoop`/`upgrade-winget`/`upgrade-translate`, `lint`/`test`,
`docs-serve`/`docs-build`, `enable-sshd` (opt-in OpenSSH server, elevated),
`enable-wsl` (WSL2 for Docker Desktop; self-elevating UAC prompt, reboot after),
`enable-wsl-ubuntu` (WSL2 Ubuntu distro + cross-platform dotfiles; needs enable-wsl first),
`wsl-dotfiles` (bootstrap the cross-platform dotfiles into an existing WSL distro; VPN if behind GFW),
`install-fonts-machine-wide` (Alacritty Nerd Font fix, elevated), and
`docker-up`/`docker-down`/`docker-clean`/`docker-logs`
(the x86-Linux+KVM Windows-in-Docker test harness — see `docker/windows/`).

## Gotchas
- Windows-only repo — no `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os }}` branching needed.
- Editor settings use a `run_onchange` pwsh merger (not `modify_`) on Windows.
- tmux / zellij are Unix-only and intentionally absent; **WezTerm** (installed) is
  the stable native tmux-like multiplexer, or use Windows Terminal panes. **herdr**
  is an opt-in (`installHerdr`) native-Windows multiplexer in preview beta —
  installed via herdr.dev's `irm|iex` script, config at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`,
  with its official global skill exported from the installed binary on each apply.
  Runtimes are native via scoop (node/bun/go/rust/ruby) + uv for Python — no mise on Windows.
- **Rime input method** (opt-in `installInputMethod`): Weasel/小狼毫 via winget
  `Rime.Weasel`. Machine-scope NSIS, so applying raises UAC; and a bare silent
  install registers **简体** — `Install-Weasel` passes `--custom '/T'` for 繁體.
  The engine-level YAML in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` is **byte-identical to the
  parent repo's** copy (Squirrel/ibus-rime); only `weasel.custom.yaml` is
  Windows-specific. Edits need a redeploy, which
  `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
  See `docs/input-method.md`.
- **cmd.exe** is opt-in via `installClink`: Clink + starship/zoxide/fzf give the DOS
  prompt parity for **prompt + navigation only** (no pwsh funcs/aliases/modules).
  `starship.lua` is chezmoi-managed at `%LocalAppData%\clink`; the zoxide/fzf Clink
  bridges are fetched from upstream at apply. pwsh stays the default shell.
- **`translate`** (`installTranslate`, on for workstation) is the one tool built from
  source: no scoop/winget manifest, so the packages script runs a version-pinned
  `go install` into `~\.local\bin` (it installs `go` itself). First build takes
  minutes; re-applies no-op via a `--version` check. Upgrade with
  `just upgrade-translate`, not `upgrade-scoop`.
- This skill body is shared: `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/` and
  `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/` both render `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-26 08:50:35Z)**_

目前不是「智能偵測最快／可用 mirror」，而是 **chezmoi init 時選定的靜態政策**。

## 選擇優先序

`.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1:6-18` 的邏輯是：

| `managedMachine` | `useChineseMirror` | PyPI 來源 |
|---:|---:|---|
| `true` | 任意 | 公司 `packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io` |
| `false` | `true` | 清華 TUNA mirror |
| `false` | `false` | 不設定環境變數，使用官方 PyPI |

也就是：

```text
Managed/company feed > China/GFW mirror > 官方預設
```

這台機器目前：

```text
managedMachine = true
useChineseMirror = true
```

所以 **managed policy 優先**，會使用公司 package feed，而不是清華 mirror。

這份 policy 同時用於：

- `chezmoi apply` 的安裝程序：  
  `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl:35-38`
- 每次 interactive PowerShell 啟動：  
  `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1.tmpl:1-4`

## 沒有自動 fallback

目前沒有：

- 網路位置／GFW 動態偵測
- mirror health check
- 503 時自動切換 PyPI
- 公司 feed → 官方 PyPI fallback

這是刻意的。特別是在 managed machine 上，靜默 fallback 到 public index 可能違反公司 policy，也可能引入 dependency-confusion／不同來源混裝問題。

## 可以單次使用官方 PyPI

可以，而且不必修改 chezmoi 設定。

對這次 docs build，直接執行：

```powershell
uv run --default-index https://pypi.org/simple `
  --with mkdocs-material `
  --with mkdocs-static-i18n `
  mkdocs build --strict
```

一般 uv command：

```powershell
uv pip install --default-index https://pypi.org/simple <package>
```

一般 pip：

```powershell
python -m pip install --index-url https://pypi.org/simple <package>
```

也可以暫時覆寫目前 shell：

```powershell
$env:UV_DEFAULT_INDEX = 'https://pypi.org/simple'
$env:PIP_INDEX_URL = 'https://pypi.org/simple'
```

重新開 PowerShell 後，`05_mirrors.ps1` 會依 chezmoi policy 恢復公司 feed。

### 建議

- **Managed machine**：維持公司 feed，不做自動 fallback；故障時明確手動 override。
- **非 managed、GFW 環境**：啟用 `useChineseMirror`，使用清華 TUNA。
- **非 managed、一般網路**：兩個選項都關閉，直接使用官方 PyPI。

這比「偵測到 503 就偷偷換來源」更可預期，也避免安全與可重現性問題。

- `useChineseMirror = false` → 使用官方 PyPI/npm 等預設來源

可以，但我不建議單純把 `managedMachine` 改成 `false` 只為了繞過 package feed，因為它還控制其他公司機器行為。

## 改成 `managedMachine = false` 會怎樣？

你目前同時有：

```text
managedMachine = true
useChineseMirror = true
```

如果只改成：

```text
managedMachine = false
useChineseMirror = true
```

再執行 `chezmoi apply`，來源會變成：

| Ecosystem | 使用來源 |
|---|---|
| pip / uv | 清華 TUNA |
| npm | `registry.npmmirror.com` |
| Go | `goproxy.cn,direct` |
| Node binary | `npmmirror.com/mirrors/node` |
| rustup | `rsproxy.cn` |
| Ruby gem | Ruby China |

定義在 `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1:10-17`。

但 `managedMachine=false` 也會重新允許安裝：

- Grammarly：`.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl:497-499`
- Tailscale：`.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl:536-538`

所以它不只是 mirror 開關。

另外，切換後應開新 PowerShell；既有 shell 裡的 `$env:PIP_INDEX_URL` 等不會因模板改變而自動消失。由 corporate → China 時新值會覆蓋舊值；若切到 official 模式，最好開新 terminal。

## 三種現有模式

### Managed

```text
pip/uv → company packagefeedproxy
npm    → company packagefeedproxy
Go     → 官方預設
Rust   → 官方預設
```

公司目前沒有配置 Go/Cargo endpoint，因此 managed 並非所有 ecosystem 都走公司 mirror。

### Unmanaged + China mirror

```text
pip/uv → TUNA
npm    → npmmirror
Go     → goproxy.cn
rustup → rsproxy.cn
```

### Unmanaged + no China mirror

模板不設定環境變數，各工具使用官方預設：

```text
pip/uv → pypi.org
npm    → registry.npmjs.org
Go     → proxy.golang.org/direct
Rust   → static.rust-lang.org
```

## 對自動 fallback 的建議

我同意可以支援，但建議**不要用 `managedMachine=false` 表示允許 fallback**。比較乾淨的設計是把兩個概念拆開：

```text
managedMachine = true
packageSource = corporate | china | official
allowPublicPackageFallback = true | false
```

建議行為：

1. Managed machine 預設使用 corporate feed。
2. corporate feed 遇到 timeout、連線錯誤或 HTTP 5xx 時，才允許 retry。
3. 若 `allowPublicPackageFallback=true`，以官方來源重試一次。
4. `401`、`403`、TLS/certificate error 不 fallback，因為可能是明確政策限制。
5. 清楚輸出「corporate feed failed, retrying official PyPI」，不可靜默切換。
6. 不使用 pip/uv 的 `extra-index-url` 長期混用兩個 index，避免 dependency-confusion。

「測一次官方 PyPI 是否能連」只能證明**當下網路可達**，不能完全證明 IT policy 永久允許。不過可以把這個測試當作使用者明確啟用 `allowPublicPackageFallback` 前的 capability check。

我的建議是：

- 保留 `managedMachine=true`，繼續跳過 Tailscale/Grammarly。
- 另外加入 opt-in 的 public fallback。
- fallback 優先官方 PyPI/npm；GFW mirror 仍由 `useChineseMirror` 決定。
- 同時補上 official 模式主動清除舊 mirror 環境變數，避免 reload 後殘留。

# dotfiles-windows

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)

## Orientation
- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).

## Shell layout (pwsh)
- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).

## Packages
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.

## copilot-proxy
- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `codex-copilot`,
  `codex-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`, `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`),
  `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
  Automatic selection excludes policy-disabled, picker-hidden and embedding-only
  entries. Claude `--auto` is Claude-first; Codex is OpenAI-first; both share the
  named OpenAI order Sol > Terra > 5.5 > 5.4 > 5.3 Codex > Luna > mini.
- The shim retries only the same buffered request/model, emits SSE keepalives for
  silent streams, and has a stall watchdog; it never performs request-time
  cross-model failover. Timing knobs: `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS`,
  `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS`, `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS`.
- `copilot-here` writes only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The
  pinned copilot-api is installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`
  (never `bunx` at launch); `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls
  whether Node fetches the GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide:
  `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.

## Editors / terminal / tv
- VSCode & Cursor settings + keybindings are deep-merged into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`
  by `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20_editor_overlays.ps1.tmpl` (sources under `editors/`).
- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),
  and WezTerm (`~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`, pwsh as default shell) are managed too.
  Television channels live under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (`tv <name>`).

## What's enabled on THIS machine

## Gotchas
- Windows-only repo — no `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os }}` branching needed.
- Editor settings use a `run_onchange` pwsh merger (not `modify_`) on Windows.

  is an opt-in (`installHerdr`) native-Windows multiplexer in preview beta —
  installed via herdr.dev's `irm|iex` script, config at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`,
  with its official global skill exported from the installed binary on each apply.
  Runtimes are native via scoop (node/bun/go/rust/ruby) + uv for Python — no mise on Windows.

  `Rime.Weasel`. Machine-scope NSIS, so applying raises UAC; and a bare silent
  install registers **简体** — `Install-Weasel` passes `--custom '/T'` for 繁體.

  parent repo's** copy (Squirrel/ibus-rime); only `weasel.custom.yaml` is
  Windows-specific. Edits need a redeploy, which
  `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
  See `docs/input-method.md`.
- **cmd.exe** is opt-in via `installClink`: Clink + starship/zoxide/fzf give the DOS
  prompt parity for **prompt + navigation only** (no pwsh funcs/aliases/modules).
  `starship.lua` is chezmoi-managed at `%LocalAppData%\clink`; the zoxide/fzf Clink
  bridges are fetched from upstream at apply. pwsh stays the default shell.
- **`translate`** (`installTranslate`, on for workstation) is the one tool built from
  source: no scoop/winget manifest, so the packages script runs a version-pinned
  `go install` into `~\.local\bin` (it installs `go` itself). First build takes
  minutes; re-applies no-op via a `--version` check. Upgrade with
  `just upgrade-translate`, not `upgrade-scoop`.

  `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/` both render `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.

# dotfiles-windows

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)

## Orientation
- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).

## Shell layout (pwsh)
- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).

## Packages
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.

## copilot-proxy
- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `codex-copilot`,
  `codex-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`, `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`),
  `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
  Automatic selection excludes policy-disabled, picker-hidden and embedding-only
  entries. Claude `--auto` is Claude-first; Codex is OpenAI-first; both share the
  named OpenAI order Sol > Terra > 5.5 > 5.4 > 5.3 Codex > Luna > mini.
- The shim retries only the same buffered request/model, emits SSE keepalives for
  silent streams, and has a stall watchdog; it never performs request-time
  cross-model failover. Timing knobs: `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS`,
  `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS`, `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS`.
- `copilot-here` writes only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The
  pinned copilot-api is installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`
  (never `bunx` at launch); `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls
  whether Node fetches the GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide:
  `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.

## Editors / terminal / tv
- VSCode & Cursor settings + keybindings are deep-merged into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`
  by `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20_editor_overlays.ps1.tmpl` (sources under `editors/`).
- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),
  and WezTerm (`~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`, pwsh as default shell) are managed too.
  Television channels live under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (`tv <name>`).

60	        # works in a normal console, but an ELEVATED one is refused ("Running the

65	        $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod get.scoop.sh))

88	    # when only "mise" was missing.
89	    $missing = @($apps | Where-Object { ($_ -split '/')[-1] -notin (Get-ScoopInstalled) })

91	    Info "scoop install: $($missing -join ', ')"
92	    try { scoop install @missing } catch { Write-Warning "scoop batch error: $_" }
93	    # Anything still absent after the batch = failed (scoop keeps going past a bad one).
94	    $after = Get-ScoopInstalled
95	    foreach ($app in $missing) {

97	        if ($name -notin $after) { Register-Failure "scoop:$name" }

3	# UTF-8 console I/O. Without this, native tools that emit UTF-8 (git, winget's

14	# zoxide state, our own copilot module) so we set them for a tidy $HOME.
15	if (-not $env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME) { $env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME = Join-Path $HOME '.config' }
16	if (-not $env:XDG_DATA_HOME)   { $env:XDG_DATA_HOME   = Join-Path $HOME '.local/share' }

47	# the persisted user PATH, but a fresh session inside chezmoi apply may not have

54	    (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\Herdr\bin')
55	) | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path $_) } |
56	    ForEach-Object { [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($_) } | Select-Object -Unique
57	
58	$SepPaths = $env:PATH -split ';'
59	foreach ($p in $UserPaths) {
60	    if ($SepPaths -notcontains $p) { $env:PATH = "$p;$env:PATH" }
61	}

The supported machine-local mechanism is:

It is loaded after all managed fragments:

## Recommended implementation plan

1. Define official mode as “remove repository-owned source values while preserving unrelated user/IT configuration.”
2. Update `package-sources.ps1` to clean known repository endpoint values before applying the selected branch.

7	#   error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF

10	# was added. This test turns that into a local `Invoke-Pester` failure with the
11	# exact missing flag line to paste in.
12	#
13	# Matching is on the prompt's TEXT (3rd arg to promptXOnce), because that is
14	# what chezmoi's `--promptBool 'text=value'` parser keys on — not the variable
15	# name.

18	    $repo = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent

28	            Kind = $_.Groups['kind'].Value
29	            Var  = $_.Groups['var'].Value
30	            Text = $_.Groups['text'].Value

35	    $script:Flags = [regex]::Matches(

167	    } catch {

169	        Register-Failure 'herdr'
170	    }
171	}
172	
173	# herdr-plus — third-party herdr plugin backing the prefix+y (Quick Actions) and
174	# prefix+O (Projects) keybinds, plus the copy-pane Quick Actions this repo deploys
175	# to ~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/. We ship that CONFIG and
176	# those KEYBINDS, so not installing the plugin leaves both keys silently dead —
177	# hence installing it here rather than leaving it to the user.
178	#
179	# Requires go: the plugin's Windows build command is `go build -o bin/herdr-plus.exe .`
180	# (its sh-based build is skipped on Windows). go is gated behind installExtraRuntimes,
181	# so SKIP with an actionable message rather than failing when it is absent.
182	# `--yes` accepts the interactive "Install this plugin? [y/N]" prompt. Keep it
183	# after the repository argument: the Windows preview parses options in that order.
184	# NB: the keybinds must target the `-windows` action ids — herdr-plus scopes
185	# `quick-actions`/`projects` to linux+macos. See
186	# pitfalls/herdr-plus-action-does-not-support-platform-windows.md
187	function Install-HerdrPlus {
188	    if (-not (Have herdr)) { return }   # herdr install failed/skipped; nothing to add to
189	    $installed = $false
190	    try { $installed = ((herdr plugin list 2>&1) -join "`n") -match 'cloudmanic\.herdr-plus' } catch { $installed = $false }
191	    if ($installed) { Info 'herdr-plus plugin already installed'; return }
192	    if (-not (Have go)) {
193	        Info 'herdr-plus: skipped — needs go to build on Windows (scoop install go, or enable Extra runtimes)'
194	        return
195	    }
196	    Info 'herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus (backs prefix+y / prefix+O)'
197	    try {
198	        herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus --yes 2>&1 | Out-Host
199	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'herdr-plus' }
200	    } catch {
201	        Write-Warning "herdr-plus install error: $_"
202	        Register-Failure 'herdr-plus'
203	    }
204	}
205	
206	# --- Rime / Weasel (小狼毫) — Traditional Chinese input method ---------------
207	# Not routed through Winget-Install because two things need overriding:
208	#
209	#  1. The manifest is machine-scope NSIS, so `--scope user` can never work and
210	#     the install always raises UAC (same class as installWsl / installSshServer).
211	#  2. winget's silent switch for nullsoft is /S, and weasel's install.nsi maps a
212	#     bare /S to `WeaselSetup.exe /s` = register the TSF service as SIMPLIFIED
213	#     Chinese. Passing /T as well makes it use /t (Traditional) instead. Silent
214	#     mode also skips the 安裝選項 dialog and auto-runs WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy.
215	#
216	# `winget list` can't be used for the installed check: the manifest's ProductCode
217	# is "Weasel" but the ARP entry is the localized display name, so we read the
218	# InstallDir the NSIS installer writes to HKLM instead — which is also how we
219	# locate WeaselSetup.exe afterwards.
220	function Install-Weasel {
221	    $key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Rime\Weasel'
222	    $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
223	    if (-not $dir) {
224	        if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel (winget unavailable)'; return }
225	        Info 'winget install Rime.Weasel (machine scope — expect a UAC prompt)'
226	        winget install --id Rime.Weasel -e --silent --custom '/T' `
227	            --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
228	        $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
229	        if (-not $dir) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel'; return }
230	    } else {
231	        Info 'Weasel already installed'
232	    }
233	    # WeaselSetup's undocumented CLI (WeaselSetup/WeaselSetup.cpp). These two
234	    # only write HKCU, so they need no elevation and are safe to re-run.
235	    #   /lt          -> Weasel's own UI in 繁體中文
236	    #   /toggleascii -> Ctrl+Space toggles ASCII rather than the whole IME,
237	    #                   which is what makes global_ascii in weasel.custom.yaml
238	    #                   behave like a single 中/英 switch.
239	    $setup = Join-Path $dir 'WeaselSetup.exe'
240	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $setup) {
241	        & $setup /lt
242	        & $setup /toggleascii
243	    } else {
244	        Register-Failure 'weasel (WeaselSetup.exe not found; UI language + Ctrl+Space unset)'
245	    }
246	}

251	# Core CLI toolset — the shell baseline, always installed.
252	Scoop-Install @(
253	    'git', 'gh', 'glab', '7zip', 'make', 'just',
254	    'starship', 'zoxide', 'fzf', 'fd', 'ripgrep', 'bat', 'eza', 'glow', 'jq',
255	    'delta', 'lazygit', 'neovim', 'yazi', 'btop', 'pueue', 'television', 'tlrc',
256	    'uv', 'gnupg',
257	    # Runtimes are NATIVE via scoop, not mise: mise's activate/shims are
258	    # unreliable on Windows and it has no windows-arm64 bun build. node + bun
259	    # here; Python via uv (below); go/rust/ruby under Extra runtimes.
260	    # copilot-proxy needs bun/bunx.
261	    'nodejs-lts', 'bun',
262	    # LazyVim pins nvim-treesitter to the `main` branch, which compiles parsers
263	    # by shelling out to `tree-sitter build`. That CLI compiles via Rust's `cc`
264	    # crate, which only knows MSVC / GCC / Clang -- NOT zig (only the retired
265	    # `master` branch accepted zig). So the parser compiler must be a real gcc on
266	    # PATH; zig here does nothing. scoop's `gcc` is nuwen MinGW-w64, amd64-only --
267	    # which also matches the amd64 nvim (native on x64, x64-emulated on ARM64), so
268	    # this ONE line covers both arches (previously gcc was ARM64-only). Plus the
269	    # tree-sitter CLI `main` requires, and win32yank so `unnamedplus` yanks reach
270	    # the Windows clipboard. (Leaner gcc alt: scoop `mingw` = niXman MinGW-w64 UCRT.)
271	    'gcc', 'tree-sitter', 'win32yank'
272	)

274	# Make the newly installed client immediately usable. Elevated applies install
275	# Pueue 4's built-in Windows service (autostart at login); non-elevated applies
276	# start detached daemon mode. profile.d/12_pueue.ps1 covers future shell starts.
277	if (-not (Start-PueuedIfNeeded -InstallService)) {
278	    Register-Failure 'pueued:auto-start'
279	}

281	# gh-dash: GitHub PR/issue dashboard TUI (`gh dash`). It's a gh extension, not a
282	# scoop package, so it needs gh to be authenticated -- this no-ops on a fresh
283	# machine until `gh auth login`. run_onchange only re-fires when this script
284	# changes, so after authenticating, install by hand (`gh extension install
285	# dlvhdr/gh-dash`) or force a reapply (`chezmoi state delete-bucket
286	# --bucket=entryState`). gh-notify / gh-select from the Unix repo are bash-only
287	# extensions and are intentionally skipped on Windows.
288	if (Have gh) {
289	    gh auth status *> $null
290	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
291	        $ghExts = gh extension list 2>$null | Out-String
292	        if ($ghExts -notmatch 'dlvhdr/gh-dash') {
293	            Info 'gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash'
294	            gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash
295	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'gh-ext:gh-dash' }
296	        }
297	    } else {
298	        Info 'gh not authenticated -- skipping gh-dash (gh auth login, then reapply)'
299	    }
300	}

302	# node/bun come from scoop above (on ~/scoop/shims, reliably on PATH). We do NOT
303	# use mise here -- see the runtimes note in the core scoop list.

305	# Default Python, uv-managed. --default also creates unversioned python/python3
306	# (not just python3.x) in UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR (~/.local/bin, on PATH via 00_env
307	# ahead of the Store's python.exe app-alias). On uv 0.8+ `--default` lives behind
308	# preview mode, so it must be paired with `--preview` (older uv just ignored it) —
309	# without it, current uv errors: "`--default` is only available in preview mode".
310	if (Have uv) {
311	    Info 'uv python install --default --preview'
312	    $env:UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
313	    uv python install --default --preview 2>&1 | Out-Host
314	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'uv:python' }

317	# Make PSGallery usable non-interactively before Install-Module (NuGet provider

321	        Install-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -Scope CurrentUser -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
322	    }
323	    if ((Get-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallationPolicy -ne 'Trusted') {
324	        Set-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -InstallationPolicy Trusted -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
325	    }
326	} catch { Write-Warning "PSGallery prep failed (non-fatal): $_" }

371	# apprise -> Windows toast notifications for the Claude Code notify hook

373	# windows:// backend imports win32api/win32con/win32gui, so pull pywin32 into
374	# the tool venv (--with). uv tool bin (~/.local/bin) is already on PATH via

376	if (Have uv) {

382	# peon-ping — game-character voice lines for agent events (CESP player; packs
383	# from the OpenPeon registry). Installed regardless of the `agentSounds` tier so
384	# `peon preview` / `peon packs list` are always available to experiment with;
385	# the tier only decides whether HOOKS get wired, and that happens in
386	# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl.
387	#
388	# `--openpeon` reroots the whole install at the tool-agnostic ~/.openpeon so the
389	# installer never touches ~/.claude/settings.json — hook wiring is ours to
390	# declare (same rule the parent repo applies to workmux's `wm setup`).
391	# NB: the PowerShell installer's param block is
392	#   param([string[]]$Packs, [switch]$All, [string]$Lang, [switch]$Local,
393	#         [switch]$Global, [switch]$OpenPeon, [switch]$InitLocalConfig)
394	# — there is NO -NoRc (that is the bash install.sh flag only), and it does not
395	# touch $PROFILE, so nothing extra is needed to keep our profile clean.
396	# Idempotent: skipped once peon.ps1 exists.
397	$peonRoot = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon'
398	$peonHook = Join-Path $peonRoot 'hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
399	if (-not (Test-Path $peonHook)) {
400	    Info 'peon-ping (agent completion sounds, ~/.openpeon root)'
401	    try {
402	        # Upstream install.ps1 dot-sources scripts/install-utils.ps1 relative to
403	        # $PSScriptRoot when run via -File; it only self-downloads that helper
404	        # when $PSScriptRoot is empty (irm|iex). So stage BOTH files preserving
405	        # the scripts/ layout in a temp dir, then run install.ps1 with -File.
406	        $peonStage = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'peon-ping-install'
407	        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts') | Out-Null
408	        $peonInstaller = Join-Path $peonStage 'install.ps1'
409	        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
410	            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/install.ps1' `
411	            -OutFile $peonInstaller
412	        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
413	            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/scripts/install-utils.ps1' `
414	            -OutFile (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts\install-utils.ps1')
415	        & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $peonInstaller `
416	            -OpenPeon -Packs 'league_of_legends'
417	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping' }
418	        # The installer downloads the pack but leaves default_pack="peon" — a pack
419	        # that ships NO sounds — so a fresh install is silent ("No sound files
420	        # found for pack 'peon'"). Activate the pack we just seeded. Runs only on
421	        # first install (whole block is guarded on peon.ps1 absence), so a pack the
422	        # user later switches to via `peon packs use` is never clobbered.
423	        $peonCli = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\peon.cmd'
424	        if (Test-Path $peonCli) {
425	            & $peonCli packs use league_of_legends
426	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack' }
427	        } else {
428	            Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack (peon CLI shim missing)'
429	        }
430	    } catch {
431	        Register-Failure 'peon-ping'
432	    }
433	} else {
434	    Info 'peon-ping already installed — skipping (upgrade: peon update)'
435	}
436	{{ end -}}

438	{{ if .installSpecstoryBuild -}}
439	# EXPERIMENTAL SpecStory Windows CLI. There is no native-Windows release yet;
440	# Windows/WSL support lives in the unmerged getspecstory PR #191. Build it from
441	# source (opt-in) and drop specstory.exe in ~/.local/bin so the Copilot module's
442	# session auto-save (claude-copilot) can pick it up. Needs git (core) + go (enable
443	# Extra runtimes, or `scoop install go`). Treat as experimental — may break until
444	# the PR lands. Tracking + revisit criteria: backlog/specstory-windows-native-cli.md.
445	if ((Have git) -and (Have go)) {
446	    try {
447	        $ssCache = Join-Path $HOME '.cache\specstory-build'
448	        $ssRepo  = Join-Path $ssCache 'getspecstory'
449	        $ssBin   = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
450	        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $ssCache, $ssBin | Out-Null
451	        if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $ssRepo '.git'))) {
452	            Info 'specstory: cloning specstoryai/getspecstory'
453	            git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory.git $ssRepo
454	        }
455	        Push-Location $ssRepo
456	        try {
457	            Info 'specstory: fetching PR #191'
458	            $ssRemoteRef = 'refs/remotes/origin/pr-191'
459	            git fetch origin "pull/191/head:$ssRemoteRef" --force
460	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'git fetch of SpecStory PR #191 failed' }
461	            # Detached checkout leaves no local branch checked out, so the next
462	            # apply can safely force-refresh the remote-tracking ref above.
463	            git checkout --detach --force $ssRemoteRef
464	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'git checkout of SpecStory PR #191 failed' }
465	            $ssOut = Join-Path $ssBin 'specstory.exe'
466	            Push-Location (Join-Path $ssRepo 'specstory-cli')
467	            try { Info "specstory: go build -> $ssOut"; go build -o $ssOut . } finally { Pop-Location }
468	            if (Test-Path $ssOut) { Info "specstory: built $ssOut" }
469	            else { Register-Failure 'specstory-build (go build produced no binary)' }
470	        } finally { Pop-Location }
471	    } catch {
472	        Write-Warning "specstory-build error: $_"
473	        Register-Failure 'specstory-build'
474	    }
475	} else {
476	    Register-Failure 'specstory-build (needs git + go; enable Extra runtimes or run: scoop install go)'
477	}
478	{{ end -}}

572	# Clink = Bash-style line editing for cmd.exe, so starship / zoxide / fzf work in
573	# the DOS prompt too (scoop main bucket). pwsh stays the default shell; this is an
574	# opt-in secondary target with prompt + navigation parity only. Our starship.lua
575	# deploys via chezmoi (AppData/Local/clink/starship.lua). The zoxide / fzf Clink
576	# bridges have no scoop/winget manifest (and zoxide has no native cmd target), so
577	# -- like herdr -- we fetch them from upstream into the Clink profile dir at apply
578	# time. Network/offline failures are collected, never fatal; starship still works.
579	Scoop-Install @('clink')
580	if (Have clink) {
581	    clink autorun install *> $null                 # HKCU AutoRun; inject into every cmd.exe (no admin)
582	    $clinkDir = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'clink'
583	    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $clinkDir | Out-Null
584	    $clinkPlugins = @{
585	        'zoxide.lua' = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shunsambongi/clink-zoxide/master/zoxide.lua'
586	        'fzf.lua'    = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisant996/clink-fzf/master/fzf.lua'
587	    }
588	    foreach ($name in $clinkPlugins.Keys) {
589	        Info "clink plugin: $name"
590	        try { Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri $clinkPlugins[$name] -OutFile (Join-Path $clinkDir $name) }
591	        catch { Register-Failure "clink-plugin:$name" }
592	    }
593	    # fzf.default_bindings is a setting DEFINED INSIDE fzf.lua, and `clink set`
594	    # reloads the profile scripts first -- so this must run AFTER fzf.lua is
595	    # downloaded above, else the setting is unknown and the value is silently
596	    # not persisted (the *> $null swallows the "unknown setting" error).
597	    clink set fzf.default_bindings true *> $null    # Ctrl-R history / Ctrl-T files / Alt-C dir
598	} else { Register-Failure 'clink (autorun/plugins not configured)' }

604	# self-contained (Scoop-Install no-ops if ruby is already there). The pwsh
605	# integration lives in profile.d/32_try.ps1 (command: `tri`).
606	Scoop-Install @('ruby')

611	{{- else }}
612	    gem install try-cli 2>&1 | Out-Host
613	{{- end }}
614	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'gem:try-cli' }
615	} else { Register-Failure 'gem:try-cli (ruby/gem unavailable)' }
616	{{ end -}}
617	
618	{{ if .installTranslate -}}
619	# translate -- terminal translator CLI+TUI (github.com/daviddwlee84/translate).
620	# There is no scoop/winget manifest and no prebuilt Windows release, so it is
621	# built from source with `go install` -- the same path the parent repo takes on
622	# Linux (dot_ansible/roles/go_tools); macOS there uses the Homebrew tap.
623	# GOBIN/GOPATH mirror that unix convention: the binary lands in ~/.local/bin
624	# (already on PATH via profile.d/00_env.ps1) and the module cache in
625	# ~/.local/share/go rather than recreating ~/go.
626	#
627	# It is pure Go (modernc.org/sqlite -- no cgo) and cross-compiles cleanly for
628	# windows/amd64 and windows/arm64. The FIRST build is slow (several minutes: the
629	# embedded swagger-ui bundle + sqlite); later applies no-op via the version check
630	# below. Bump $translateVersion to upgrade -- editing it re-renders this script,
631	# which is what re-fires the run_onchange. go.mod needs go >= 1.26.4; the default
632	# GOTOOLCHAIN=auto fetches a newer toolchain if scoop's go is older.
633	$translateVersion = 'v0.5.2'
634	Scoop-Install @('go')   # self-contained: installExtraRuntimes may well be off
635	if (Have go) {
636	    $trBin  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\translate.exe'
637	    $trHave = ''
638	    # `translate --version` prints "translate version v0.5.2 ..."; a module-proxy
639	    # build carries no VCS metadata, so token 3 is exactly the module version. An
640	    # absent/unparseable answer just falls through to a reinstall, which is cheap
641	    # once the module cache is warm.
642	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin) {
643	        try { $trHave = ((& $trBin --version 2>$null) -split '\s+')[2] } catch { $trHave = '' }
644	    }
645	    if ($trHave -eq $translateVersion) {
646	        Info "translate $translateVersion already installed"
647	    } else {
648	        Info "go install translate@$translateVersion (first build takes several minutes)"
649	        $env:GOBIN  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
650	        $env:GOPATH = Join-Path $HOME '.local\share\go'
651	        go install "github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@$translateVersion" 2>&1 | Out-Host
652	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin)) {
653	            Register-Failure "go:translate@$translateVersion"
654	        }
655	    }
656	} else {
657	    Register-Failure 'translate (needs go; enable Extra runtimes or run: scoop install go)'
658	}
659	{{ end -}}
660	
661	{{ if .installInputMethod -}}
662	# Rime input method. The managed YAML under %APPDATA%\Rime is deployed by chezmoi
663	# itself (gated in .chezmoiignore); 重新部署 happens in
664	# run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1 once the files are on disk.
665	Install-Weasel
666	{{ end -}}

668	if ($script:Failures.Count -gt 0) {
669	    Write-Warning ("package install: {0} item(s) failed and were skipped:" -f $script:Failures.Count)
670	    $script:Failures | ForEach-Object { Write-Warning "  - $_" }

673	} else {

42	    # Keep the cache detached so a later fetch never tries to update the

9	#     network (idempotent — chezmoi init is safe to re-run), or
10	#   - install the dotfiles into a WSL distro you set up yourself.
11	#
12	# The frozen answers come from the persisted chezmoi config (`chezmoi data`), and
13	# the bootstrap is piped via `bash -s` on stdin — so `$(...)`, `$HOME` and quotes
14	# are expanded by the Linux shell, never mangled by PowerShell / wsl (see the
15	# pitfall doc). Behind a proxy / GFW: connect a VPN first (WSL routes through the
16	# Windows network). NB: the bootstrap here is kept in sync with the headless
17	# block of scripts/enable-wsl-ubuntu.ps1.
18	param(
19	    [string]$Distro = 'Ubuntu-24.04',
20	    [string]$WslUser   # default: the distro's own default user
21	)
22	
23	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
24	if (Test-Path variable:PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference) { $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $false }
25	$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)   # BOM-free stdin to wsl/bash
26	$env:WSL_UTF8 = '1'
27	
28	function Info($m) { Write-Host "==> $m" -ForegroundColor Cyan }
29	
30	# Frozen answers from the persisted chezmoi config.
31	$Name = ''; $Email = ''; $Mirror = 'false'
32	try {
33	    $d = & chezmoi data --format json 2>$null | ConvertFrom-Json
34	    $Name   = $d.name
35	    $Email  = $d.email
36	    $Mirror = "$($d.useChineseMirror)".ToLower()
37	    if (-not $WslUser) { $WslUser = $d.wslUsername }
38	} catch { Write-Verbose "chezmoi data unavailable; using defaults: $_" }
39	if (-not $Mirror) { $Mirror = 'false' }
40	
41	# -u <user> only if we have one (else use the distro's default user).
42	$wslArgs = @('-d', $Distro)
43	if ($WslUser) {
44	    $u = ((("$WslUser" -replace '.*\\', '') -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9_-]', '')).ToLower()
45	    if ($u) { $wslArgs += @('-u', $u) }
46	}
47	
48	$boot = @"
49	command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq curl; }
50	i=1
51	while [ "`$i" -le 3 ]; do
52	  script="`$(curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-connrefused --retry-all-errors https://get.chezmoi.io)"
53	  if [ -n "`$script" ] && printf '%s' "`$script" | sh -s -- -b "`$HOME/.local/bin" \
54	       init --apply "https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles.git" --promptDefaults \
55	       --promptString "What is your full name=$Name" \
56	       --promptString "What is your email address=$Email" \
57	       --promptChoice "Which profile=ubuntu_server" \
58	       --promptBool "Are you in China (behind GFW) and need to use mirrors=$Mirror"; then
59	    exit 0
60	  fi
61	  echo "chezmoi bootstrap attempt `$i failed (likely a proxy/GFW reset); retrying in 5s..." >&2
62	  i=`$((i + 1)); sleep 5
63	done
64	exit 1
65	"@ -replace "`r`n", "`n"
66	
67	try {
68	    Info "Bootstrapping cross-platform dotfiles in $Distro (headless)"
69	    $boot | & wsl.exe @wslArgs -- bash -s
70	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
71	        Write-Warning "dotfiles bootstrap in $Distro failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE) — usually a proxy/GFW reset fetching chezmoi/the repo from GitHub (curl 56). Connect a VPN (WSL uses the Windows network) and re-run: just wsl-dotfiles"
72	        return
73	    }
74	    Info "Done — open it with: wsl -d $Distro"
75	} catch {
76	    Write-Warning "WSL dotfiles bootstrap failed (non-fatal): $_"
77	}
78

114	        emit(template_text)
115	        sys.exit(0)
116	
117	try:
118	    import tomlkit
119	except ModuleNotFoundError:
120	    print(
121	        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
122	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
123	        file=sys.stderr,
124	    )
125	    emit(template_text)
126	    sys.exit(0)
127	
128	# Tables the template owns outright.
129	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
130	# Single keys re-asserted into an otherwise pulled-through table.
131	FORCED = {("update", "channel"): "preview"}
132	
133	with open(live_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
134	    live_text = fh.read().strip()
135	
136	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
137	try:
138	    live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
139	except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
140	    # A corrupt live file must not block the apply — enforce the template.
141	    print("modify_config.toml: live config is not valid TOML; enforcing template", file=sys.stderr)
142	    live = {}
143	
144	for key, value in live.items():
145	    if key in MANAGED:
146	        continue
147	    if key in doc:
148	        # The template also declares this table. Keep herdr's runtime keys and
149	        # let the template win only on the keys it actually sets.
150	        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(doc[key], dict):
151	            for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
152	                if sub_key not in doc[key]:
153	                    doc[key][sub_key] = sub_value
154	        continue
155	    doc[key] = value
156	
157	for (table, sub_key), forced_value in FORCED.items():
158	    if table not in doc:
159	        doc[table] = tomlkit.table()
160	    doc[table][sub_key] = forced_value
161	
162	emit(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
163	'@
164	
165	    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($pyFile, $pySource, $utf8)
166	
167	    $env:HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE = $tmplFile
168	    $env:HERDR_LIVE_FILE = $liveFile
169	    $env:HERDR_OUT_FILE = $outFile
170	
171	    $exe = $py[0]
172	    $rest = @($py[1..($py.Count - 1)]) + @($pyFile)
173	    & $exe @rest
174	    $rc = $LASTEXITCODE
175	
176	    if ($rc -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outFile)) {
177	        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("modify_config.toml: merge failed (exit $rc); emitting managed template")
178	        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
179	        return
180	    }
181	
182	    Write-StdoutBytes ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($outFile))
183	} finally {
184	    foreach ($f in $tmplFile, $liveFile, $pyFile, $outFile) {
185	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $f -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
186	    }
187	    foreach ($v in 'HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE', 'HERDR_LIVE_FILE', 'HERDR_OUT_FILE') {
188	        Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
189	    }
190	}

1	# Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1 — managed by chezmoi (Windows dotfiles).
2	#
3	# Thin loader: dot-sources every fragment in ~/.config/powershell/profile.d in
4	# sorted order, then the user's untracked local override. Keep logic in the
5	# fragments, not here — this file is intentionally boring.
6	
7	$ConfigRoot  = Join-Path $HOME '.config/powershell'
8	$FragmentDir = Join-Path $ConfigRoot 'profile.d'
9	$ModuleDir   = Join-Path $ConfigRoot 'modules'
10	
11	# Make chezmoi-managed modules importable (e.g. Copilot).
12	if (Test-Path $ModuleDir) {
13	    if (($env:PSModulePath -split [System.IO.Path]::PathSeparator) -notcontains $ModuleDir) {
14	        $env:PSModulePath = $ModuleDir + [System.IO.Path]::PathSeparator + $env:PSModulePath
15	    }
16	}
17	
18	if (Test-Path $FragmentDir) {
19	    foreach ($fragment in Get-ChildItem -Path $FragmentDir -Filter '*.ps1' | Sort-Object Name) {
20	        try { . $fragment.FullName }
21	        catch { Write-Warning "profile.d: failed to load $($fragment.Name): $_" }
22	    }
23	}
24	
25	# Untracked, user-local overrides (secrets, machine-specific tweaks).
26	$LocalProfile = Join-Path $ConfigRoot 'local.ps1'
27	if (Test-Path $LocalProfile) { . $LocalProfile }
28
```

```text
1	# Shell & environment
2	
3	How a PowerShell session is assembled — what loads, how to reload, and how
4	`PATH` and the XDG base dirs get set — **without ever touching the Windows
5	"Environment Variables" GUI**.
6	
7	## Profile loading
8	
9	`$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a thin
10	loader. It dot-sources every fragment under `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1`
11	in sorted (numeric-prefix) order, then your untracked `local.ps1` last. All the
12	logic lives in the fragments; the loader stays boring.
13	
14	| Fragment | Does |
15	|---|---|
16	| `00_env.ps1` | XDG base dirs, `$env:EDITOR`, PATH |
17	| `05_mirrors.ps1` | company-approved registries on managed machines; otherwise China mirrors when enabled |
18	| `10_tools.ps1` | `init` hooks: starship, zoxide, mise, atuin, fzf, direnv, tv |
19	| `20_aliases.ps1` | aliases + helpers (`reload`, `cas`/`cau`, modern-CLI shims) |
20	| `21_git.ps1` | oh-my-zsh `git`-plugin aliases ported to pwsh (`gst`, `gco`, `gl`=pull, `gcam`, `glol`, …) |
21	| `28_tldr.ps1` | `tldrf` — tldr with a `zh_TW → zh → en` language fallback |
22	| `30_apps.ps1` | app control (`applaunch`/`appquit`/…), audio, clipboard |
23	| `32_try.ps1` | `tri` — try (tobi/try) ephemeral dated workspaces (opt-in; inert without ruby) |
24	| `35_yazi.ps1` | `y` — launch yazi, cd to where you quit |
25	| `40_copilot.ps1` | import the `copilot-proxy` PowerShell module |
26	| `90_psreadline.ps1` | PSReadLine (vi mode, history) |
27	| `96_ssh_setup.ps1` | `ssh-setup-remote` (`Set-RemoteSshKey`) — interactive, ProxyJump-aware SSH key setup wizard |
28	
29	Modules under `~/.config/powershell/modules` are prepended to
30	`$env:PSModulePath` by the loader, so they import by name (e.g. `Copilot`).
31	
32	## Reloading
33	
34	`reload` **dot-sources** the profile back into the current session — the same
35	mechanism `$PROFILE` uses at startup:
36	
37	```powershell
38	function reload { . $PROFILE }                    # re-source everything
39	function cas { chezmoi apply  @args; . $PROFILE } # apply, then reload
40	function cau { chezmoi update @args; . $PROFILE } # git pull + apply, then reload
41	```
42	
43	!!! note "reload is additive, not a clean restart"
44	    Dot-sourcing **re-runs** the profile in place. PATH edits are idempotent
45	    (guarded, never double-added) and `Set-Alias` / `Import-Module` just
46	    re-apply — but anything a *previous* load defined that this load no longer
47	    defines is **not** removed. For a guaranteed-clean state, open a new pwsh
48	    session.
49	
50	## PATH: Windows vs Unix
51	
52	On **Unix**, `PATH` is a single colon-separated variable the shell rc
53	(`.zshrc` / `.bashrc`) assembles at startup — purely process-scoped, inherited
54	by child processes, no system database involved. Edit a dotfile, and it changes
55	on the next shell.
56	
57	**Windows** has two *persistent* layers stored in the **registry**, plus the
58	in-process copy:
59	
60	| Layer | Where | Scope |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| Machine PATH | `HKLM\…\Session Manager\Environment` | all users (needs admin) |
63	| User PATH | `HKCU\Environment` | your account, all your processes |
64	| `$env:PATH` | in memory, per process | this session + its children |
65	
66	At logon Windows concatenates Machine + User into each process's `$env:PATH`.
67	Editing the registry does **not** update already-running processes.
68	
69	### We change PATH without the GUI
70	
71	This repo touches `PATH` two ways, both scripted — the System Properties
72	"Environment Variables" dialog is never opened:
73	
74	1. **Persistent (registry User PATH) — scoop only.** When scoop installs, it
75	   writes `~/scoop/shims` into the User PATH programmatically
76	   (`[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', …, 'User')`), so scoop CLIs
77	   resolve in *every* shell and GUI app — no admin, no dialog.
78	
79	2. **In-process only — our profile.** `00_env.ps1` prepends `~/.local/bin` and
80	   `~/scoop/shims` to `$env:PATH` on every shell start, idempotently and only
81	   when the directory exists:
82	
83	   ```powershell
84	   $UserPaths = @(
85	       (Join-Path $HOME '.local/bin'),
86	       (Join-Path $HOME 'scoop/shims')
87	   ) | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path $_) } | Select-Object -Unique
88	   foreach ($p in $UserPaths) {
89	       if (($env:PATH -split ';') -notcontains $p) { $env:PATH = "$p;$env:PATH" }
90	   }
91	   ```
92	
93	`bootstrap.ps1` does a third, one-shot variant: right after scoop installs the
94	baseline tools it rebuilds `$env:PATH` from the `Machine + User` registry values
95	so the just-installed shims resolve **in the same session** (scoop persisted
96	them, but the running process's copy predates that write).
97	
98	!!! warning "`~/.local/bin` is pwsh-session-scoped"
99	    `~/.local/bin` is the Windows home for your own scripts and binaries — same
100	    path name as Unix. But unlike `~/scoop/shims`, it is added to `$env:PATH`
101	    **only** by this profile; it is **never** persisted to the registry. So it's
102	    on PATH inside pwsh sessions that load the profile, but **not** in Windows
103	    PowerShell 5.1, in GUI apps, or in anything launched outside pwsh. To make a
104	    binary there visible everywhere, add `~/.local/bin` to the User PATH
105	    yourself (`setx` or `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(…, 'User')`).
106	
107	Resolution order after the profile runs: `~/scoop/shims` → `~/.local/bin` →
108	inherited PATH (each is prepended, so the last one added ends up first).
109	
110	## XDG base dirs on Windows
111	
112	XDG and Windows split directories on **different axes** — XDG by *purpose*
113	(config / data / state / cache), Windows by *whether it roams* (Roaming vs
114	Local) — so there is no clean 1:1. The rough mapping:
115	
116	| XDG (Unix) | Closest Windows folder |
117	|---|---|
118	| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (`~/.config`) | `%APPDATA%` = `AppData\Roaming` |
119	| `XDG_DATA_HOME` (`~/.local/share`) | `%APPDATA%` = `AppData\Roaming` |
120	| `XDG_STATE_HOME` (`~/.local/state`) | `%LOCALAPPDATA%` = `AppData\Local` |
121	| `XDG_CACHE_HOME` (`~/.cache`) | `%LOCALAPPDATA%` = `AppData\Local` |
122	
123	`AppData\Roaming` bundles what XDG calls *config* and *data* into one folder;
124	`AppData\Local` bundles *cache*, *state*, and non-roaming data. ("Roaming" only
125	actually roams under domain Roaming Profiles / Enterprise State Roaming — on a
126	standalone PC it's just a folder with that name.)
127	
128	Rather than live with the ambiguity, `00_env.ps1` sets the XDG variables to
129	Unix-style paths, so **XDG-aware tools keep a tidy `$HOME` shared with the
130	macOS/Linux dotfiles**:
131	
132	```powershell
133	$env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME = Join-Path $HOME '.config'
134	$env:XDG_DATA_HOME   = Join-Path $HOME '.local/share'
135	$env:XDG_STATE_HOME  = Join-Path $HOME '.local/state'
136	$env:XDG_CACHE_HOME  = Join-Path $HOME '.cache'
137	$env:YAZI_CONFIG_HOME = Join-Path $env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME 'yazi'  # yazi defaults to %APPDATA%
138	```
139	
140	starship, atuin, zoxide, and yazi then read `~/.config`. Apps that **hard-code
```

```text
1	# Setup
2	
3	## One-line install
4	
5	From a fresh Windows PowerShell (or PowerShell 7) session:
6	
7	```powershell
8	irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows/main/bootstrap.ps1 | iex
9	```
10	
11	Or from **cmd.exe** — there's no native-cmd bootstrap to maintain; you hand off to
12	the in-box **Windows PowerShell (5.1)**, present on every Windows machine. Start
13	it, then run the one-liner interactively:
14	
15	```bat
16	powershell
17	```
18	```powershell
19	irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows/main/bootstrap.ps1 | iex
20	```
21	
22	Or download the script, read it, and run the **file** (safer — and it sidesteps
23	the Defender warning below):
24	
25	```bat
26	powershell -Command "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows/main/bootstrap.ps1 -OutFile $env:TEMP\bootstrap.ps1"
27	notepad "%TEMP%\bootstrap.ps1"
28	powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%TEMP%\bootstrap.ps1"
29	```
30	
31	Use `powershell`, **not** `pwsh` — pwsh isn't installed yet on a fresh box. The
32	bootstrap logic lives once, in PowerShell (`bootstrap.ps1`): cmd is a poor
33	language for the elevation / `PATH` / `chezmoi` steps, and these dotfiles are
34	PowerShell anyway, so a machine with *no* PowerShell couldn't use the repo.
35	
36	!!! warning "Defender may flag the cmd irm|iex one-liner as ClickFix"
37	    Wrapping the cradle on a cmd command line —
38	    `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm <url> | iex"` — can trip
39	    Defender's **`Trojan:Win32/ClickFix.*!ml`** machine-learning heuristic. It's a
40	    **false positive on the command-line _shape_**, not our script (a content scan
41	    is clean): a `powershell` process whose command line is a remote
42	    download-cradle (`irm|iex`) plus `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` / `-NoProfile` is
43	    exactly the shape the
44	    [ClickFix](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/08/21/think-before-you-clickfix-analyzing-the-clickfix-social-engineering-technique/)
45	    fake-CAPTCHA campaigns use. The two forms above avoid it — the cradle never
46	    lands on a process command line, or you run a file instead — and inside an
47	    already-open PowerShell the one-liner is fine. Bigger lesson: **never paste a
48	    `powershell -c "irm|iex"` handed to you by a web page or a "verify you're
49	    human" prompt — that request _is_ the attack.**
50	
51	`bootstrap.ps1` does the following, idempotently:
52	
53	1. Sets the execution policy to `RemoteSigned` for the current user.
54	2. Installs [scoop](https://scoop.sh) (user-scoped, no admin — but if the shell
55	   is already elevated it auto-passes `-RunAsAdmin`, which the installer
56	   otherwise refuses with *"Running the installer as administrator is disabled
57	   by default"*).
58	3. Installs `git`, PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`), `chezmoi`, and `uv` via scoop.
59	4. Refreshes `PATH` from the registry so the just-installed scoop shims
60	   (`chezmoi`, `pwsh`, `uv`) resolve in the same session.
61	5. Runs `chezmoi init --apply` (or `chezmoi update` if the source is already
62	   cloned) — chezmoi runs the repo's `.ps1` scripts under pwsh itself
63	   (`[interpreters.ps1]`), so it never relaunches the shell. Works from Windows
64	   PowerShell 5.1 or pwsh 7.
65	
66	!!! warning "Behind the GFW"
67	    Keep a VPN on for the bootstrap — scoop downloads git / pwsh / chezmoi / uv
68	    from **GitHub releases**. The `China mirrors` option only redirects
69	    pip / npm / cargo / go / node at runtime, **not** scoop's own downloads.
70	
71	## Init prompts
72	
73	`chezmoi init` asks a few questions once (answers are stored and never re-asked):
74	
75	| Prompt | Default | Meaning |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| Role | `workstation` | `workstation` = full desktop; `minimal` = shell only |
78	| Coding agents | on (workstation) | Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Copilot CLI, SpecStory |
79	| Agent completion feedback | `notify` (workstation) / `none` (minimal) | what a coding agent does when it finishes: `none` / `notify` (Windows toast) / `peon` (game voice line) / `both` — see [Agent completion sounds](agent-sounds.md) |
80	| SpecStory build | off | build the experimental SpecStory CLI for Windows from the unmerged PR #191 (needs git + go) |
81	| Windows GUI apps | on (workstation) | VSCode, Cursor, Notepad++, Terminal, Alacritty, PowerToys, Raycast, Docker Desktop, Discord |
82	| WSL2 backend | on (workstation) | WSL2 for Docker Desktop's backend; self-elevates (one UAC prompt), reboot required |
83	| WSL2 Ubuntu | off | install a WSL2 Ubuntu distro + bootstrap cross-platform dotfiles (needs `installWsl`) |
84	| WSL Ubuntu username | your Windows user | UNIX login for the WSL Ubuntu (passwordless sudo, auto-login) |
85	| WSL Ubuntu bootstrap | `headless` | dotfiles install mode: `headless` (frozen from Windows) / `interactive` / `none` |
86	| Utility apps | on (workstation) | CPU-Z, GPU-Z, TreeSize, VLC, Everything, ShareX, HWiNFO |
87	| Gaming apps | off | Steam |
88	| Extra runtimes | on (workstation) | rust, go, ruby via mise (node/bun/uv are baseline) |
89	| Media CLIs | off | ffmpeg, imagemagick |
90	| Local LLM tools | off | Ollama, LiteLLM |
91	| Tunnel tools | off | ngrok, cloudflared |
92	| IaC tools | off | Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu |
93	| OpenSSH server | off | install + enable sshd (needs admin; opens inbound TCP 22) |
94	| herdr multiplexer | off | native Windows terminal multiplexer (preview beta) |
95	| Clink (cmd.exe) | off | starship + zoxide + fzf in `cmd.exe` via Clink (opt-in secondary shell) |
96	| try (ephemeral workspaces) | off | Ruby CLI (`gem try-cli`): dated trial dirs + fuzzy selector; pwsh command is `tri` |
97	| translate | on (workstation) | terminal translator CLI + TUI, built from source with `go install` (first build takes minutes) |
98	| Rime input method (Weasel) | off | Traditional Chinese IME. Machine-scope installer — expect a UAC prompt; deploys the shared Rime `*.custom.yaml` to `%APPDATA%\Rime` |
99	| China mirrors | off | pip / npm / cargo / go / node via GFW mirrors |
100	| Managed machine | off | use company PyPI/npm registries and skip apps org policy usually blocks (Tailscale, Grammarly) |
101	| Backup mode | `smart` | snapshot existing files before the first apply (`smart`/`full`/`off`) |
102	| PSReadLine vi mode | on | vi editing in the shell |
103	
104	Re-run the prompts later with `chezmoi init` again, or edit
105	`%USERPROFILE%\.config\chezmoi\chezmoi.toml`.
106	
107	## Day-to-day
108	
109	```powershell
110	chezmoi diff            # preview pending changes
111	chezmoi apply           # apply local source edits only (no pull)
112	chezmoi update --init   # git pull + apply; --init re-asks any newly-added prompts (noop if none)
113	just upgrade-scoop     # upgrade CLI tools
114	just upgrade-winget    # upgrade GUI apps
115	```
116	
117	Inside a loaded pwsh session, `cau` (= `chezmoi update --init` + reload
118	`$PROFILE`) and `cas` (= `chezmoi apply` + reload) are the shortcuts. Prefer
119	`cau` as the normal "sync my dotfiles" verb — `--init` means a machine that's
120	behind on newly-added init prompts gets asked them on the next pull.
121	
122	## Local overrides
123	
124	Drop machine-specific tweaks or secrets in
125	`~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` — it is dot-sourced last by `$PROFILE` and is
126	never managed by chezmoi.
127	
128	## Git configuration
129	
130	`~/.gitconfig` is managed by a `modify_` overlay (`modify_dot_gitconfig.ps1.tmpl`).
131	`chezmoi apply` keeps a fixed set of keys in sync: `user.name` / `user.email`
132	from the init prompts, `core.autocrlf = input`, `init.defaultBranch`,
133	`pull.rebase`, `rebase.autoStash`, the Git-LFS filter and `http.postBuffer`.
134	
135	Everything the overlay does **not** own is preserved untouched — including the
136	`[credential "..."]` blocks Git Credential Manager writes out of band. That is
137	precisely why it is an overlay and not a plain managed file: a plain file would
138	clobber those blocks on every apply and break corporate auth.
139	
140	Put machine-specific settings in `~/.gitconfig.local`; the baseline wires it up
141	via `[include]` and chezmoi never touches it. Do not hand-edit `~/.gitconfig` —
142	managed keys are reverted on the next apply.
143	
144	`core.hooksPath` is deliberately not set, because Git honours it *instead of*
145	`.git/hooks/` and it would silently disable per-repository hooks such as the one
146	`pre-commit install` writes.
147	
148	## The Raycast / PowerToys clash
149	
150	Raycast and PowerToys Run both default their launcher to **Alt+Space**. Pick one:
151	disable PowerToys Run (PowerToys Settings → PowerToys Run → off) or rebind its
152	hotkey. The installer prints a reminder.
153
```
</details></tool-use>

 `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\pitfalls\packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md`

```text
1	# npm returns 404 against `packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io` — and the registry is actually fine
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): probing the internal Microsoft npm mirror
4	looks like a dead service —
5	
6	```
7	npm error 404
8	npm error 404 Note that you can also install from a
9	npm error 404 tarball, folder, http url, or git url.
10	```
11	
12	`npm ping --registry https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/` → **404**.
13	`https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/` and `/undici` → **404** in a browser or
14	`Invoke-WebRequest`. `npm view <pkg> --registry https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/registry/`
15	→ **404**. Yet DNS resolves and TCP 443 connects fine, and *some* tarball URLs
16	return 200. The natural conclusion — "this is only a tarball proxy for specific
17	packages, not a real npm registry" — is **wrong**.
18	**First seen**: 2026-07-29 (reached independently on two company laptops)
19	**Affects**: Microsoft corp machines where `registry=https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/`
20	is set at the machine level (`Q:\.tools\.npm-global\etc\npmrc`) and
21	`registry.npmjs.org` is blocked.
22	**Status**: not a bug — three probing mistakes.
23	
24	## Root cause
25	
26	`packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/` **is** a full pull-through npm registry.
27	Three separate things make it look broken:
28	
29	### 1. `npm ping` is not implemented — 404 does not mean unhealthy
30	
31	`npm ping` hits `/-/ping`, which this mirror does not serve. It returns 404 on a
32	perfectly working registry. **Never use `npm ping` as the health probe here.**
33	Use a metadata read instead:
34	
35	```bash
36	npm view undici version --registry https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/
37	# 8.8.0
38	```
39	
40	### 2. `/npm/registry/` is one segment too deep
41	
42	The registry root is `/npm/`, **not** `/npm/registry/`:
43	
44	| URL | Result |
45	|---|---|
46	| `https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/` | works |
47	| `https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/registry/` | 404 |
48	| `https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/` | 404 |
49	
50	The `/npm/registry/...` shape is what **Azure Artifacts** feeds use
51	(`pkgs.dev.azure.com/<org>/_packaging/<feed>/npm/registry/`), so it is an easy
52	habit to carry over. The give-away that `/npm/` is correct: the tarball path
53	that *does* work, `/npm/@scope/name/-/name-1.2.3.tgz`, is the standard npm
54	layout relative to base `/npm/`.
55	
56	### 3. The internal feed can be *ahead* of the public mirror
57	
58	Asking the internal Azure Artifacts feed for `undici@latest` yields a version
59	the public mirror does not have yet. Requesting that newer tarball from
60	`packagefeedproxy` then 404s, which reads as "tarball not provided" when it
61	actually means "that version isn't mirrored". At time of writing the internal
62	feed had `undici` 8.9.0 while the mirror's latest was **8.8.0**.
63	
64	## How to verify it is healthy
65	
66	```bash
67	R='https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/'
68	npm view undici version   --registry "$R"   # 8.8.0   -> metadata works
69	npm view left-pad version --registry "$R"   # 1.3.0   -> arbitrary public pkg, so no allowlist
70	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14' version --registry "$R"
71	```
72	
73	`left-pad` is the important one: an obscure package nobody on the machine has
74	ever installed proves this is a general pull-through proxy, not a curated
75	allowlist.
76	
77	Metadata rewrites `dist.tarball` to Microsoft's 1ES **public** mirror:
78	
79	```
80	https://ms-feed-25.pkgs.visualstudio.com/1es-public/_packaging/npm-public/npm/registry/undici/-/undici-8.8.0.tgz
81	```
82	
83	Note `npm-public` — packages served here are public npm packages, so a scoped
84	name resolving through it is **not** evidence that a package is internal or
85	that an internal-feed credential is required.
86	
87	## Prevention
88	
89	- Health-probe with `npm view <pkg> version --registry <url>`, never `npm ping`.
90	- Do not copy the `/npm/registry/` suffix from Azure Artifacts URLs.
91	- Before concluding a version is missing, check the mirror's own `latest`
92	  rather than the internal feed's.
93	- `npm config list` shows which file supplies `registry` (`builtin` / `global` /
94	  `user` / `env`) and masks credentials — prefer it to reading `~/.npmrc`, which
95	  contains a live token.
96	
97	## Related
98	
99	- [`copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module`](copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module.md)
100	  — the failure this investigation was chasing. It was not a registry problem
101	  at all; a stale deployed module was falling back to Bun, which ignores the
102	  configured registry.
103
```
</details></tool-use>

 `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\pitfalls\copilot-proxy-npm-etarget-but-doctor-says-installed.md`

```text
1	# `npm ETARGET` is followed by `copilot-proxy doctor` saying the requested version is installed
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `copilot-proxy restart` prints:
4	
5	```text
6	copilot-proxy: installing @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0 (one-time — later starts skip this) ...
7	npm error code ETARGET
8	npm error notarget No matching version found for @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0.
9	copilot-proxy: starting (@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0) on port 4141 ...
10	```
11	
12	A subsequent doctor contradicts npm:
13	
14	```text
15	Package
16	  ✓ installed        @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0
17	```
18	
19	The proxy can listen and serve models because it actually launched an older tree
20	left in `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`.
21	**First seen**: 2026-08
22	**Affects**: the Windows Copilot module before installed `package.json` metadata
23	became the installation postcondition, especially after the pin changed from
24	`1.13.14` to `2.1.0` on a lagging corporate npm mirror.
25	**Status**: fixed — stale package contents cannot satisfy readiness or receive a
26	new stamp.
27	
28	## Root cause
29	
30	The old installer used this success test after npm/Bun exited:
31	
32	1. any `node_modules/.bin/copilot-api*` shim exists, **or**
33	2. any `node_modules/@jeffreycao/copilot-api` directory exists.
34	
35	It did not read that package’s `package.json`. When npm returned `ETARGET`, the
36	old package tree remained, the weak filesystem predicate returned true, and the
37	installer wrote the **requested string** `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0` to
38	`.installed-spec`. Doctor trusted that stamp plus the same old directory/binlink,
39	so it claimed 2.1.0 and `start` launched the stale binary.
40	
41	The exact 2.1.0 release exists on public npm. In the first report, `ETARGET` was
42	therefore consistent with the configured corporate pull-through mirror not having
43	synchronized that version yet—not evidence that the public package never existed.
44	
45	Reference: [public npm metadata for 2.1.0](https://registry.npmjs.org/@jeffreycao%2Fcopilot-api/2.1.0).
46	
47	## Workaround
48	
49	First identify the registry and verify the exact pin **before** deleting the
50	working prefix:
51	
52	```powershell
53	npm config get registry
54	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version
55	# Compare only where direct public npm is permitted:
56	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/
57	```
58	
59	If only the corporate mirror is missing 2.1.0, wait/request synchronization or
60	use an approved registry for the reinstall. The fixed Windows module can also
61	recover automatically from this exact case: it downloads the published 2.1.0
62	runtime files from jsDelivr, verifies a baked SHA-256 for every file, and installs
63	only ordinary dependencies through the configured npm registry. Then deploy the
64	fixed module and reinstall:
65	
66	```powershell
67	chezmoi apply ~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1
68	Import-Module "$HOME/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psd1" -Force
69	copilot-proxy reinstall
70	copilot-proxy doctor
71	```
72	
73	Do not switch the managed pin to `latest`; that trades a diagnosable mirror delay
74	for an unreviewed gateway upgrade.
75	
76	## Prevention
77	
78	- Read installed `package.json.name` and `.version`; a directory or binlink is not
79	  proof of which package landed.
80	- Store requested spec plus verified installed name/version in the stamp, and
81	  compare the stamp back to live metadata on every readiness check.
82	- Write the stamp only after metadata and a runnable launch path agree.
83	- Keep filesystem metadata as the authoritative postcondition. The existing
84	  Windows `Start-Process` child shape has returned misleading exit-code data, so
85	  exit status alone is insufficient.
86	- Test the exact regression: stale 1.13.14 tree + desired 2.1.0 + failed installer
87	  must return false, write no 2.1.0 stamp, and never reach proxy launch.
88	
89	## Related
90	
91	- [`copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module`](copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module.md)
92	- [`packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path`](packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md)
93	- [`docs/copilot-proxy.md`](../docs/copilot-proxy.md)
94
```
</details></tool-use>

    fix(packages): support managed registries and offline fallbacks
    
    Use one shared package-source policy for apply-time installers and interactive PowerShell. Managed machines now select the company PyPI and npm pull-through registries, with managed policy taking precedence over optional China mirrors.
    
    Replace the Codex modifier's apply-time PyPI dependency with Bun's built-in TOML parser, recover historical BOM mojibake safely, and add a hash-pinned jsDelivr fallback for copilot-api 2.1.0 while dependencies continue through the configured npm registry.
    
    Force Copilot module reloads, document the package-source behavior bilingually, and add regression coverage. Full Pester: 204 passed, 1 skipped; strict docs build passes.

new file mode 100644

+++ b/.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+# Package-source policy shared by apply-time installers and interactive pwsh.
+# Precedence is intentional: a managed/corporate machine must stay on the
+# company-approved pull-through registries even if useChineseMirror was also
+# selected. NuGet is provisioned machine-wide by IT; Go/Cargo keep their normal
+# defaults because no company endpoints were discovered for them.
+{{ if .managedMachine -}}
+$env:PIP_INDEX_URL       = 'https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/pypi/simple/'
+$env:UV_DEFAULT_INDEX    = 'https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/pypi/simple/'
+$env:npm_config_registry = 'https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/'
+{{ else if .useChineseMirror -}}
+$env:PIP_INDEX_URL        = 'https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple'
+$env:UV_DEFAULT_INDEX     = 'https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple'
+$env:npm_config_registry  = 'https://registry.npmmirror.com'
+$env:GOPROXY              = 'https://goproxy.cn,direct'
+$env:MISE_NODE_MIRROR_URL = 'https://npmmirror.com/mirrors/node/'
+$env:RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER   = 'https://rsproxy.cn'
+$env:RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT   = 'https://rsproxy.cn/rustup'
+{{ end -}}

+## Package registries
+
+One shared policy is applied both at install time and in interactive shells
+(`profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`):
+
+- **Managed machines** route pip/uv through the company PyPI pull-through
+  registry and npm through the company npm pull-through registry. The PyPI path
+  was verified with `tomlkit==0.13.3`; its artifacts are served by the corporate
+  Azure Artifacts backend. IT already provisions the enabled company NuGet source
+  and disables nuget.org, so the dotfiles do not rewrite NuGet configuration.
+- **China mirrors** apply only on non-managed machines and route pip / npm / cargo /
+  go / node through Tsinghua / npmmirror / goproxy.cn / rsproxy.
+- No company Go or Cargo registry was discovered, so managed machines leave those
+  ecosystems at their existing defaults.
+
+The managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true. This prevents a GFW
+mirror from bypassing corporate package policy.
