<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\pitfalls\copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module.md`

```text
1	# `copilot-proxy` install dies with `error: ConnectionRefused downloading package manifest`
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `copilot-proxy start` / `copilot-proxy reinstall`
4	prints
5	
6	```
7	Resolving dependencies
8	Resolved, downloaded and extracted [6]
9	error: ConnectionRefused downloading package manifest @jeffreycao/copilot-api
10	WARNING: copilot-proxy: install stalled with the proxy env — retrying without it ...
11	Resolving dependencies
12	Resolved, downloaded and extracted [6]
13	error: ConnectionRefused downloading package manifest @jeffreycao/copilot-api
14	Write-Error: copilot-proxy: could not install @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 — run 'copilot-proxy doctor'.
15	```
16	
17	Both attempts fail identically (with and without the proxy env), so it looks
18	like a hard network block. `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg` stays empty and
19	`.installed-spec` is never written. Meanwhile plain `npm` works fine —
20	`npm view @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 version` returns the version, and
21	other global npm CLIs install without complaint. That mismatch is the tell.
22	**First seen**: 2026-07-29
23	**Affects**: corp/managed Windows boxes where the npm registry is an internal
24	mirror (here `packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io`) and `registry.npmjs.org` is
25	blocked, **and** the deployed Copilot module predates the npm-install branch.
26	**Status**: fixed — `chezmoi apply`.
27	
28	## Root cause
29	
30	Two things compound:
31	
32	1. **Bun does not use the corp npm registry.** `Resolving dependencies` /
33	   `Resolved, downloaded and extracted [N]` / `error: ConnectionRefused` is
34	   **Bun's** output format, not npm's. Bun reaches for `registry.npmjs.org`,
35	   which the corp network blocks, hence `ConnectionRefused`. npm, by contrast,
36	   honours the `registry=` line in `~/.npmrc` (and the machine-level npmrc), so
37	   the same package resolves instantly.
38	2. **The deployed module was stale.** `Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry` prefers npm
39	   when `npm.cmd` is on PATH and only falls back to Bun otherwise — but that
40	   npm branch was added in commit `5351411`. The copy at
41	   `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1` still had the
42	   **Bun-only** version, because `chezmoi apply` had not been run since. The
43	   source tree was correct; the deployed file was not.
44	
45	So the error says "network", the real answer is "your deployed module is behind
46	your source tree". `chezmoi status` had been flagging it the whole time:
47	
48	```
49	 M .config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1
50	```
51	
52	## Workaround
53	
54	```powershell
55	chezmoi status                 # look for a modified Copilot.psm1
56	chezmoi apply ~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1
57	copilot-proxy reinstall        # now uses npm
58	# copilot-proxy: installed @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 -> ...\copilot-api\pkg
59	```
60	
61	Successful run takes ~22s and reports `added 149 packages`.
62	
63	A full `chezmoi apply` also works but runs the `run_onchange` package installers
64	(scoop/winget/npm), which can take many minutes; target the single file when
65	you only need the module refreshed.
66	
67	## Prevention
68	
69	- **Check `chezmoi status` before debugging any behaviour of a chezmoi-managed
70	  script.** A stale deployed copy reproduces bugs that no longer exist in the
71	  source, and nothing warns you.
72	- Do **not** conclude "the registry is broken" from a Bun error. Confirm with
73	  npm first — `npm view <pkg> version` uses the configured registry, Bun does
74	  not. See
75	  [`packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path`](packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md)
76	  for how to probe the registry correctly.
77	- This is why `Copilot.psm1` carries the warning
78	  `npm.cmd not found; falling back to Bun (authenticated Azure Artifacts feeds require npm)`
79	  — if you see that line, the Bun path is about to be taken and will fail on a
80	  corp network.
81	
82	## Related
83	
84	- [`packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path`](packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md)
85	  — the companion trap: probing the internal registry the wrong way and
86	  concluding it is broken.
87	- `docs/copilot-proxy.md` — module overview; note it lists **bun** as the only
88	  prerequisite, which is true for *running* the proxy but not for *installing*
89	  the package on a corp feed.
90
```

## Summary

The repository has centralized source selection but no general fallback layer.

- Corporate source policy currently applies only to **PyPI/uv package resolution** and **npm registry resolution**.
- There is no opt-in corporate-to-public fallback toggle, no package-manager error classifier, and no helper that retries with a different source.
- Most package commands stream output and retain only `$LASTEXITCODE`, so their output cannot currently be classified.
- The current policy does not guarantee a single index per attempt if pre-existing extra/scoped registry configuration exists.
- No direct `pip`, `rustup`, `cargo`, `node`, or `npx` commands occur in the requested apply/recipe surfaces.
- No files were edited.

## 1. Source-policy definition and propagation

### Central policy

`C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\.chezmoitemplates\package-sources.ps1`

- Lines 1-5 document corporate precedence and explicitly say no company Go/Cargo endpoints were discovered.
- Lines 6-9 select the corporate feeds:
  - `PIP_INDEX_URL`

## 6. Obstacles to “no mixed indexes”

The current source policy sets a default/primary source, but does not sanitize other source inputs.

Repository-wide searches found no handling for:

- `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`
- `UV_INDEX`
- `UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`
- scoped npm registries
- `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`
- Cargo source replacement

Consequences:

- A corporate uv attempt can still see additional indexes from uv configuration.
- A pip command can retain an extra index from environment/configuration.
- npm scoped packages such as `@openai/*` or `@github/*` can be redirected by scoped npm configuration independently of the default registry.
- The bare public/default Gem path can use multiple configured sources.
- Go’s China value explicitly contains a two-source sequence:
  `https://goproxy.cn,direct`.

Even with exclusive command-line sources, caches are a separate provenance question: a resolver can reuse artifacts cached from an earlier source. “No mixed indexes” is achievable by source sanitization; “single-source artifacts” may additionally require isolated/no-cache execution.

## 7. Recommended fallback boundary

A safe opt-in design should target only commands currently backed by corporate feeds:

1. npm global installation and update:
   - main installer lines 131-151;
   - just recipe lines 35-37.
2. uv/PyPI dependency resolution:
   - Apprise lines 371-380;
   - LiteLLM lines 542-546;
   - Herdr Tomlkit modifier lines 73-79 and 171-179;
   - docs recipes lines 111-117.

It should not automatically wrap:

- `uv python install`;
- Scoop Node/Go/Rust/Ruby/uv downloads;
- Go builds or installs;
- Rustup/Cargo;
- RubyGems;
- Git clones;
- Herdr/Peon/CDN installers;

because no corporate source is configured for those paths.

### Suggested behavior

- Add a default-false fallback prompt effective only on managed machines.
- Keep the corporate environment as the persistent/default policy.
- For each eligible command:
  1. run against only the corporate source;
  2. capture exit code and combined diagnostics;
  3. retry against only the public source when the failure is narrowly eligible;
  4. restore all environment/configuration state afterward.
- Never configure corporate and public indexes simultaneously.
- Emit modifier diagnostics only to stderr/host.
- Split the batched npm update into package-level attempts.

### Conservative eligibility

npm:

- Eligible: actual install/update `ETARGET`, `notarget`, or package/version `E404`.
- Do not use `npm ping`:  
  `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\pitfalls\packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md:29-38` documents that the healthy corporate mirror does not implement `/-/ping`.
- Ineligible: authentication/authorization, TLS, connectivity, timeout, filesystem lock, lifecycle-script, or policy failures.

uv:

- Eligible only when output clearly identifies a distribution/version absent from the selected registry.
- Generic “no solution” should not automatically qualify because it can represent dependency incompatibility rather than mirror lag.
- Authentication, policy, TLS, timeout, and general solver errors should not trigger public fallback.

Coverage should include:

- fallback disabled by default;
- fallback effective only for the intended managed configuration;
- corporate success produces one attempt;
- eligible corporate absence produces exactly one public retry;
- 401/403/TLS/network/timeout/general resolution failures do not retry;
- exactly one registry/index is visible to each child;
- extra/scoped configuration is neutralized;
- environment is restored after success, fallback, exception, and timeout;
- output remains visible while also being classifiable;
- Herdr modifier stdout contains only TOML;
- npm packages are retried independently;
- managed-plus-China does not select Ruby China;
- rendered scripts include fallback configuration so run-onchange hashing notices policy changes.

Design package fallback implementation

```text
## Recommended architecture

Implement one reusable PowerShell library at:

`C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\scripts\package-source-runner.ps1`

It should have two responsibilities:

1. Run a native package-manager command in a child process with an isolated source configuration.
2. Classify a failed corporate attempt and, only when explicitly allowed, run exactly one public-only attempt.

Keep `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` responsible only for persistent interactive-shell policy and convergence. Do not put fallback logic or simultaneous corporate/public indexes into that template.

### Policy model

Add one init value:

```text
allowPublicPackageFallback = false
```

Semantics:

- `managedMachine` continues to:
  - select corporate PyPI/npm sources;
  - suppress Grammarly and Tailscale;
  - take precedence over `useChineseMirror`.
- `useChineseMirror` remains an independent mirror preference for unmanaged machines.
- `allowPublicPackageFallback` only permits eligible corporate-first uv/npm commands to make a second public attempt.
- It has no effect when `managedMachine=false`.
- Interactive environments always contain at most one source. Never configure public as an extra index beside corporate.

## Helper API and behavior

Expose a testable entry point shaped like:

```powershell
Invoke-PackageSourceCommand `
    -Manager uv|npm `
    -Executable <resolved executable> `
    -Arguments <string[]> `
    -Operation <diagnostic label> `
    -PackageSpec <optional npm package or uv requirement> `
    -ManagedMachine <bool> `
    -AllowPublicFallback <bool> `
    -OutputMode Host|StandardError|Capture `
    -Environment <optional child-only variables> `
    -TimeoutSeconds 600
```

Return a structured object rather than only `$LASTEXITCODE`:

```text
Succeeded
ExitCode
TimedOut
FallbackUsed
FailureClass
Attempts[]
Stdout
Stderr
```

Each attempt record should contain its source kind, exit code, timeout state, captured output, and classification.

Supporting internal functions should be:

- `Invoke-CapturedPackageProcess`
  - Uses `ProcessStartInfo`.
  - Reads stdout and stderr asynchronously to avoid deadlocks.
  - Retains output for classification.
  - Streams text while running in `Host` mode.
  - Routes both child streams and helper diagnostics to stderr in `StandardError` mode.
  - Kills the process tree on timeout.
- `Get-PackageSourceAttempt`
  - Produces the exact corporate or public command/environment.
- `Get-PackageFailureClass`
  - Applies deny-first, manager-specific classification.
- `Test-PackageFallbackEligible`
  - Returns true only for the approved classes.
- `Get-ChezmoiPackageSourceSettings`
  - Used by `justfile`; reads `chezmoi data --format=json` and extracts only `managedMachine` and `allowPublicPackageFallback`.

All source overrides must be placed in `ProcessStartInfo.Environment` or command arguments. Do not mutate the parent PowerShell environment, so success, failure, timeout, and exceptions inherently preserve it.

For Herdr, pass `HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE`, `HERDR_LIVE_FILE`, and `HERDR_OUT_FILE` through the child environment as well. This fixes the current remove-in-`finally` behavior, which loses pre-existing values rather than restoring them.

### Diagnostics

Print one explicit line for each decision:

```text
package-source[uv:apprise]: attempt 1/2 using corporate PyPI
package-source[uv:apprise]: corporate attempt failed: http-5xx (HTTP 503)
package-source[uv:apprise]: public fallback enabled; retrying with public PyPI only
```

For a denied retry:

```text
package-source[npm:@openai/codex]: corporate attempt failed: auth-policy (HTTP 403)
package-source[npm:@openai/codex]: public fallback not permitted for auth-policy; not retrying
```

When the toggle is false, say so explicitly. Never print npmrc contents, environment dumps, auth tokens, or URLs containing user-info credentials.

## Exact fallback classification

Classification must be deny-first. If output matches both a deny class and an eligible class, the deny class wins.

### Eligible

1. **`timeout`**
   - Runner-enforced timeout.
   - Explicit request timeout, including HTTP 408.
   - Codes/phrases such as:
     - `ETIMEDOUT`
     - `ESOCKETTIMEDOUT`
     - `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`
     - `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`
     - `timed out`
     - `request timeout`

2. **`transient-network`**
   - `ECONNRESET`
   - `ECONNREFUSED`
   - `EAI_AGAIN`
   - `ENETUNREACH`
   - `EHOSTUNREACH`
   - `socket hang up`
   - `connection reset`
   - `connection refused`
   - temporary DNS failure
   - `ENOTFOUND` or “could not resolve host” only when the failed host is the configured corporate endpoint

3. **`http-5xx`**
   - Explicit HTTP status 500–599.
   - npm `E500`–`E599`.
   - Require HTTP/status/error context so an unrelated package version containing a three-digit number cannot trigger fallback.

4. **`mirror-absence`**
   - npm:
     - `E404`/404 tied to a package metadata or tarball URL on `packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io` or its documented `*.pkgs.visualstudio.com` backend.
     - `ETARGET`.
     - `No matching version found`.
     - `is not in this registry`.
   - uv:
     - `was not found in the package registry`.
     - `Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement`.
     - `No matching distribution found`.
     - A 404 explicitly tied to the configured corporate package endpoint.
   - A bare uv `No solution found` is not sufficient.

### Never eligible

- **Authentication or authorization**
  - HTTP 401/403, `E401`, `E403`, unauthorized, forbidden, authentication required, invalid authentication.
- **TLS/certificate**
  - certificate verification failures, expired certificates, unknown issuer, self-signed chain, TLS/SSL handshake or peer-certificate errors.
- **Policy**
  - explicitly blocked/prohibited by administrator, organization, or policy.
- **Rate limiting**
  - HTTP 429 is a 4xx and must not be treated as a transient-network fallback.
- **Generic resolution**
  - npm `ERESOLVE`.
  - uv `No solution found` without explicit registry absence.
  - incompatible Python/platform/version constraints.
- **Build/install**
  - wheel or sdist build failure, compiler failure, postinstall failure, subprocess error.
- **Local state**
  - `EPERM`, `EACCES`, `EBUSY`, locked executable, disk-full, invalid arguments.
- **Runner failures**
  - executable missing, child launch error, malformed command.

There is one corporate attempt and at most one public attempt. Do not loop across sources.

## Source isolation

### uv

Corporate attempt:

```powershell
uv <subcommand> `
  --no-config `
  --default-index https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/pypi/simple/ `
  --index-strategy first-index `
  <remaining arguments>
```

Public attempt:

```powershell
uv <subcommand> `
  --no-config `
  --default-index https://pypi.org/simple `
  --index-strategy first-index `
  <remaining arguments>
```

Remove the following from the child environment for every isolated attempt:

```text
UV_INDEX
UV_DEFAULT_INDEX
UV_INDEX_URL
UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL
UV_FIND_LINKS
UV_NO_INDEX
UV_CONFIG_FILE
UV_INSECURE_HOST
PIP_INDEX_URL
PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL
PIP_FIND_LINKS
PIP_NO_INDEX
PIP_CONFIG_FILE
PIP_TRUSTED_HOST
```

Leave proxies, certificate-store selection, keyring settings, and cache settings intact. Do not add `--no-cache`, `--refresh`, or delete caches.

Both `uv run` surfaces must also use `--no-project`, because the repository’s `uv.lock` contains corporate artifact URLs and would otherwise contaminate a public attempt.

Exact eligible uv invocations become:

```powershell
uv tool install --no-config --default-index <one-url> --index-strategy first-index `
    --with pywin32 apprise

uv tool install --no-config --default-index <one-url> --index-strategy first-index `
    'litellm[proxy]'

uv run --no-project --no-config --default-index <one-url> --index-strategy first-index `
    --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python <merge-script>

uv run --no-project --no-config --default-index <one-url> --index-strategy first-index `
    --with mkdocs-material --with mkdocs-static-i18n mkdocs serve
```

The build recipe uses the same shape with `mkdocs build --strict`.

Do not wrap `uv python install`; Python runtime downloads have no corporate package index.

### npm

Each attempt should:

1. Resolve npm’s current user/global npmrc paths without displaying their contents.
2. Create attempt-specific temporary npmrc copies.
3. Copy source-neutral configuration verbatim, including prefix, cache, proxy, certificate, and host-bound authentication entries.
4. Remove every active `registry=` and `@scope:registry=` assignment from the temporary copies.

# dotfiles-windows

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)

## Orientation
- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).

## Shell layout (pwsh)
- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).

## Packages
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.

## copilot-proxy
- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `codex-copilot`,
  `codex-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`, `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`),
  `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
  Automatic selection excludes policy-disabled, picker-hidden and embedding-only
  entries. Claude `--auto` is Claude-first; Codex is OpenAI-first; both share the
  named OpenAI order Sol > Terra > 5.5 > 5.4 > 5.3 Codex > Luna > mini.
- The shim retries only the same buffered request/model, emits SSE keepalives for
  silent streams, and has a stall watchdog; it never performs request-time
  cross-model failover. Timing knobs: `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS`,
  `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS`, `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS`.
- `copilot-here` writes only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The
  pinned copilot-api is installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`
  (never `bunx` at launch); `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls
  whether Node fetches the GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide:
  `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.

## Editors / terminal / tv
- VSCode & Cursor settings + keybindings are deep-merged into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`
  by `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20_editor_overlays.ps1.tmpl` (sources under `editors/`).
- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),
  and WezTerm (`~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`, pwsh as default shell) are managed too.
  Television channels live under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (`tv <name>`).

## What's enabled on THIS machine
- role: **workstation**
- Coding agents: true · Agent sounds: peon · SpecStory build (PR #191): true · GUI apps: true · WSL2 (Docker backend): true · WSL Ubuntu: true · Utility apps: true · Gaming: true
- Extra runtimes: true · Media: true · LLM: true · Tunnel: true · IaC: true · OpenSSH: true · herdr: true · Clink(cmd): true · try: true · translate: true · Rime/Weasel: true
- China mirrors: true · Backup mode: smart · Vim mode: true · Managed machine: true

## just recipes
`just --list`: `apply`/`diff`/`update`, `upgrade-scoop`/`upgrade-winget`/`upgrade-translate`, `lint`/`test`,
`docs-serve`/`docs-build`, `enable-sshd` (opt-in OpenSSH server, elevated),
`enable-wsl` (WSL2 for Docker Desktop; self-elevating UAC prompt, reboot after),
`enable-wsl-ubuntu` (WSL2 Ubuntu distro + cross-platform dotfiles; needs enable-wsl first),
`wsl-dotfiles` (bootstrap the cross-platform dotfiles into an existing WSL distro; VPN if behind GFW),
`install-fonts-machine-wide` (Alacritty Nerd Font fix, elevated), and
`docker-up`/`docker-down`/`docker-clean`/`docker-logs`
(the x86-Linux+KVM Windows-in-Docker test harness — see `docker/windows/`).

## Gotchas
- Windows-only repo — no `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os }}` branching needed.
- Editor settings use a `run_onchange` pwsh merger (not `modify_`) on Windows.
- tmux / zellij are Unix-only and intentionally absent; **WezTerm** (installed) is
  the stable native tmux-like multiplexer, or use Windows Terminal panes. **herdr**
  is an opt-in (`installHerdr`) native-Windows multiplexer in preview beta —
  installed via herdr.dev's `irm|iex` script, config at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`,
  with its official global skill exported from the installed binary on each apply.
  Runtimes are native via scoop (node/bun/go/rust/ruby) + uv for Python — no mise on Windows.
- **Rime input method** (opt-in `installInputMethod`): Weasel/小狼毫 via winget
  `Rime.Weasel`. Machine-scope NSIS, so applying raises UAC; and a bare silent
  install registers **简体** — `Install-Weasel` passes `--custom '/T'` for 繁體.
  The engine-level YAML in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` is **byte-identical to the
  parent repo's** copy (Squirrel/ibus-rime); only `weasel.custom.yaml` is
  Windows-specific. Edits need a redeploy, which
  `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
  See `docs/input-method.md`.
- **cmd.exe** is opt-in via `installClink`: Clink + starship/zoxide/fzf give the DOS
  prompt parity for **prompt + navigation only** (no pwsh funcs/aliases/modules).
  `starship.lua` is chezmoi-managed at `%LocalAppData%\clink`; the zoxide/fzf Clink
  bridges are fetched from upstream at apply. pwsh stays the default shell.
- **`translate`** (`installTranslate`, on for workstation) is the one tool built from
  source: no scoop/winget manifest, so the packages script runs a version-pinned
  `go install` into `~\.local\bin` (it installs `go` itself). First build takes
  minutes; re-applies no-op via a `--version` check. Upgrade with
  `just upgrade-translate`, not `upgrade-scoop`.
- This skill body is shared: `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/` and
  `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/` both render `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.

1	#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Runs under pwsh via [interpreters.ps1] in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl. chezmoi pipes the
5	# CURRENT target file into stdin and takes the new contents from stdout.
6	#
7	# WHY AN OVERLAY (this replaced a plain managed dot_config/herdr/config.toml):
8	# herdr rewrites this file at runtime — the onboarding flag, in-app settings
9	# popups, [session] / [remote] / [experimental] / [update] state. A plain managed
10	# file clobbers all of that on every `chezmoi apply`, which can re-trigger
11	# onboarding. The parent (unix) repo hit this and moved create_ -> modify_ on
12	# 2026-07-06; this repo's config was added five days later and still used the
13	# plain form. Same fix, ported.
14	#
15	# MERGE MODEL — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
16	#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
17	#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
18	#   - Every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file that is NOT managed and NOT already in
19	#     the template is copied across (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
20	#     [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
21	#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins).
22	#   - FORCED single keys are re-asserted INTO a pulled-through table, so the table
23	#     keeps herdr's own bookkeeping. Windows needs exactly one: update.channel
24	#     must stay "preview" (the installer rejects "stable" on Windows builds), but
25	#     [update] also holds herdr's last-check state, which we do not want to wipe.
26	#     This sub-key merge is the one deliberate divergence from the unix overlay.
27	#
28	# WHY tomlkit (not a hand-rolled emitter): herdr's config has an array-of-tables
29	# ([[keys.command]]) and comments worth keeping; stdlib tomllib is read-only.
30	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees >=3.11 -> stdlib tomllib), fall back to
31	# system python, then to emitting the raw template (a fresh host with neither
32	# still gets a full config — note we emit the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a
33	# fresh host stdin is empty).
34	#
35	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
36	# Validate the result with `herdr server reload-config` (empty diagnostics).
37	
38	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
39	
40	# modify_ scripts run under `pwsh -NoProfile`, so the deployed 05_mirrors.ps1
41	# fragment is not loaded here. Apply the same source policy inline before uv
42	# resolves tomlkit: managed machines must use the IT-approved pull-through feed.
43	{{ template "package-sources.ps1" . }}
44	
45	# Emit bytes verbatim so nothing re-encodes the config's ⭐ / box-drawing glyphs
46	# and no BOM or trailing CRLF churn creeps into chezmoi's diff.
47	function Write-StdoutBytes {
48	    param([byte[]] $Bytes)
49	    $out = [Console]::OpenStandardOutput()
50	    $out.Write($Bytes, 0, $Bytes.Length)
51	    $out.Flush()
52	}
53	
54	$utf8 = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)   # no BOM
55	
56	$templateText = @'
57	{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
58	'@
59	
60	$liveText = [Console]::In.ReadToEnd()
61	
62	$tmpDir = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()
63	$stamp = [System.IO.Path]::GetRandomFileName()
64	$tmplFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-tmpl-$stamp.toml"
65	$liveFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-live-$stamp.toml"
66	$pyFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-merge-$stamp.py"
67	$outFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-out-$stamp.toml"
68	
69	try {
70	    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($tmplFile, $templateText, $utf8)
71	    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($liveFile, $liveText, $utf8)
72	
73	    # Pick a Python. uv is in this repo's scoop package set; `python` is the
74	    # uv-managed default install (--default --preview creates the unversioned shim).
75	    $py = $null
76	    if (Get-Command uv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
77	        $py = @('uv', 'run', '--no-project', '--quiet', '--with', 'tomlkit', '--python', '>=3.11', 'python')
78	    } elseif (Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
79	        $py = @('python')
80	    } elseif (Get-Command python3 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
81	        $py = @('python3')
82	    }
83	
84	    if (-not $py) {
85	        [Console]::Error.WriteLine('modify_config.toml: no uv/python found; emitting managed template (runtime keys not preserved this run)')
86	        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
87	        return
88	    }
89	
90	    $pySource = @'
91	import os
92	import sys
93	
94	tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
95	live_path = os.environ["HERDR_LIVE_FILE"]
96	out_path = os.environ["HERDR_OUT_FILE"]
97	
98	with open(tmpl_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
99	    template_text = fh.read()
100	
101	
102	def emit(text):
103	    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
104	        fh.write(text)
105	
106	
107	try:
108	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
109	except ModuleNotFoundError:
110	    try:
111	        import tomli as tomllib
112	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
113	        # No TOML reader -> can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is.
114	        emit(template_text)
115	        sys.exit(0)
116	
117	try:
118	    import tomlkit
119	except ModuleNotFoundError:
120	    print(
121	        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
122	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
123	        file=sys.stderr,
124	    )
125	    emit(template_text)
126	    sys.exit(0)
127	
128	# Tables the template owns outright.
129	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
130	# Single keys re-asserted into an otherwise pulled-through table.
131	FORCED = {("update", "channel"): "preview"}
132	
133	with open(live_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
134	    live_text = fh.read().strip()
135	
136	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
137	try:
138	    live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
139	except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
140	    # A corrupt live file must not block the apply — enforce the template.
141	    print("modify_config.toml: live config is not valid TOML; enforcing template", file=sys.stderr)
142	    live = {}
143	
144	for key, value in live.items():
145	    if key in MANAGED:
146	        continue
147	    if key in doc:
148	        # The template also declares this table. Keep herdr's runtime keys and
149	        # let the template win only on the keys it actually sets.
150	        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(doc[key], dict):
151	            for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
152	                if sub_key not in doc[key]:
153	                    doc[key][sub_key] = sub_value
154	        continue
155	    doc[key] = value
156	
157	for (table, sub_key), forced_value in FORCED.items():
158	    if table not in doc:
159	        doc[table] = tomlkit.table()
160	    doc[table][sub_key] = forced_value
161	
162	emit(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
163	'@
164	
165	    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($pyFile, $pySource, $utf8)
166	
167	    $env:HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE = $tmplFile
168	    $env:HERDR_LIVE_FILE = $liveFile
169	    $env:HERDR_OUT_FILE = $outFile
170	
171	    $exe = $py[0]
172	    $rest = @($py[1..($py.Count - 1)]) + @($pyFile)
173	    & $exe @rest
174	    $rc = $LASTEXITCODE
175	
176	    if ($rc -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outFile)) {
177	        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("modify_config.toml: merge failed (exit $rc); emitting managed template")
178	        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
179	        return
180	    }
181	
182	    Write-StdoutBytes ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($outFile))
183	} finally {
184	    foreach ($f in $tmplFile, $liveFile, $pyFile, $outFile) {
185	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $f -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
186	    }
187	    foreach ($v in 'HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE', 'HERDR_LIVE_FILE', 'HERDR_OUT_FILE') {
188	        Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
189	    }
190	}

```text
1	# Shared Herdr agent-skill synchronizer.
2	#
3	# The installed binary is the version authority. `herdr --skill` emits the
4	# official skill compiled for that release, avoiding drift from a Git branch.
5	
6	function Resolve-HerdrExecutable {
7	    $command = Get-Command herdr -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
8	    if ($command) { return $command.Source }
9	
10	    if ($env:LOCALAPPDATA) {
11	        $fallback = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\Herdr\bin\herdr.exe'
12	        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $fallback -PathType Leaf) { return $fallback }
13	    }
14	    return $null
15	}
16	
17	function Get-HerdrSkillContent {
18	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$HerdrPath)
19	
20	    $start = [Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo]::new()
21	    $start.FileName = $HerdrPath
22	    $start.ArgumentList.Add('--skill')
23	    $start.UseShellExecute = $false
24	    $start.RedirectStandardOutput = $true
25	    $start.RedirectStandardError = $true
26	    $start.CreateNoWindow = $true
27	
28	    $process = [Diagnostics.Process]::Start($start)
29	    $stdoutTask = $process.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync()
30	    $stderrTask = $process.StandardError.ReadToEndAsync()
31	    $process.WaitForExit()
32	    $stdout = $stdoutTask.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
33	    $stderr = $stderrTask.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
34	
35	    if ($process.ExitCode -ne 0) {
36	        $detail = $stderr.Trim()
37	        if (-not $detail) { $detail = "exit $($process.ExitCode)" }
38	        throw "herdr --skill failed: $detail"
39	    }
40	    return $stdout
41	}
42	
43	function Write-HerdrSkillContent {
44	    param(
45	        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Content,
46	        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$Destinations
47	    )
48	
49	    if ($Content -notmatch '\A---\r?\n' -or $Content -notmatch '(?m)^name:\s*herdr\s*$') {
50	        Write-Warning 'herdr --skill returned invalid skill content; keeping existing copies'
51	        return $false
52	    }
53	
54	    $encoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
55	    foreach ($destination in $Destinations) {
56	        $directory = Split-Path -Parent $destination
57	        $temporary = Join-Path $directory ('.SKILL.md.tmp.' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
58	        try {
59	            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $directory | Out-Null
60	            if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $destination -PathType Leaf) -and
61	                ([IO.File]::ReadAllText($destination) -ceq $Content)) {
62	                continue
63	            }
64	            [IO.File]::WriteAllText($temporary, $Content, $encoding)
65	            [IO.File]::Move($temporary, $destination, $true)
66	        } catch {
67	            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $temporary -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
68	            Write-Warning "Could not synchronize Herdr skill at ${destination}: $_"
69	            return $false
70	        }
71	    }
72	    return $true
73	}
74	
75	function Sync-HerdrSkill {
76	    param(
77	        [string[]]$Destinations = @(
78	            (Join-Path $HOME '.agents\skills\herdr\SKILL.md'),
79	            (Join-Path $HOME '.claude\skills\herdr\SKILL.md')
80	        ),
81	        [string]$HerdrPath = (Resolve-HerdrExecutable)
82	    )
83	
84	    if (-not $HerdrPath) {
85	        Write-Warning 'Herdr is not installed; keeping any existing global skill copies'
86	        return $false
87	    }
88	
89	    try {
90	        $content = Get-HerdrSkillContent -HerdrPath $HerdrPath
91	        return Write-HerdrSkillContent -Content $content -Destinations $Destinations
92	    } catch {
93	        Write-Warning "Could not read the official skill from the installed Herdr binary: $_"
94	        return $false
95	    }
96	}
97

1	# Windows dotfiles — chezmoi config template.
2	# Rendered once at `chezmoi init`; answers are stored in
3	# %USERPROFILE%\.config\chezmoi\chezmoi.toml and never re-asked.
4	#
5	# This repo targets **native Windows + PowerShell 7 (pwsh)** only. There is no
6	# OS branching: everything here assumes Windows. WSL/macOS/Linux are handled by
7	# the separate cross-platform dotfiles repo.
8	
9	[data]
10	    # role picks coarse defaults; every toggle can still be overridden.
11	    {{- $role := promptChoiceOnce . "role" "Role: workstation (full desktop) or minimal (shell only)" (list "workstation" "minimal") "workstation" }}
12	    {{- $full := eq $role "workstation" }}
13	    role  = {{ $role | quote }}
14	    name  = {{ promptStringOnce . "name" "Your full name (git)" "Da-Wei Lee" | quote }}
15	    email = {{ promptStringOnce . "email" "Your git email" "daviddwlee84@gmail.com" | quote }}
16	
17	    # --- feature toggles (role-defaulted) ---
18	    installCodingAgents  = {{ promptBoolOnce . "installCodingAgents" "Install coding agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Copilot CLI, SpecStory)" $full }}
19	    # How a coding agent announces it finished. Gates HOOK WIRING ONLY — the
20	    # peon CLI installs alongside the agents so you can experiment any time.
21	    #   none   = silent
22	    #   notify = notify.ps1 -> apprise -> Windows toast (current behavior)
23	    #   peon   = peon-ping game voice lines + its own overlay banner
24	    #   both   = toast + voice (two banners; `peon notifications off` to trim)
25	    # peon's own volume/pack/notification style stay unmanaged by chezmoi, so
26	    # tweaking them never shows up as drift. Parent repo: docs/tools/agent-sounds.md
27	    agentSounds          = {{ promptChoiceOnce . "agentSounds" "Agent completion feedback (none|notify|peon|both)" (list "none" "notify" "peon" "both") (ternary "notify" "none" $full) | quote }}
28	    installSpecstoryBuild = {{ promptBoolOnce . "installSpecstoryBuild" "Build the experimental SpecStory CLI for Windows from the unmerged PR #191 (needs git + go)" false }}

1	#Requires -Version 7
2	# Guards hard invariant #1 (AGENTS.md): every init prompt in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl
3	# must have a matching non-interactive flag in .github/workflows/windows.yml.
4	#
5	# Why this exists: adding a prompt without the flag does not fail loudly at
6	# authoring time — it fails much later, on the Windows runner, as an opaque
7	#   error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF
8	# because `chezmoi init --no-tty` has no answer for the new question and hits
9	# end-of-input. That broke CI for three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds`
10	# was added. This test turns that into a local `Invoke-Pester` failure with the
11	# exact missing flag line to paste in.
12	#
13	# Matching is on the prompt's TEXT (3rd arg to promptXOnce), because that is
14	# what chezmoi's `--promptBool 'text=value'` parser keys on — not the variable
15	# name.
16	
17	BeforeAll {
18	    $repo = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent
19	    $tomlTmpl = Join-Path $repo '.chezmoi.toml.tmpl'
20	    $workflow = Join-Path $repo '.github/workflows/windows.yml'
21	
22	    # promptBoolOnce . "varName" "Prompt text" <default>
23	    $script:Prompts = [regex]::Matches(
24	        (Get-Content -Raw $tomlTmpl),
25	        'prompt(?<kind>Bool|String|Choice)Once\s+\.\s+"(?<var>[^"]+)"\s+"(?<text>[^"]+)"'
26	    ) | ForEach-Object {
27	        [pscustomobject]@{
28	            Kind = $_.Groups['kind'].Value
29	            Var  = $_.Groups['var'].Value
30	            Text = $_.Groups['text'].Value
31	        }
32	    }
33	
34	    # '--promptBool','Prompt text=value'
35	    $script:Flags = [regex]::Matches(
36	        (Get-Content -Raw $workflow),
37	        "'--prompt(?<kind>Bool|String|Choice)'\s*,\s*'(?<text>[^=']+)="
38	    ) | ForEach-Object {
39	        [pscustomobject]@{
40	            Kind = $_.Groups['kind'].Value
41	            Text = $_.Groups['text'].Value
42	        }
43	    }
44	}
45	
46	# NB: no angle brackets in Describe/It names — Pester expands `<...>` in test
47	# names as a data placeholder, so a name like "prompts <-> flags" is rewritten
48	# to `$-` and the whole file dies with a bogus CommandNotFoundException.
49	Describe 'init prompts vs CI flags (invariant #1)' {
50	    It 'finds prompts in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl' {
51	        $script:Prompts.Count | Should -BeGreaterThan 10
52	    }
53	
54	    It 'finds prompt flags in windows.yml' {
55	        $script:Flags.Count | Should -BeGreaterThan 10
56	    }
57	
58	    It 'has a CI flag for every init prompt' {
59	        $flagText = @($script:Flags.Text)
60	        $missing = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object { $flagText -notcontains $_.Text })
61	        $hint = ($missing | ForEach-Object {
62	            "            '--prompt$($_.Kind)','$($_.Text)=<value>',   # $($_.Var)"
63	        }) -join "`n"
64	        $missing.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "windows.yml is missing these flags; add to the `$flags array:`n$hint"
65	    }
66	
67	    It 'has no stale CI flag without a matching prompt' {
68	        # Catches the other half of a rename: the prompt text changed but the
69	        # flag did not. chezmoi silently ignores an unmatched flag and then
70	        # blocks on the real prompt, so this would otherwise be invisible.
71	        $promptText = @($script:Prompts.Text)
72	        $stale = @($script:Flags | Where-Object { $promptText -notcontains $_.Text })
73	        $stale.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "these windows.yml flags match no prompt: $($stale.Text -join '; ')"
74	    }
75	
76	    It 'uses the right flag kind for each prompt' {
77	        $byText = @{}
78	        foreach ($f in $script:Flags) { $byText[$f.Text] = $f.Kind }
79	        $wrong = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object {
80	            $byText.ContainsKey($_.Text) -and $byText[$_.Text] -ne $_.Kind
81	        })
82	        $wrong.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "flag kind mismatch for: $($wrong.Var -join '; ')"
83	    }
84	
85	    It 'has no "=" in any prompt text' {
86	        # Invariant #1 corollary: chezmoi's `name=value` parser splits on the
87	        # FIRST "=", so a prompt whose text contains one can never be answered
88	        # non-interactively. This already broke the `role` prompt once.
89	        $bad = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object { $_.Text -match '=' })
90	        $bad.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "prompt text may not contain '=': $($bad.Var -join '; ')"
91	    }

```text
1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) and other coding
4	agents when working with code in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to this file.
5	
6	## What this is
7	
8	Standalone, **Windows-only** dotfiles managed by [chezmoi](https://chezmoi.io),
9	targeting **PowerShell 7 (pwsh)**. It is a companion to the cross-platform
10	macOS/Linux repo `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` — the PowerShell layer is written
11	natively, **not** ported from that repo's POSIX shell config. No ansible;
12	packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI). Published at
13	`github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows`.
14	
15	**Dev box vs target:** the deploy target is Windows, but this checkout is usually
16	edited on macOS/Linux. You therefore **cannot execute the `.ps1` run-scripts
17	here** (they call winget / `%APPDATA%`). Validate with the isolated-apply +
18	render/parse pattern below; the `windows-latest` CI is the real gate.
19	
20	## Commands
21	
22	Real machine:
23	
24	- `chezmoi apply` / `chezmoi diff` (or `just apply` / `just diff`)
25	- `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`
26	
27	Validate locally (needs a local pwsh, e.g. installed to `~/.local/bin/pwsh`):
28	
29	- Lint: `pwsh -NoProfile -c "Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path . -Recurse -Settings ./PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1"` (fails only on Error; the excludes are deliberate — see the settings file header)
30	- Tests: `pwsh -NoProfile -c "Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests"` (single file: `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/Copilot.Tests.ps1`)
31	- Docs: `just docs-build` (= `uv run --with mkdocs-material --with mkdocs-static-i18n mkdocs build --strict`)
32	
33	Isolated apply + template render (the core idiom for testing without a Windows
34	box — all chezmoi state is redirected to a temp dir, so it never touches your
35	real setup):
36	
37	```bash
38	TMPD=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$TMPD/home"
39	chezmoi init --source="$PWD" --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --persistent-state="$TMPD/s.db" \
40	  --destination="$TMPD/home" --no-tty \
41	  --promptChoice='Role: workstation (full desktop) or minimal (shell only)=minimal' \
42	  --promptString='Your full name (git)=T' --promptString='Your git email=t@e.com' ...  # EVERY prompt, exact text
43	chezmoi apply --source="$PWD" --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --persistent-state="$TMPD/s.db" \
44	  --destination="$TMPD/home" --exclude=scripts   # scripts can't run off-Windows
45	chezmoi execute-template --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --source="$PWD" < some.ps1.tmpl > r.ps1  # then parse r.ps1 with pwsh
46	```
47	
48	## Architecture (big picture)
49	
50	- **Init** — `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` `[data]` prompts once (`role` → coarse defaults, then `installX` toggles) and sets `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` so chezmoi runs `.ps1` scripts under pwsh. Prompts are hand-authored here (the parent repo generates them; this repo does not).
51	- **Shell** — `Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1` is a thin `$PROFILE` loader that dot-sources `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in numeric order (env → tool activation → aliases → apps/audio/clipboard → copilot import → yazi → tv cache → psreadline). Add a shell feature = a new numbered fragment. User overrides go in the untracked `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1`.
52	- **Packages** — `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the single source of truth for installs: scoop (CLI), winget (GUI), npm (AI agents), PSGallery (PSFzf / AudioDeviceCmdlets), all gated by init toggles. `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` is the single source for registry environment variables used both by that installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines use company PyPI/npm pull-through feeds; otherwise the China-mirror toggle selects GFW mirrors. Fault-tolerant (see invariants).
53	- **copilot-proxy** — `dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/` is a native PowerShell port of the parent's `43_copilot_proxy.sh` / `44_copilot_embed.sh` (runs the copilot-api fork so GitHub Copilot can back Claude Code and Codex). Reuses the Bun `copilot-throttle-shim.js` verbatim.
54	- **Config surfaces** — Alacritty (`AppData/Roaming/alacritty/`), Windows Terminal (a run_onchange that merges `profiles.defaults` non-destructively), WezTerm (`dot_config/wezterm/wezterm.lua` — sets pwsh as `default_prog`), editors (a run_onchange that deep-merges `editors/*.json` into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`), Claude Code (one `installCodingAgents`-gated, fail-closed run_onchange deep-merges settings and claude-hud Full config while preserving live/user-owned keys; see `docs/rationale.md`), Codex (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` fail-closed-merges only the native `tui.status_line` into `~/.codex/config.toml`, preserving providers/projects/plugins and gated on `installCodingAgents`), apprise desktop notifications (`dot_config/apprise/apprise.yaml` → `~/.config/apprise/`; the `windows://` toast backend behind the Claude notify hook `dot_claude/hooks/notify.ps1`, `installCodingAgents`-gated — the notify hook and peon-ping's voice-line hooks are both gated on the `agentSounds` tier (none|notify|peon|both) and built in the run_onchange, NOT in `claude/settings-overlay.json`; see docs/agent-sounds.md), television channels (`AppData/Roaming/television/`), starship + yazi (`~/.config`, yazi via `YAZI_CONFIG_HOME`), Rime/Weasel (see below), herdr (see below).
55	- **Rime input method** — `installInputMethod`-gated, and the one config surface **shared with the parent repo**. The engine-level YAML lives in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` (`default.custom.yaml`, `luna_pinyin.custom.yaml`) and is kept **byte-identical** to `daviddwlee84/dotfiles`'s copy of the same path — `diff -r` between the two dirs is the drift check, so edit one and copy to the other in the same session. Each platform is a one-line `{{ template "rime/…" . }}` renderer: `AppData/Roaming/Rime/` here, `private_Library/Rime/` (Squirrel) and `dot_config/ibus/rime/` (ibus-rime) there. Only `weasel.custom.yaml` is Windows-specific (`style/` is Weasel's own, `app_options` keys on the EXE name vs. Squirrel's bundle ids, and `global_ascii` doesn't exist on Squirrel). Plain managed files, **not** a `modify_` overlay: Rime persists runtime state to `user.yaml`, never back into `*.custom.yaml`. Two gotchas: a bare silent winget install registers **简体** (hence `--custom '/T'` in `Install-Weasel` — see `pitfalls/weasel-silent-install-registers-simplified-chinese.md`), and config edits need a redeploy, which `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
56	- **herdr** — `dot_config/herdr/` is deployed via `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` and gated on `installHerdr`. `config.toml` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` + `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`), never a plain managed file: herdr rewrites that file at runtime (onboarding flag, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]` bookkeeping) and a plain file clobbers it. The overlay enforces `[theme]`/`[ui]`/`[terminal]`/`[keys]` wholesale, pulls every other top-level key through, and re-asserts the single key `update.channel = "preview"` (the Windows installer rejects `stable`). `run_after_15_sync_herdr_skill.ps1.tmpl` exports the exact installed binary's `herdr --skill` output to real copies under both `~/.agents/skills/herdr/` and `~/.claude/skills/herdr/`; no symlink/junction is used. Helper-script paths in the keymap are baked **absolute at render time** — `pwsh -File` does not expand `~`. Six pwsh helpers (`_common.ps1` + run-command / new-tab-at-space-root / url-pick / path-pick / pane-copy / review-mark) back the `[[keys.command]]` bindings; three `herdr-*` tv channels and the herdr-plus quick-actions are gated by the same toggle. Ported from the parent repo 2026-07-27; the behaviours that still need a real Windows box are listed in [`backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md`](backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md).
57	- **git config** — `~/.gitconfig` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_dot_gitconfig.ps1.tmpl`), never a plain managed file: Git Credential Manager writes `[credential "azrepos:*"]` blocks into it out of band and a plain file would clobber them every apply. The baseline body is `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (identity from the existing `.name`/`.email` init prompts); the merge engine is `scripts/gitconfig-merge.ps1`, inlined via `{{ include }}` (the `editors/` idiom) and dot-sourced by `tests/GitConfig.Tests.ps1`. The model is **key-level pull-through**: the baseline owns a fixed set of `section.key` pairs and every other live key is carried over untouched — the inverse of the parent repo's allowlist, which would silently drop `[otel]` and future corp sections. Two hard rules: `core.hooksPath` is **never** emitted (git honours it *instead of* `.git/hooks/`, silently disarming `pre-commit`), and the carry dictionary is **case-sensitive** (`[ordered]@{}` collapses `azrepos:org/O365Exchange` into `azrepos:org/o365exchange`, merging two credential contexts).
58	- **Docs** — bilingual mkdocs-material (`docs/X.md` + `docs/X.zh-TW.md`), deployed to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/docs.yml`. `docs/rationale.md` records the design choices (scoop > Chocolatey, starship > oh-my-posh, pwsh > cmd, native pwsh tree > ported shell layer).
59	- **CI** — `.github/workflows/windows.yml` on `windows-latest` is the real gate: PSScriptAnalyzer, non-interactive `chezmoi init --apply`, render+parse of every `.ps1.tmpl`, and Pester.
60	
61	## Conventions & hard invariants
62	
63	1. **A new/renamed init prompt must update the CI flags in the same commit.** `chezmoi init --promptBool/--promptChoice "<text>=value"` matches the prompt's exact TEXT (3rd arg to `promptXOnce` in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`), used non-interactively by `.github/workflows/windows.yml`. Forget it → CI's init hangs/EOFs (`error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF`; this broke three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds` was added). Corollary: **never put `=` in a prompt's text** — the `name=value` parser splits on the first `=` (this broke the `role` prompt once). Enforced by `tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` (missing flag, stale flag, wrong flag kind, `=` in text), which CI runs *before* `chezmoi init` so the failure names the missing flag instead of EOF-ing — run `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` locally after touching either file.
64	2. **Run-scripts must never abort the apply.** The installer + editor/terminal/backup/skill scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'` (+ `PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$false`), collect failures via `Register-Failure`, print a summary, and exit 0. One bad scoop/winget manifest (e.g. btop's stale `.conf`) must not stop the rest.
65	3. **Preserve raw escapes when authoring config with control chars.** Alacritty CSI-u (`[…u`), VSCode `sendSequence`, tv `\t` — hand-typing tends to drop them. Generate via a throwaway Python script and re-parse (`tomllib` / `json`) to confirm the escape landed.
66	4. **tv channel commands are `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "…"` inside TOML literal (`'''…'''`) strings** — runs regardless of tv's shell, sidesteps nested-quote escaping; placeholders `{split: :0}` (space) / `{split:\t:0}` (tab). tv reads config from `%APPDATA%\television\` on Windows.
67	5. **Editors use a run_onchange pwsh merger, not `modify_`** (`modify_` interpreter selection is unreliable on Windows). Overlay sources live in `editors/` (chezmoi-ignored, embedded via `{{ include }}`).
68	6. **The agent skill body lives once** in `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`; both `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` and `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` render it via `{{ "{{" }} template … {{ "}}" }}` → real files at `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/`. Edit the shared template, not the two one-line renderers (no symlink/junction — those need elevation/Developer Mode on Windows).
69	7. **PSScriptAnalyzer exclusions are intentional** (`PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`): hyphenated command names, `Write-Host`, `Invoke-Expression` for tool init, no-BOM UTF-8. Don't "fix" these; do fix real Errors.
70	
71	### Cross-file mirrors (same commit)
72	
73	- New installer tool → `docs/tools.md` **and** `docs/tools.zh-TW.md`.
74	- New init prompt → `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `windows.yml` flags + `docs/setup.md`/`setup.zh-TW.md` tables + the "What's enabled" block in `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.
75	- New `docs/**/*.md` → its `.zh-TW.md` twin + `nav` + `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`; `just docs-build` must stay green.
76	- Any edit under `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` → copy the file verbatim into the parent repo's `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` (`chezmoi source-path` there, usually `~/.local/share/chezmoi`). 77	- `dot_config/powershell/copilot-throttle-shim.js` is copied verbatim from the parent repo's `dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js`. Update both in the same maintenance session, then update the reviewed Unix source commit + SHA-256 contract in `tests/Copilot.Tests.ps1`; the Windows test must remain runnable without a sibling checkout.
78	- `core.autocrlf = input` has **two writers** — `bootstrap.ps1` (runs before chezmoi exists, so scoop's first bucket clone is protected) and `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (the managed baseline). Change one → change the other.
79	
80	### `scripts/*.sh` are wrappers, not implementations
81	
82	`scripts/{add-todo,todo-kanban,promote-todo,sweep-inbox}.sh` are byte-identical
83	three-line shims. The real code is vendored at
84	`.agents/skills/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/<same-name>.sh`, and each
85	wrapper derives its target from `$0`, so adding a new helper only needs a copy
86	of an existing wrapper under the new name.
87	
88	They exist because the skill documents its helpers with cwd-relative paths
89	(`scripts/add-todo.sh`) and that prose was copied verbatim into the guidance
90	block below — where `scripts/` means *this* directory. Fixing the prose instead
91	would not survive, because `project-knowledge-harness` regenerates everything
92	between its sentinel markers. **This note is deliberately above the opening
93	sentinel so regeneration cannot erase it.**
94	
95	Not symlinks — invariant 6 (symlinks/junctions need elevation or Developer
96	Mode on Windows).
97	
98	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:agent-guidance -->
99	<!-- Snippet for the project's agent contract file (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md /
100	     similar). The bundled scripts/init.sh appends this between sentinel
101	     markers; safe to re-run. -->
102	
103	### Long-term backlog → `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
104	
105	When the user surfaces an idea explicitly **not** being implemented this
106	session (signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
107	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來"), add an entry to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using
108	the priority + effort tag schema. Do **not** create new `ROADMAP.md` /
109	`IDEAS.md` / `BACKLOG.md` files — `TODO.md` is the single index.
110	
111	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates the format. Run it
112	(`scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md`) after editing so syntax
113	drift is caught immediately.
114	
115	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
116	
117	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
118	
119	   ```
120	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
121	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
122	   ```
123	
124	   Inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane and
125	   re-runs the validator. Add `--backlog` to also scaffold
126	   `backlog/<slug>.md` from the bundled template.
127	
128	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
129	
130	   ```
131	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
132	   ```
133	
134	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox", run
135	   `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`. It prompts for the missing fields per loose
136	   line and calls `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs
137	   that only formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
138	
139	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh; run
140	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
141	
142	Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` companion doc when the item meets any of:
143	
144	- carries a `P?` tag (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
145	- captures a paused troubleshooting session that you intend to fix later
146	  (preserve the error trace + root cause analysis before context evaporates)
147	- weighs multiple options (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
148	- is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)
149	
150	`[S]` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the `TODO.md` line is
151	usually enough. See [`backlog/README.md`](backlog/README.md) for the full
152	template and "when to add a doc" rules.
153	
154	When implementing a `TODO.md` item, in the same commit:
155	
156	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`
157	   to move the entry into `## Done` with the dated syntax and re-validate.
158	2. Mark the corresponding `backlog/<slug>.md` (if any) `Status: shipped`
159	   and keep it as a historical record (don't delete — future-you may
160	   revisit adjacent decisions).
161	
162	`backlog/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore); it
163	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
164	
165	### Past pitfalls → `pitfalls/`
166	
167	When you spend more than ~15 minutes debugging something that wasn't
168	googleable and the fix is non-obvious, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
169	capturing:
170	
171	1. **Verbatim symptom** — copy-paste error messages exactly, do not
172	   paraphrase (preserves grep-ability for future-you / future agent)
173	2. **Root cause** — why this happens (with source / docs / upstream issue link)
174	3. **Workaround** — copy-pasteable commands or config diff
175	4. **Prevention** — how to avoid stepping on this again
176	
177	Title the doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause (you'll search by what
178	you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned). See
179	[`pitfalls/README.md`](pitfalls/README.md) for the full template and
180	when-to-add rules.
181	
182	**Pitfall vs Hard invariant**: a pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant in
183	this file when it (a) recurs across machines/agents/sessions despite being
184	documented, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround is non-obvious
185	enough that "remember to do X" isn't safe. When graduating, leave the
186	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the new
187	invariant.
188	
189	`pitfalls/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore) and
190	**not** auto-redacted; review for secrets before committing.

Two caller constraints materially shape the implementation: Herdr’s modifier cannot use ordinary pipeline streaming because stdout is the managed TOML payload, while installer/just commands need live, explicit attempt diagnostics. The runner should therefore capture child stdout/stderr with `ProcessStartInfo`, replay it to host/stderr as appropriate, and classify only the captured failure text plus timeout state—never infer fallback merely from a nonzero exit code.

208	## Package registries
209	
210	One shared policy is applied both at install time and in interactive shells
211	(`profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`):
212	
213	- **Managed machines** route pip/uv through the company PyPI pull-through
214	  registry and npm through the company npm pull-through registry. The PyPI path
215	  was verified with `tomlkit==0.13.3`; its artifacts are served by the corporate
216	  Azure Artifacts backend. IT already provisions the enabled company NuGet source
217	  and disables nuget.org, so the dotfiles do not rewrite NuGet configuration.
218	- **China mirrors** apply only on non-managed machines and route pip / npm / cargo /
219	  go / node through Tsinghua / npmmirror / goproxy.cn / rsproxy.
220	- No company Go or Cargo registry was discovered, so managed machines leave those
221	  ecosystems at their existing defaults.
222

```text
1	---
2	name: dotfiles-windows
3	description: Operate and navigate THIS Windows machine's chezmoi-managed dotfiles (native PowerShell 7). Use when the user asks how to apply/edit/diff dotfiles, where a config or tool lives, how the pwsh $PROFILE / copilot-proxy / scoop+winget install works, how a keybinding or helper (applaunch/sysvol/x/cas) works, or how to use chezmoi / just in this repo.
4	---
5	
6	# dotfiles-windows
7	
8	This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
9	Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
10	there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
11	(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)
12	
13	## Orientation
14	- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
15	- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
16	- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
17	- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
18	- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).
19	
20	## Shell layout (pwsh)
21	- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
22	  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
23	  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
24	- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
25	  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
26	  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
27	  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
28	  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).
29	
30	## Packages
31	- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
32	  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
33	  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
34	  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
35	- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
36	  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
37	  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
38	  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
39	- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
40	  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.
41	
42	## copilot-proxy
43	- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
44	  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
45	  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `codex-copilot`,
46	  `codex-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`, `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`),
47	  `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
48	- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
49	  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
50	  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
51	  Automatic selection excludes policy-disabled, picker-hidden and embedding-only
52	  entries. Claude `--auto` is Claude-first; Codex is OpenAI-first; both share the
53	  named OpenAI order Sol > Terra > 5.5 > 5.4 > 5.3 Codex > Luna > mini.
54	- The shim retries only the same buffered request/model, emits SSE keepalives for
55	  silent streams, and has a stall watchdog; it never performs request-time
56	  cross-model failover. Timing knobs: `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS`,
57	  `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS`, `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS`.
58	- `copilot-here` writes only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The
59	  pinned copilot-api is installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`
60	  (never `bunx` at launch); `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls
61	  whether Node fetches the GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide:
62	  `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.
63	
64	## Editors / terminal / tv
65	- VSCode & Cursor settings + keybindings are deep-merged into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`
66	  by `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20_editor_overlays.ps1.tmpl` (sources under `editors/`).
67	- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),
68	  and WezTerm (`~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`, pwsh as default shell) are managed too.
69	  Television channels live under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (`tv <name>`).
70	
71	## What's enabled on THIS machine
72	- role: **{{ .role }}**
73	- Coding agents: {{ .installCodingAgents }} · Agent sounds: {{ .agentSounds }} · SpecStory build (PR #191): {{ .installSpecstoryBuild }} · GUI apps: {{ .installWindowsApps }} · WSL2 (Docker backend): {{ .installWsl }} · WSL Ubuntu: {{ .installWslUbuntu }} · Utility apps: {{ .installUtilityApps }} · Gaming: {{ .installGamingApps }}
74	- Extra runtimes: {{ .installExtraRuntimes }} · Media: {{ .installMediaTools }} · LLM: {{ .installLlmTools }} · Tunnel: {{ .installTunnelTools }} · IaC: {{ .installIacTools }} · OpenSSH: {{ .installSshServer }} · herdr: {{ .installHerdr }} · Clink(cmd): {{ .installClink }} · try: {{ .installTry }} · translate: {{ .installTranslate }} · Rime/Weasel: {{ .installInputMethod }}
75	- China mirrors: {{ .useChineseMirror }} · Backup mode: {{ .backupMode }} · Vim mode: {{ .enableVimMode }} · Managed machine: {{ .managedMachine }}
76	
77	## just recipes
78	`just --list`: `apply`/`diff`/`update`, `upgrade-scoop`/`upgrade-winget`/`upgrade-translate`, `lint`/`test`,
79	`docs-serve`/`docs-build`, `enable-sshd` (opt-in OpenSSH server, elevated),
80	`enable-wsl` (WSL2 for Docker Desktop; self-elevating UAC prompt, reboot after),
81	`enable-wsl-ubuntu` (WSL2 Ubuntu distro + cross-platform dotfiles; needs enable-wsl first),
82	`wsl-dotfiles` (bootstrap the cross-platform dotfiles into an existing WSL distro; VPN if behind GFW),
83	`install-fonts-machine-wide` (Alacritty Nerd Font fix, elevated), and
84	`docker-up`/`docker-down`/`docker-clean`/`docker-logs`
85	(the x86-Linux+KVM Windows-in-Docker test harness — see `docker/windows/`).
86	
87	## Gotchas
88	- Windows-only repo — no `{{ "{{" }} if eq .chezmoi.os {{ "}}" }}` branching needed.
89	- Editor settings use a `run_onchange` pwsh merger (not `modify_`) on Windows.
90	- tmux / zellij are Unix-only and intentionally absent; **WezTerm** (installed) is
91	  the stable native tmux-like multiplexer, or use Windows Terminal panes. **herdr**
92	  is an opt-in (`installHerdr`) native-Windows multiplexer in preview beta —
93	  installed via herdr.dev's `irm|iex` script, config at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`,
94	  with its official global skill exported from the installed binary on each apply.
95	  Runtimes are native via scoop (node/bun/go/rust/ruby) + uv for Python — no mise on Windows.
96	- **Rime input method** (opt-in `installInputMethod`): Weasel/小狼毫 via winget
97	  `Rime.Weasel`. Machine-scope NSIS, so applying raises UAC; and a bare silent
98	  install registers **简体** — `Install-Weasel` passes `--custom '/T'` for 繁體.
99	  The engine-level YAML in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` is **byte-identical to the
100	  parent repo's** copy (Squirrel/ibus-rime); only `weasel.custom.yaml` is
101	  Windows-specific. Edits need a redeploy, which
102	  `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
103	  See `docs/input-method.md`.
104	- **cmd.exe** is opt-in via `installClink`: Clink + starship/zoxide/fzf give the DOS
105	  prompt parity for **prompt + navigation only** (no pwsh funcs/aliases/modules).
106	  `starship.lua` is chezmoi-managed at `%LocalAppData%\clink`; the zoxide/fzf Clink
107	  bridges are fetched from upstream at apply. pwsh stays the default shell.
108	- **`translate`** (`installTranslate`, on for workstation) is the one tool built from
109	  source: no scoop/winget manifest, so the packages script runs a version-pinned
110	  `go install` into `~\.local\bin` (it installs `go` itself). First build takes
111	  minutes; re-applies no-op via a `--version` check. Upgrade with
112	  `just upgrade-translate`, not `upgrade-scoop`.
113	- This skill body is shared: `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/` and
114	  `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/` both render `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `C:/Users/hanruzhou/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md`

```text
1	# npm returns 404 against `packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io` — and the registry is actually fine
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): probing the internal Microsoft npm mirror
4	looks like a dead service —
5	
6	```
7	npm error 404
8	npm error 404 Note that you can also install from a
9	npm error 404 tarball, folder, http url, or git url.
10	```
11	
12	`npm ping --registry https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/` → **404**.
13	`https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/` and `/undici` → **404** in a browser or
14	`Invoke-WebRequest`. `npm view <pkg> --registry https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/registry/`
15	→ **404**. Yet DNS resolves and TCP 443 connects fine, and *some* tarball URLs
16	return 200. The natural conclusion — "this is only a tarball proxy for specific
17	packages, not a real npm registry" — is **wrong**.
18	**First seen**: 2026-07-29 (reached independently on two company laptops)
19	**Affects**: Microsoft corp machines where `registry=https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/`
20	is set at the machine level (`Q:\.tools\.npm-global\etc\npmrc`) and
21	`registry.npmjs.org` is blocked.
22	**Status**: not a bug — three probing mistakes.
23	
24	## Root cause
25	
26	`packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/` **is** a full pull-through npm registry.
27	Three separate things make it look broken:
28	
29	### 1. `npm ping` is not implemented — 404 does not mean unhealthy
30	
31	`npm ping` hits `/-/ping`, which this mirror does not serve. It returns 404 on a
32	perfectly working registry. **Never use `npm ping` as the health probe here.**
33	Use a metadata read instead:
34	
35	```bash
36	npm view undici version --registry https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/
37	# 8.8.0
38	```
39	
40	### 2. `/npm/registry/` is one segment too deep
41	
42	The registry root is `/npm/`, **not** `/npm/registry/`:
43	
44	| URL | Result |
45	|---|---|
46	| `https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/` | works |
47	| `https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/registry/` | 404 |
48	| `https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/` | 404 |
49	
50	The `/npm/registry/...` shape is what **Azure Artifacts** feeds use
51	(`pkgs.dev.azure.com/<org>/_packaging/<feed>/npm/registry/`), so it is an easy
52	habit to carry over. The give-away that `/npm/` is correct: the tarball path
53	that *does* work, `/npm/@scope/name/-/name-1.2.3.tgz`, is the standard npm
54	layout relative to base `/npm/`.
55	
56	### 3. The internal feed can be *ahead* of the public mirror
57	
58	Asking the internal Azure Artifacts feed for `undici@latest` yields a version
59	the public mirror does not have yet. Requesting that newer tarball from
60	`packagefeedproxy` then 404s, which reads as "tarball not provided" when it
61	actually means "that version isn't mirrored". At time of writing the internal
62	feed had `undici` 8.9.0 while the mirror's latest was **8.8.0**.
63	
64	## How to verify it is healthy
65	
66	```bash
67	R='https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/'
68	npm view undici version   --registry "$R"   # 8.8.0   -> metadata works
69	npm view left-pad version --registry "$R"   # 1.3.0   -> arbitrary public pkg, so no allowlist
70	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14' version --registry "$R"
71	```
72	
73	`left-pad` is the important one: an obscure package nobody on the machine has
74	ever installed proves this is a general pull-through proxy, not a curated
75	allowlist.
76	
77	Metadata rewrites `dist.tarball` to Microsoft's 1ES **public** mirror:
78	
79	```
80	https://ms-feed-25.pkgs.visualstudio.com/1es-public/_packaging/npm-public/npm/registry/undici/-/undici-8.8.0.tgz
81	```
82	
83	Note `npm-public` — packages served here are public npm packages, so a scoped
84	name resolving through it is **not** evidence that a package is internal or
85	that an internal-feed credential is required.
86	
87	## Prevention
88	
89	- Health-probe with `npm view <pkg> version --registry <url>`, never `npm ping`.
90	- Do not copy the `/npm/registry/` suffix from Azure Artifacts URLs.
91	- Before concluding a version is missing, check the mirror's own `latest`
92	  rather than the internal feed's.
93	- `npm config list` shows which file supplies `registry` (`builtin` / `global` /
94	  `user` / `env`) and masks credentials — prefer it to reading `~/.npmrc`, which
95	  contains a live token.
96	
97	## Related
98	
99	- [`copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module`](copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module.md)
100	  — the failure this investigation was chasing. It was not a registry problem
101	  at all; a stale deployed module was falling back to Bun, which ignores the
102	  configured registry.
103
```
</details></tool-use>
