````md
# uv fails with HTTP 503 while downloading from the company PyPI feed

**Symptoms**: `Request failed after 3 retries`, `HTTP status server error (503 Service Unavailable)`, final URL under `ms-feed-*.pkgs.visualstudio.com`, `just docs-build` fails although the configured index is `packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/pypi/simple`

**First seen**: 2026-08  
**Affects**: managed Windows machines using uv through the company PyPI pull-through feed  
**Status**: source-isolated opt-in fallback implemented

## Symptom

A managed shell configures:

```text
UV_DEFAULT_INDEX=https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/pypi/simple/
```

but uv reports the failure against a different-looking host:

```text
error: Request failed after 3 retries
Caused by: Failed to fetch: https://ms-feed-*.pkgs.visualstudio.com/.../pypi/download/...
Caused by: HTTP status server error (503 Service Unavailable)
```

A successful feed-root or package-metadata probe does not disprove the problem;
the redirected artifact download can fail independently.

## Root cause

`packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io` is the configured company pull-through endpoint.
It resolves package artifacts through an Azure Artifacts backend, so uv displays
the final `*.pkgs.visualstudio.com` download URL when that backend returns 503.
This is not a malformed PyPI URL and does not show that `pypi.org` itself failed.

## Workaround

The default remains corporate-only. On a machine where public fallback is
explicitly permitted, enable the `Allow one public PyPI/npm retry after eligible
corporate feed failures` init prompt and re-apply/reload the profile.

Repo-owned npm/uv commands then:

1. try only the corporate source;
2. classify the captured failure;
3. retry exactly once against only the public source for timeout, temporary
   network errors, or explicit HTTP 5xx.

For a one-off manual docs build without changing the prompt:

```powershell
uv run --no-project --no-config `
  --default-index https://pypi.org/simple --index-strategy first-index `
  --with mkdocs-material --with mkdocs-static-i18n mkdocs build --strict
```

## Prevention

- Never configure public PyPI as an `extra-index` beside the company feed.
- Never fall back on 401/403, TLS/certificate, policy, 404/package-absence,
  rate-limit, solver/build, or local permission failures.
- Keep fallback command-scoped; do not rewrite the parent shell or npmrc.
- Test artifact resolution, not only the index root.
- Keep `scripts/package-source-runner.ps1` covered by deterministic fake-command
  tests so classification does not broaden accidentally.

## Related

- [`packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path`](packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md)
- [`docs/tools.md`](../docs/tools.md#package-registries)
- `AGENTS.md` hard invariant 8
````

`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

# dotfiles-windows

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)

## Orientation
- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).

## Shell layout (pwsh)
- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).

## Packages
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.

## copilot-proxy
- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `codex-copilot`,
  `codex-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`, `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`),
  `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
  Automatic selection excludes policy-disabled, picker-hidden and embedding-only
  entries. Claude `--auto` is Claude-first; Codex is OpenAI-first; both share the
  named OpenAI order Sol > Terra > 5.5 > 5.4 > 5.3 Codex > Luna > mini.
- The shim retries only the same buffered request/model, emits SSE keepalives for
  silent streams, and has a stall watchdog; it never performs request-time
  cross-model failover. Timing knobs: `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS`,
  `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS`, `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS`.
- `copilot-here` writes only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The
  pinned copilot-api is installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`
  (never `bunx` at launch); `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls
  whether Node fetches the GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide:
  `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.

## Editors / terminal / tv
- VSCode & Cursor settings + keybindings are deep-merged into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`
  by `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20_editor_overlays.ps1.tmpl` (sources under `editors/`).
- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),
  and WezTerm (`~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`, pwsh as default shell) are managed too.
  Television channels live under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (`tv <name>`).

## What's enabled on THIS machine
- role: **workstation**
- Coding agents: true · Agent sounds: peon · SpecStory build (PR #191): true · GUI apps: true · WSL2 (Docker backend): true · WSL Ubuntu: true · Utility apps: true · Gaming: true
- Extra runtimes: true · Media: true · LLM: true · Tunnel: true · IaC: true · OpenSSH: true · herdr: true · Clink(cmd): true · try: true · translate: true · Rime/Weasel: true
- China mirrors: true · Backup mode: smart · Vim mode: true · Managed machine: true

## just recipes
`just --list`: `apply`/`diff`/`update`, `upgrade-scoop`/`upgrade-winget`/`upgrade-translate`, `lint`/`test`,
`docs-serve`/`docs-build`, `enable-sshd` (opt-in OpenSSH server, elevated),
`enable-wsl` (WSL2 for Docker Desktop; self-elevating UAC prompt, reboot after),
`enable-wsl-ubuntu` (WSL2 Ubuntu distro + cross-platform dotfiles; needs enable-wsl first),
`wsl-dotfiles` (bootstrap the cross-platform dotfiles into an existing WSL distro; VPN if behind GFW),
`install-fonts-machine-wide` (Alacritty Nerd Font fix, elevated), and
`docker-up`/`docker-down`/`docker-clean`/`docker-logs`
(the x86-Linux+KVM Windows-in-Docker test harness — see `docker/windows/`).

## Gotchas
- Windows-only repo — no `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os }}` branching needed.
- Editor settings use a `run_onchange` pwsh merger (not `modify_`) on Windows.
- tmux / zellij are Unix-only and intentionally absent; **WezTerm** (installed) is
  the stable native tmux-like multiplexer, or use Windows Terminal panes. **herdr**
  is an opt-in (`installHerdr`) native-Windows multiplexer in preview beta —
  installed via herdr.dev's `irm|iex` script, config at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`,
  with its official global skill exported from the installed binary on each apply.
  Runtimes are native via scoop (node/bun/go/rust/ruby) + uv for Python — no mise on Windows.
- **Rime input method** (opt-in `installInputMethod`): Weasel/小狼毫 via winget
  `Rime.Weasel`. Machine-scope NSIS, so applying raises UAC; and a bare silent
  install registers **简体** — `Install-Weasel` passes `--custom '/T'` for 繁體.
  The engine-level YAML in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` is **byte-identical to the
  parent repo's** copy (Squirrel/ibus-rime); only `weasel.custom.yaml` is
  Windows-specific. Edits need a redeploy, which
  `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
  See `docs/input-method.md`.
- **cmd.exe** is opt-in via `installClink`: Clink + starship/zoxide/fzf give the DOS
  prompt parity for **prompt + navigation only** (no pwsh funcs/aliases/modules).
  `starship.lua` is chezmoi-managed at `%LocalAppData%\clink`; the zoxide/fzf Clink
  bridges are fetched from upstream at apply. pwsh stays the default shell.
- **`translate`** (`installTranslate`, on for workstation) is the one tool built from
  source: no scoop/winget manifest, so the packages script runs a version-pinned
  `go install` into `~\.local\bin` (it installs `go` itself). First build takes
  minutes; re-applies no-op via a `--version` check. Upgrade with
  `just upgrade-translate`, not `upgrade-scoop`.
- This skill body is shared: `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/` and
  `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/` both render `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.

Review target: `Altitude-angle read-only review. Scope only requested task files and relevant changed docs in C:/Users/hanruzhou/.local/share/chezmoi. Check source selection/fallback, process invocation, npm cmd wrapping/source isolation, package script/template handling, Herdr output, and just actions. Report concrete observable defects or maintenance costs only; ignore unrelated dirty files; do not edit or delegate; return up to 6 candidates with file, line, summary, failure scenario.`

`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule

altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

Dedup candidates that point at the same line/mechanism, keeping the one with

file(s), and the candidate, and have it return exactly one of:

  output or crash. Quote the line.
- **PLAUSIBLE** — mechanism is real, trigger is uncertain (timing, env,
  config). State what would confirm it.
- **REFUTED** — factually wrong (code doesn't say that) or guarded elsewhere.
  Quote the line that proves it.

Keep candidates where the vote is CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 8 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 8 survive, keep the 8 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

48	## Architecture (big picture)
49	
50	- **Init** — `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` `[data]` prompts once (`role` → coarse defaults, then `installX` toggles) and sets `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` so chezmoi runs `.ps1` scripts under pwsh. Prompts are hand-authored here (the parent repo generates them; this repo does not).
51	- **Shell** — `Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1` is a thin `$PROFILE` loader that dot-sources `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in numeric order (env → tool activation → aliases → apps/audio/clipboard → copilot import → yazi → tv cache → psreadline). Add a shell feature = a new numbered fragment. User overrides go in the untracked `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1`.
52	- **Packages** — `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the single source of truth for installs: scoop (CLI), winget (GUI), npm (AI agents), PSGallery (PSFzf / AudioDeviceCmdlets), all gated by init toggles. `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` owns persistent registry environment variables; `scripts/package-source-runner.ps1` owns command-scoped corporate-first fallback for the enumerated npm/uv operations. Managed machines use company PyPI/npm feeds; otherwise the China toggle selects GFW mirrors. Fault-tolerant (see invariants).
53	- **copilot-proxy** — `dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/` is a native PowerShell port of the parent's `43_copilot_proxy.sh` / `44_copilot_embed.sh` (runs the copilot-api fork so GitHub Copilot can back Claude Code and Codex). Reuses the Bun `copilot-throttle-shim.js` verbatim.
54	- **Config surfaces** — Alacritty (`AppData/Roaming/alacritty/`), Windows Terminal (a run_onchange that merges `profiles.defaults` non-destructively), WezTerm (`dot_config/wezterm/wezterm.lua` — sets pwsh as `default_prog`), editors (a run_onchange that deep-merges `editors/*.json` into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`), Claude Code (one `installCodingAgents`-gated, fail-closed run_onchange deep-merges settings and claude-hud Full config while preserving live/user-owned keys; see `docs/rationale.md`), Codex (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` fail-closed-merges only the native `tui.status_line` into `~/.codex/config.toml`, preserving providers/projects/plugins and gated on `installCodingAgents`), apprise desktop notifications (`dot_config/apprise/apprise.yaml` → `~/.config/apprise/`; the `windows://` toast backend behind the Claude notify hook `dot_claude/hooks/notify.ps1`, `installCodingAgents`-gated — the notify hook and peon-ping's voice-line hooks are both gated on the `agentSounds` tier (none|notify|peon|both) and built in the run_onchange, NOT in `claude/settings-overlay.json`; see docs/agent-sounds.md), television channels (`AppData/Roaming/television/`), starship + yazi (`~/.config`, yazi via `YAZI_CONFIG_HOME`), Rime/Weasel (see below), herdr (see below).
55	- **Rime input method** — `installInputMethod`-gated, and the one config surface **shared with the parent repo**. The engine-level YAML lives in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` (`default.custom.yaml`, `luna_pinyin.custom.yaml`) and is kept **byte-identical** to `daviddwlee84/dotfiles`'s copy of the same path — `diff -r` between the two dirs is the drift check, so edit one and copy to the other in the same session. Each platform is a one-line `{{ template "rime/…" . }}` renderer: `AppData/Roaming/Rime/` here, `private_Library/Rime/` (Squirrel) and `dot_config/ibus/rime/` (ibus-rime) there. Only `weasel.custom.yaml` is Windows-specific (`style/` is Weasel's own, `app_options` keys on the EXE name vs. Squirrel's bundle ids, and `global_ascii` doesn't exist on Squirrel). Plain managed files, **not** a `modify_` overlay: Rime persists runtime state to `user.yaml`, never back into `*.custom.yaml`. Two gotchas: a bare silent winget install registers **简体** (hence `--custom '/T'` in `Install-Weasel` — see `pitfalls/weasel-silent-install-registers-simplified-chinese.md`), and config edits need a redeploy, which `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
56	- **herdr** — `dot_config/herdr/` is deployed via `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` and gated on `installHerdr`. `config.toml` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` + `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`), never a plain managed file: herdr rewrites that file at runtime (onboarding flag, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]` bookkeeping) and a plain file clobbers it. The overlay enforces `[theme]`/`[ui]`/`[terminal]`/`[keys]` wholesale, pulls every other top-level key through, and re-asserts the single key `update.channel = "preview"` (the Windows installer rejects `stable`). `run_after_15_sync_herdr_skill.ps1.tmpl` exports the exact installed binary's `herdr --skill` output to real copies under both `~/.agents/skills/herdr/` and `~/.claude/skills/herdr/`; no symlink/junction is used. Helper-script paths in the keymap are baked **absolute at render time** — `pwsh -File` does not expand `~`. Six pwsh helpers (`_common.ps1` + run-command / new-tab-at-space-root / url-pick / path-pick / pane-copy / review-mark) back the `[[keys.command]]` bindings; three `herdr-*` tv channels and the herdr-plus quick-actions are gated by the same toggle. Ported from the parent repo 2026-07-27; the behaviours that still need a real Windows box are listed in [`backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md`](backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md).
57	- **git config** — `~/.gitconfig` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_dot_gitconfig.ps1.tmpl`), never a plain managed file: Git Credential Manager writes `[credential "azrepos:*"]` blocks into it out of band and a plain file would clobber them every apply. The baseline body is `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (identity from the existing `.name`/`.email` init prompts); the merge engine is `scripts/gitconfig-merge.ps1`, inlined via `{{ include }}` (the `editors/` idiom) and dot-sourced by `tests/GitConfig.Tests.ps1`. The model is **key-level pull-through**: the baseline owns a fixed set of `section.key` pairs and every other live key is carried over untouched — the inverse of the parent repo's allowlist, which would silently drop `[otel]` and future corp sections. Two hard rules: `core.hooksPath` is **never** emitted (git honours it *instead of* `.git/hooks/`, silently disarming `pre-commit`), and the carry dictionary is **case-sensitive** (`[ordered]@{}` collapses `azrepos:org/O365Exchange` into `azrepos:org/o365exchange`, merging two credential contexts).
58	- **Docs** — bilingual mkdocs-material (`docs/X.md` + `docs/X.zh-TW.md`), deployed to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/docs.yml`. `docs/rationale.md` records the design choices (scoop > Chocolatey, starship > oh-my-posh, pwsh > cmd, native pwsh tree > ported shell layer).
59	- **CI** — `.github/workflows/windows.yml` on `windows-latest` is the real gate: PSScriptAnalyzer, non-interactive `chezmoi init --apply`, render+parse of every `.ps1.tmpl`, and Pester.
60	
61	## Conventions & hard invariants
62	
63	1. **A new/renamed init prompt must update the CI flags in the same commit.** `chezmoi init --promptBool/--promptChoice "<text>=value"` matches the prompt's exact TEXT (3rd arg to `promptXOnce` in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`), used non-interactively by `.github/workflows/windows.yml`. Forget it → CI's init hangs/EOFs (`error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF`; this broke three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds` was added). Corollary: **never put `=` in a prompt's text** — the `name=value` parser splits on the first `=` (this broke the `role` prompt once). Enforced by `tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` (missing flag, stale flag, wrong flag kind, `=` in text), which CI runs *before* `chezmoi init` so the failure names the missing flag instead of EOF-ing — run `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` locally after touching either file.
64	2. **Run-scripts must never abort the apply.** The installer + editor/terminal/backup/skill scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'` (+ `PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$false`), collect failures via `Register-Failure`, print a summary, and exit 0. One bad scoop/winget manifest (e.g. btop's stale `.conf`) must not stop the rest.
65	3. **Preserve raw escapes when authoring config with control chars.** Alacritty CSI-u (`[…u`), VSCode `sendSequence`, tv `\t` — hand-typing tends to drop them. Generate via a throwaway Python script and re-parse (`tomllib` / `json`) to confirm the escape landed.
66	4. **tv channel commands are `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "…"` inside TOML literal (`'''…'''`) strings** — runs regardless of tv's shell, sidesteps nested-quote escaping; placeholders `{split: :0}` (space) / `{split:\t:0}` (tab). tv reads config from `%APPDATA%\television\` on Windows.

100	<!-- Snippet for the project's agent contract file (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md /

102	     markers; safe to re-run. -->

104	### Long-term backlog → `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
105	
106	When the user surfaces an idea explicitly **not** being implemented this
107	session (signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
108	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來"), add an entry to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using
109	the priority + effort tag schema. Do **not** create new `ROADMAP.md` /
110	`IDEAS.md` / `BACKLOG.md` files — `TODO.md` is the single index.
111	
112	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates the format. Run it
113	(`scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md`) after editing so syntax
114	drift is caught immediately.
115	
116	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
117	
118	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
119	
120	   ```
121	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
122	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
123	   ```
124	
125	   Inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane and
126	   re-runs the validator. Add `--backlog` to also scaffold
127	   `backlog/<slug>.md` from the bundled template.
128	
129	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
130	
131	   ```
132	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
133	   ```
134	
135	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox", run
136	   `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`. It prompts for the missing fields per loose
137	   line and calls `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs
138	   that only formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
139	
140	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh; run
141	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
142	
143	Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` companion doc when the item meets any of:
144	
145	- carries a `P?` tag (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
146	- captures a paused troubleshooting session that you intend to fix later
147	  (preserve the error trace + root cause analysis before context evaporates)
148	- weighs multiple options (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
149	- is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)
150	
151	`[S]` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the `TODO.md` line is
152	usually enough. See [`backlog/README.md`](backlog/README.md) for the full
153	template and "when to add a doc" rules.
154	
155	When implementing a `TODO.md` item, in the same commit:
156	
157	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`
158	   to move the entry into `## Done` with the dated syntax and re-validate.
159	2. Mark the corresponding `backlog/<slug>.md` (if any) `Status: shipped`
160	   and keep it as a historical record (don't delete — future-you may
161	   revisit adjacent decisions).
162	
163	`backlog/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore); it
164	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
165	
166	### Past pitfalls → `pitfalls/`
167	
168	When you spend more than ~15 minutes debugging something that wasn't
169	googleable and the fix is non-obvious, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
170	capturing:
171	
172	1. **Verbatim symptom** — copy-paste error messages exactly, do not
173	   paraphrase (preserves grep-ability for future-you / future agent)
174	2. **Root cause** — why this happens (with source / docs / upstream issue link)
175	3. **Workaround** — copy-pasteable commands or config diff
176	4. **Prevention** — how to avoid stepping on this again
177	
178	Title the doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause (you'll search by what
179	you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned). See
180	[`pitfalls/README.md`](pitfalls/README.md) for the full template and
181	when-to-add rules.
182	
183	**Pitfall vs Hard invariant**: a pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant in
184	this file when it (a) recurs across machines/agents/sessions despite being
185	documented, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround is non-obvious
186	enough that "remember to do X" isn't safe. When graduating, leave the
187	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the new
188	invariant.
189	
190	`pitfalls/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore) and
191	**not** auto-redacted; review for secrets before committing.

```text
118	function Invoke-CapturedPackageProcess {
119	    param(
120	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Executable,
121	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [string[]] $Arguments,
122	        [hashtable] $Environment = @{},
123	        [string] $WorkingDirectory,
124	        [ValidateRange(1, 86400)] [int] $TimeoutSeconds = 600,
125	        [ValidateSet('Host', 'StandardError', 'Capture')] [string] $OutputMode = 'Host'
126	    )
127	
128	    $startInfo = [Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo]::new()
129	    $startInfo.FileName = $Executable
130	    $startInfo.UseShellExecute = $false
131	    $startInfo.CreateNoWindow = $true
132	    $startInfo.RedirectStandardOutput = $true
133	    $startInfo.RedirectStandardError = $true
134	    if ($WorkingDirectory) { $startInfo.WorkingDirectory = $WorkingDirectory }
135	    foreach ($argument in $Arguments) { $startInfo.ArgumentList.Add([string] $argument) }
136	    foreach ($name in $Environment.Keys) {
137	        if ($null -eq $Environment[$name]) { $startInfo.Environment.Remove([string] $name) }
138	        else { $startInfo.Environment[[string] $name] = [string] $Environment[$name] }
139	    }
140	
141	    $process = [Diagnostics.Process]::new()
142	    $process.StartInfo = $startInfo
143	    $timedOut = $false
144	    $launchFailed = $false
145	    $exitCode = -1
146	    $stdout = ''
147	    $stderr = ''
148	    try {
149	        try {
150	            if (-not $process.Start()) { throw 'process did not start' }
151	        } catch {
152	            $launchFailed = $true
153	            $stderr = "failed to start $Executable`: $($_.Exception.Message)"
154	            return [pscustomobject]@{
155	                ExitCode = -1; TimedOut = $false; LaunchFailed = $true
156	                Stdout = ''; Stderr = (Protect-PackageSourceOutput $stderr)
157	            }
158	        }
159	
160	        $stdoutTask = $process.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync()
161	        $stderrTask = $process.StandardError.ReadToEndAsync()
162	        if (-not $process.WaitForExit($TimeoutSeconds * 1000)) {
163	            $timedOut = $true
164	            try { $process.Kill($true) } catch { $null = $_ }
165	            $process.WaitForExit()
166	        }
167	        $stdout = $stdoutTask.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
168	        $stderr = $stderrTask.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
169	        $exitCode = if ($timedOut) { -1 } else { $process.ExitCode }
170	    } finally {
171	        $process.Dispose()
172	    }
173	
174	    $stdout = Protect-PackageSourceOutput $stdout
175	    $stderr = Protect-PackageSourceOutput $stderr
176	    if ($OutputMode -eq 'Host') {
177	        if ($stdout) { Write-Host $stdout.TrimEnd() }
178	        if ($stderr) { [Console]::Error.Write($stderr) }
179	    } elseif ($OutputMode -eq 'StandardError') {
180	        if ($stdout) { [Console]::Error.Write($stdout) }
181	        if ($stderr) { [Console]::Error.Write($stderr) }
182	    }
183	
184	    [pscustomobject]@{
185	        ExitCode = $exitCode
186	        TimedOut = $timedOut
187	        LaunchFailed = $launchFailed
188	        Stdout = $stdout
189	        Stderr = $stderr
190	    }
191	}

243	function Invoke-PackageSourceCommand {
244	    [CmdletBinding()]
245	    param(
246	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [ValidateSet('uv', 'npm')] [string] $Manager,
247	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Executable,
248	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [string[]] $Arguments,
249	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Operation,

252	        [string] $PackageSpec,

255	        [hashtable] $AdditionalEnvironment = @{},
256	        [ValidateSet('Host', 'StandardError', 'Capture')] [string] $OutputMode = 'Host',
257	        [ValidateRange(1, 86400)] [int] $TimeoutSeconds = 600,
258	        [string] $CorporatePyPiIndex = $script:CorporatePyPiIndex,
259	        [string] $PublicPyPiIndex = $script:PublicPyPiIndex,
260	        [string] $CorporateNpmRegistry = $script:CorporateNpmRegistry,
261	        [string] $PublicNpmRegistry = $script:PublicNpmRegistry
262	    )

264	    $attempts = [Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
265	    $tempRoot = $null
266	    try {
267	        $workingDirectory = $null
268	        $baseEnvironment = @{}
269	        foreach ($key in $AdditionalEnvironment.Keys) { $baseEnvironment[$key] = $AdditionalEnvironment[$key] }
270	        if ($ManagedMachine) {

272	            if ($Manager -eq 'npm') {
273	                if (-not $NpmPrefix) { throw 'NpmPrefix is required for npm source isolation' }
274	                $tempRoot = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ('package-source-npm-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
275	                New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $tempRoot | Out-Null
276	                $userConfig = Join-Path $tempRoot 'user.npmrc'
277	                $globalConfig = Join-Path $tempRoot 'global.npmrc'
278	                [IO.File]::WriteAllText($userConfig, '', [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
279	                [IO.File]::WriteAllText($globalConfig, '', [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
280	                $baseEnvironment['NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG'] = $userConfig
281	                $baseEnvironment['NPM_CONFIG_GLOBALCONFIG'] = $globalConfig
282	                $workingDirectory = $tempRoot
283	            }
284	        }
285	
286	        $sourceQueue = [Collections.Generic.Queue[string]]::new()
287	        $sourceQueue.Enqueue($(if ($ManagedMachine) { 'corporate' } else { 'ambient' }))
288	        while ($sourceQueue.Count -gt 0) {
289	            $sourceKind = $sourceQueue.Dequeue()
290	            $attemptNumber = $attempts.Count + 1
291	            $sourceLabel = if ($sourceKind -eq 'ambient') { 'ambient package policy' } elseif ($Manager -eq 'uv') { "$sourceKind PyPI" } else { "$sourceKind npm" }
292	            Write-PackageSourceDiagnostic -OutputMode $OutputMode -Message "package-source[$Manager`:$Operation]: attempt $attemptNumber using $sourceLabel"
293	
294	            $attemptArguments = @($Arguments)
295	            $attemptEnvironment = @{} + $baseEnvironment
296	            if ($sourceKind -ne 'ambient') {
297	                $sourceUrl = if ($Manager -eq 'uv') {
298	                    if ($sourceKind -eq 'corporate') { $CorporatePyPiIndex } else { $PublicPyPiIndex }
299	                } else {
300	                    if ($sourceKind -eq 'corporate') { $CorporateNpmRegistry } else { $PublicNpmRegistry }
301	                }
302	                if ($Manager -eq 'uv') {
303	                    $attemptArguments = Add-UvSourceArguments -Arguments $attemptArguments -SourceUrl $sourceUrl
304	                } else {
305	                    $attemptArguments += "--registry=$sourceUrl"
306	                    $scope = Get-NpmPackageScope -PackageSpec $PackageSpec
307	                    if ($scope) { $attemptArguments += "--$scope`:registry=$sourceUrl" }
308	                    $attemptArguments += "--prefix=$NpmPrefix"
309	                    if ($NpmCache) { $attemptArguments += "--cache=$NpmCache" }
310	                }
311	            }
312	
313	            $processResult = Invoke-CapturedPackageProcess -Executable $Executable -Arguments $attemptArguments `
314	                -Environment $attemptEnvironment -WorkingDirectory $workingDirectory `
315	                -TimeoutSeconds $TimeoutSeconds -OutputMode $OutputMode
316	            $combinedOutput = "$($processResult.Stdout)`n$($processResult.Stderr)"
317	            $failureClass = if ($processResult.ExitCode -eq 0) { 'none' } else {
318	                Get-PackageFailureClass -Output $combinedOutput -TimedOut $processResult.TimedOut -LaunchFailed $processResult.LaunchFailed
319	            }
320	            $attempts.Add([pscustomobject]@{
321	                Source = $sourceKind
322	                ExitCode = $processResult.ExitCode
323	                TimedOut = $processResult.TimedOut
324	                FailureClass = $failureClass
325	                Stdout = $processResult.Stdout
326	                Stderr = $processResult.Stderr
327	            })
328	
329	            if ($processResult.ExitCode -eq 0) { break }
330	            Write-PackageSourceDiagnostic -OutputMode $OutputMode -Message "package-source[$Manager`:$Operation]: $sourceKind attempt failed: $failureClass"
331	
332	            if ($sourceKind -eq 'corporate' -and $AllowPublicFallback -and (Test-PackageFallbackEligible $failureClass)) {
333	                Write-PackageSourceDiagnostic -OutputMode $OutputMode -Message "package-source[$Manager`:$Operation]: public fallback enabled; retrying once"
334	                $sourceQueue.Enqueue('public')
335	            } elseif ($sourceKind -eq 'corporate') {
336	                $reason = if (-not $AllowPublicFallback) { 'fallback is disabled' } else { "$failureClass is not eligible" }
337	                Write-PackageSourceDiagnostic -OutputMode $OutputMode -Message "package-source[$Manager`:$Operation]: $reason; not retrying"
338	            }
339	        }
340	
341	        $final = $attempts[$attempts.Count - 1]
342	        [pscustomobject]@{
343	            Succeeded = $final.ExitCode -eq 0
344	            ExitCode = $final.ExitCode
345	            TimedOut = $final.TimedOut
346	            FallbackUsed = $attempts.Count -gt 1 -and $attempts[1].Source -eq 'public'
347	            FailureClass = $final.FailureClass
348	            Attempts = @($attempts)
349	            Stdout = $final.Stdout
350	            Stderr = $final.Stderr
351	        }
352	    } finally {
353	        if ($tempRoot) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $tempRoot -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
354	    }
355	}

357	function Get-ChezmoiPackageSourcePolicy {
358	    $raw = @(& chezmoi data --format json 2>$null)
359	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $raw) { throw 'could not read chezmoi package-source policy' }
360	    $data = ($raw -join "`n") | ConvertFrom-Json
361	    [pscustomobject]@{
362	        ManagedMachine = [bool] $data.managedMachine
363	        AllowPublicFallback = [bool] $data.allowPublicPackageFallback
364	    }
```

```text
146	    live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
147	except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
148	    # A corrupt live file must not block the apply — enforce the template.
149	    print("modify_config.toml: live config is not valid TOML; enforcing template", file=sys.stderr)
150	    live = {}
151	
152	for key, value in live.items():
153	    if key in MANAGED:
154	        continue
155	    if key in doc:
156	        # The template also declares this table. Keep herdr's runtime keys and
157	        # let the template win only on the keys it actually sets.
158	        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(doc[key], dict):
159	            for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
160	                if sub_key not in doc[key]:
161	                    doc[key][sub_key] = sub_value
162	        continue
163	    doc[key] = value
164	
165	for (table, sub_key), forced_value in FORCED.items():
166	    if table not in doc:
167	        doc[table] = tomlkit.table()
168	    doc[table][sub_key] = forced_value
169	
170	emit(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
171	'@
172	
173	    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($pyFile, $pySource, $utf8)
174	
175	    $childEnvironment = @{
176	        HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE = $tmplFile
177	        HERDR_LIVE_FILE = $liveFile
178	        HERDR_OUT_FILE = $outFile
179	    }
180	    $exe = $py[0]
181	    $rest = if ($py.Count -gt 1) { @($py[1..($py.Count - 1)]) + @($pyFile) } else { @($pyFile) }
182	    if ($pyUsesPackageRunner) {
183	        $result = Invoke-PackageSourceCommand -Manager uv -Executable $exe -Arguments $rest `
184	            -Operation herdr-tomlkit -ManagedMachine $managedMachine `
185	            -AllowPublicFallback $allowPublicPackageFallback -AdditionalEnvironment $childEnvironment `
186	            -OutputMode StandardError
187	        $rc = $result.ExitCode
188	    } else {
189	        $result = Invoke-CapturedPackageProcess -Executable $exe -Arguments $rest `
190	            -Environment $childEnvironment -OutputMode StandardError
191	        $rc = $result.ExitCode
192	    }
193	
194	    if ($rc -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outFile)) {
195	        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("modify_config.toml: merge failed (exit $rc); emitting managed template")
196	        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
197	        return
198	    }
199	
200	    Write-StdoutBytes ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($outFile))
201	} finally {
202	    foreach ($f in $tmplFile, $liveFile, $pyFile, $outFile) {
203	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $f -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
204	    }
205	}
```

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same

silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[

    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

```text
36	# Package registries: company-approved pull-through feeds on managed machines,
37	# otherwise optional China/GFW mirrors. Shared with profile.d so apply-time and
38	# interactive commands cannot drift apart.
39	{{ template "package-sources.ps1" . }}
40	$managedMachine = {{ if .managedMachine }}$true{{ else }}$false{{ end }}
41	$allowPublicPackageFallback = {{ if (get . "allowPublicPackageFallback") }}$true{{ else }}$false{{ end }}

45	{{ include "scripts/package-source-runner.ps1" }}

48	function Have($n) { [bool](Get-Command $n -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) }
49	function Register-Failure($what) { $script:Failures.Add($what); Write-Warning "FAILED (skipped): $what" }
50	
51	# Shared with profile.d/12_pueue.ps1: install-time service setup plus the
52	# no-admin detached-daemon fallback use the same readiness checks.
53	{{ include "scripts/pueue-bootstrap.ps1" }}

55	# --- scoop -----------------------------------------------------------------
56	function Test-Admin {
57	    # $true when this pwsh is running elevated (member of the Administrators role).
58	    try {
59	        $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
60	        ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal]$id).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
61	    } catch { $false }
62	}
63	
64	function Ensure-Scoop {
65	    if (-not (Have scoop)) {
66	        # get.scoop.sh returns install.ps1's text. Piping it to Invoke-Expression
67	        # works in a normal console, but an ELEVATED one is refused ("Running the
68	        # installer as administrator is disabled by default") unless -RunAsAdmin is
69	        # passed. Some dev boxes always open the shell as admin, so detect that and
70	        # forward the flag. We build a scriptblock from the fetched text so we can
71	        # pass args -- equivalent to `iex "& {$(irm get.scoop.sh)} -RunAsAdmin"`.
72	        $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod get.scoop.sh))
73	        if (Test-Admin) {
74	            Info 'scoop not found — installing (elevated console: passing -RunAsAdmin)'
75	            & $installer -RunAsAdmin
76	        } else {
77	            Info 'scoop not found — installing (user-scoped, no admin)'
78	            & $installer
79	        }
80	    }
81	    foreach ($b in 'main', 'extras', 'versions', 'nerd-fonts') {
82	        scoop bucket add $b *> $null
83	    }
84	}
85	
86	function Get-ScoopInstalled {
87	    try { return @((scoop export | ConvertFrom-Json).apps.name) } catch { return @() }
88	}
89	
90	function Scoop-Install([string[]]$apps) {
91	    if (-not $apps) { return }
92	    # Wrap in @() so a lone survivor stays an array. Without it PowerShell
93	    # unwraps a single match to a bare string, and `scoop install @missing`
94	    # then splats it one CHARACTER per arg => "Couldn't find manifest for 'm'"
95	    # when only "mise" was missing.
96	    $missing = @($apps | Where-Object { ($_ -split '/')[-1] -notin (Get-ScoopInstalled) })
97	    if (-not $missing) { Info 'scoop: all requested tools already present'; return }
98	    Info "scoop install: $($missing -join ', ')"
99	    try { scoop install @missing } catch { Write-Warning "scoop batch error: $_" }
100	    # Anything still absent after the batch = failed (scoop keeps going past a bad one).
101	    $after = Get-ScoopInstalled
102	    foreach ($app in $missing) {
103	        $name = ($app -split '/')[-1]
104	        if ($name -notin $after) { Register-Failure "scoop:$name" }
105	    }
106	}
107	
108	# --- winget ----------------------------------------------------------------
109	function Winget-Install([string]$id) {
110	    if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure "winget:$id (winget unavailable)"; return }
111	    winget list --id $id -e --accept-source-agreements *> $null
112	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { return }   # already installed
113	    Info "winget install $id"
114	    winget install --id $id -e --silent --scope user `
115	        --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
116	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
117	        # some packages don't support --scope user; retry machine scope.
118	        winget install --id $id -e --silent `
119	            --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
120	    }
121	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure "winget:$id" }
122	}

124	# Microsoft Store packages (installed by Store product id via the msstore
125	# source) — used for apps with no community winget manifest, e.g. Raycast and the
126	# official ChatGPT desktop app. msstore ignores --scope, so we don't pass it.
127	function Winget-InstallStore([string]$id) {
128	    if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure "msstore:$id (winget unavailable)"; return }
129	    winget list --id $id -e --accept-source-agreements *> $null
130	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { return }   # already installed
131	    Info "winget (msstore) install $id"
132	    winget install --id $id -e --source msstore --silent `
133	        --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
134	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure "msstore:$id" }
135	}

137	# --- npm CLI agents --------------------------------------------------------
138	function Npm-InstallGlobal([string[]]$pkgs) {
139	    if (-not (Have npm)) { foreach ($p in $pkgs) { Register-Failure "npm:$p (npm unavailable)" }; return }
140	    $npmExecutable = (Get-Command npm -CommandType Application | Select-Object -First 1).Source
141	    $npmRootOutput = @(npm root -g 2>$null)
142	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $npmRootOutput) {
143	        foreach ($p in $pkgs) { Register-Failure "npm:$p (cannot resolve global npm root)" }
144	        return
145	    }
146	    $npmRoot = ([string]$npmRootOutput[-1]).Trim()
147	    $npmPrefix = Split-Path -Parent $npmRoot
148	    $npmCacheOutput = @(npm config get cache 2>$null)
149	    $npmCache = if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0 -and $npmCacheOutput) { ([string]$npmCacheOutput[-1]).Trim() } else { '' }
150	    foreach ($p in $pkgs) {
151	        # Apply is install-only. Re-running `npm install -g` as an implicit
152	        # upgrade fails with EBUSY/EPERM whenever an agent executable is live on
153	        # Windows. A package.json is a cheap, registry-independent presence test.
154	        $packageManifest = Join-Path (Join-Path $npmRoot $p) 'package.json'
155	        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $packageManifest) {
156	            Info "npm: $p already installed -- skipping (upgrade: just upgrade-npm-agents)"
157	            continue
158	        }
159	        Info "npm i -g $p"
160	        $result = Invoke-PackageSourceCommand -Manager npm -Executable $env:ComSpec `
161	            -Arguments @('/d', '/c', $npmExecutable, 'install', '-g', $p) -Operation $p `
162	            -PackageSpec $p -NpmPrefix $npmPrefix -NpmCache $npmCache `
163	            -ManagedMachine $managedMachine -AllowPublicFallback $allowPublicPackageFallback
164	        if (-not $result.Succeeded) { Register-Failure "npm:$p" }
165	    }
166	}

169	# No scoop/winget/npm manifest — installs via herdr.dev's irm|iex bootstrap
170	# (same shape as Ensure-Scoop). This repo selects the preview channel; the bin
171	# junction is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Herdr\bin (added to PATH in profile.d/00_env.ps1).
172	function Install-Herdr {
173	    $herdrBin = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\Herdr\bin\herdr.exe'
174	    if ((Have herdr) -or (Test-Path -LiteralPath $herdrBin)) { Info 'herdr already installed'; return }
175	    Info 'installing herdr (preview) via herdr.dev/install.ps1'
176	    try {

178	        $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod https://herdr.dev/install.ps1))
179	        & $installer
180	        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $herdrBin)) { Register-Failure 'herdr' }
181	    } catch {
182	        Write-Warning "herdr install error: $_"

187	# herdr-plus — third-party herdr plugin backing the prefix+y (Quick Actions) and
188	# prefix+O (Projects) keybinds, plus the copy-pane Quick Actions this repo deploys
189	# to ~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/. We ship that CONFIG and
190	# those KEYBINDS, so not installing the plugin leaves both keys silently dead —
191	# hence installing it here rather than leaving it to the user.
192	#
193	# Requires go: the plugin's Windows build command is `go build -o bin/herdr-plus.exe .`
194	# (its sh-based build is skipped on Windows). go is gated behind installExtraRuntimes,
195	# so SKIP with an actionable message rather than failing when it is absent.
196	# `--yes` accepts the interactive "Install this plugin? [y/N]" prompt. Keep it
197	# after the repository argument: the Windows preview parses options in that order.
198	# NB: the keybinds must target the `-windows` action ids — herdr-plus scopes
199	# `quick-actions`/`projects` to linux+macos. See
200	# pitfalls/herdr-plus-action-does-not-support-platform-windows.md
201	function Install-HerdrPlus {
202	    if (-not (Have herdr)) { return }   # herdr install failed/skipped; nothing to add to
203	    $installed = $false
204	    try { $installed = ((herdr plugin list 2>&1) -join "`n") -match 'cloudmanic\.herdr-plus' } catch { $installed = $false }
205	    if ($installed) { Info 'herdr-plus plugin already installed'; return }
206	    if (-not (Have go)) {
207	        Info 'herdr-plus: skipped — needs go to build on Windows (scoop install go, or enable Extra runtimes)'
208	        return
209	    }
210	    Info 'herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus (backs prefix+y / prefix+O)'
211	    try {
212	        herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus --yes 2>&1 | Out-Host
213	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'herdr-plus' }
214	    } catch {
215	        Write-Warning "herdr-plus install error: $_"
216	        Register-Failure 'herdr-plus'
217	    }
218	}
219	
220	# --- Rime / Weasel (小狼毫) — Traditional Chinese input method ---------------
221	# Not routed through Winget-Install because two things need overriding:
222	#
223	#  1. The manifest is machine-scope NSIS, so `--scope user` can never work and
224	#     the install always raises UAC (same class as installWsl / installSshServer).
225	#  2. winget's silent switch for nullsoft is /S, and weasel's install.nsi maps a
226	#     bare /S to `WeaselSetup.exe /s` = register the TSF service as SIMPLIFIED
227	#     Chinese. Passing /T as well makes it use /t (Traditional) instead. Silent
228	#     mode also skips the 安裝選項 dialog and auto-runs WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy.
229	#
230	# `winget list` can't be used for the installed check: the manifest's ProductCode
231	# is "Weasel" but the ARP entry is the localized display name, so we read the
232	# InstallDir the NSIS installer writes to HKLM instead — which is also how we
233	# locate WeaselSetup.exe afterwards.
234	function Install-Weasel {
235	    $key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Rime\Weasel'
236	    $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
237	    if (-not $dir) {
238	        if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel (winget unavailable)'; return }
239	        Info 'winget install Rime.Weasel (machine scope — expect a UAC prompt)'
240	        winget install --id Rime.Weasel -e --silent --custom '/T' `
241	            --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
242	        $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
243	        if (-not $dir) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel'; return }
244	    } else {
245	        Info 'Weasel already installed'
246	    }
247	    # WeaselSetup's undocumented CLI (WeaselSetup/WeaselSetup.cpp). These two
248	    # only write HKCU, so they need no elevation and are safe to re-run.
249	    #   /lt          -> Weasel's own UI in 繁體中文
250	    #   /toggleascii -> Ctrl+Space toggles ASCII rather than the whole IME,
251	    #                   which is what makes global_ascii in weasel.custom.yaml
252	    #                   behave like a single 中/英 switch.
253	    $setup = Join-Path $dir 'WeaselSetup.exe'
254	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $setup) {
255	        & $setup /lt
256	        & $setup /toggleascii
257	    } else {
258	        Register-Failure 'weasel (WeaselSetup.exe not found; UI language + Ctrl+Space unset)'
259	    }
260	}

265	# Core CLI toolset — the shell baseline, always installed.
266	Scoop-Install @(
267	    'git', 'gh', 'glab', '7zip', 'make', 'just',
268	    'starship', 'zoxide', 'fzf', 'fd', 'ripgrep', 'bat', 'eza', 'glow', 'jq',
269	    'delta', 'lazygit', 'neovim', 'yazi', 'btop', 'pueue', 'television', 'tlrc',
270	    'uv', 'gnupg',
271	    # Runtimes are NATIVE via scoop, not mise: mise's activate/shims are
272	    # unreliable on Windows and it has no windows-arm64 bun build. node + bun
273	    # here; Python via uv (below); go/rust/ruby under Extra runtimes.
274	    # copilot-proxy needs bun/bunx.
275	    'nodejs-lts', 'bun',
276	    # LazyVim pins nvim-treesitter to the `main` branch, which compiles parsers
277	    # by shelling out to `tree-sitter build`. That CLI compiles via Rust's `cc`
278	    # crate, which only knows MSVC / GCC / Clang -- NOT zig (only the retired
279	    # `master` branch accepted zig). So the parser compiler must be a real gcc on
280	    # PATH; zig here does nothing. scoop's `gcc` is nuwen MinGW-w64, amd64-only --
281	    # which also matches the amd64 nvim (native on x64, x64-emulated on ARM64), so
282	    # this ONE line covers both arches (previously gcc was ARM64-only). Plus the
283	    # tree-sitter CLI `main` requires, and win32yank so `unnamedplus` yanks reach
284	    # the Windows clipboard. (Leaner gcc alt: scoop `mingw` = niXman MinGW-w64 UCRT.)
285	    'gcc', 'tree-sitter', 'win32yank'
286	)

288	# Make the newly installed client immediately usable. Elevated applies install
289	# Pueue 4's built-in Windows service (autostart at login); non-elevated applies
290	# start detached daemon mode. profile.d/12_pueue.ps1 covers future shell starts.

295	# gh-dash: GitHub PR/issue dashboard TUI (`gh dash`). It's a gh extension, not a
296	# scoop package, so it needs gh to be authenticated -- this no-ops on a fresh
297	# machine until `gh auth login`. run_onchange only re-fires when this script
298	# changes, so after authenticating, install by hand (`gh extension install
299	# dlvhdr/gh-dash`) or force a reapply (`chezmoi state delete-bucket
300	# --bucket=entryState`). gh-notify / gh-select from the Unix repo are bash-only
301	# extensions and are intentionally skipped on Windows.
302	if (Have gh) {
303	    gh auth status *> $null
304	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
305	        $ghExts = gh extension list 2>$null | Out-String
306	        if ($ghExts -notmatch 'dlvhdr/gh-dash') {
307	            Info 'gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash'
308	            gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash
309	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'gh-ext:gh-dash' }
310	        }
311	    } else {
312	        Info 'gh not authenticated -- skipping gh-dash (gh auth login, then reapply)'
313	    }
314	}

320	# (not just python3.x) in UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR (~/.local/bin, on PATH via 00_env
321	# ahead of the Store's python.exe app-alias). On uv 0.8+ `--default` lives behind
322	# preview mode, so it must be paired with `--preview` (older uv just ignored it) —
323	# without it, current uv errors: "`--default` is only available in preview mode".
324	if (Have uv) {

327	    uv python install --default --preview 2>&1 | Out-Host

336	    }

338	        Set-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -InstallationPolicy Trusted -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

399	# peon-ping — game-character voice lines for agent events (CESP player; packs
400	# from the OpenPeon registry). Installed regardless of the `agentSounds` tier so
401	# `peon preview` / `peon packs list` are always available to experiment with;
402	# the tier only decides whether HOOKS get wired, and that happens in
403	# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl.
404	#
405	# `--openpeon` reroots the whole install at the tool-agnostic ~/.openpeon so the
406	# installer never touches ~/.claude/settings.json — hook wiring is ours to
407	# declare (same rule the parent repo applies to workmux's `wm setup`).
408	# NB: the PowerShell installer's param block is
409	#   param([string[]]$Packs, [switch]$All, [string]$Lang, [switch]$Local,
410	#         [switch]$Global, [switch]$OpenPeon, [switch]$InitLocalConfig)
411	# — there is NO -NoRc (that is the bash install.sh flag only), and it does not
412	# touch $PROFILE, so nothing extra is needed to keep our profile clean.
413	# Idempotent: skipped once peon.ps1 exists.
414	$peonRoot = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon'
415	$peonHook = Join-Path $peonRoot 'hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
416	if (-not (Test-Path $peonHook)) {
417	    Info 'peon-ping (agent completion sounds, ~/.openpeon root)'
418	    try {
419	        # Upstream install.ps1 dot-sources scripts/install-utils.ps1 relative to
420	        # $PSScriptRoot when run via -File; it only self-downloads that helper
421	        # when $PSScriptRoot is empty (irm|iex). So stage BOTH files preserving
422	        # the scripts/ layout in a temp dir, then run install.ps1 with -File.
423	        $peonStage = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'peon-ping-install'
424	        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts') | Out-Null
425	        $peonInstaller = Join-Path $peonStage 'install.ps1'
426	        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
427	            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/install.ps1' `
428	            -OutFile $peonInstaller
429	        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
430	            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/scripts/install-utils.ps1' `
431	            -OutFile (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts\install-utils.ps1')
432	        & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $peonInstaller `
433	            -OpenPeon -Packs 'league_of_legends'
434	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping' }
435	        # The installer downloads the pack but leaves default_pack="peon" — a pack
436	        # that ships NO sounds — so a fresh install is silent ("No sound files
437	        # found for pack 'peon'"). Activate the pack we just seeded. Runs only on
438	        # first install (whole block is guarded on peon.ps1 absence), so a pack the
439	        # user later switches to via `peon packs use` is never clobbered.
440	        $peonCli = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\peon.cmd'
441	        if (Test-Path $peonCli) {
442	            & $peonCli packs use league_of_legends
443	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack' }
444	        } else {
445	            Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack (peon CLI shim missing)'
446	        }
447	    } catch {
448	        Register-Failure 'peon-ping'
449	    }
450	} else {
451	    Info 'peon-ping already installed — skipping (upgrade: peon update)'
452	}
453	{{ end -}}

455	{{ if .installSpecstoryBuild -}}
456	# EXPERIMENTAL SpecStory Windows CLI. There is no native-Windows release yet;
457	# Windows/WSL support lives in the unmerged getspecstory PR #191. Build it from
458	# source (opt-in) and drop specstory.exe in ~/.local/bin so the Copilot module's
459	# session auto-save (claude-copilot) can pick it up. Needs git (core) + go (enable
460	# Extra runtimes, or `scoop install go`). Treat as experimental — may break until
461	# the PR lands. Tracking + revisit criteria: backlog/specstory-windows-native-cli.md.
462	if ((Have git) -and (Have go)) {
463	    try {
464	        $ssCache = Join-Path $HOME '.cache\specstory-build'
465	        $ssRepo  = Join-Path $ssCache 'getspecstory'
466	        $ssBin   = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
467	        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $ssCache, $ssBin | Out-Null
468	        if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $ssRepo '.git'))) {
469	            Info 'specstory: cloning specstoryai/getspecstory'
470	            git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory.git $ssRepo
471	        }
472	        Push-Location $ssRepo
473	        try {
474	            Info 'specstory: fetching PR #191'
475	            $ssRemoteRef = 'refs/remotes/origin/pr-191'
476	            git fetch origin "pull/191/head:$ssRemoteRef" --force
477	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'git fetch of SpecStory PR #191 failed' }
478	            # Detached checkout leaves no local branch checked out, so the next
479	            # apply can safely force-refresh the remote-tracking ref above.
480	            git checkout --detach --force $ssRemoteRef
481	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'git checkout of SpecStory PR #191 failed' }
482	            $ssOut = Join-Path $ssBin 'specstory.exe'
483	            Push-Location (Join-Path $ssRepo 'specstory-cli')
484	            try { Info "specstory: go build -> $ssOut"; go build -o $ssOut . } finally { Pop-Location }
485	            if (Test-Path $ssOut) { Info "specstory: built $ssOut" }
486	            else { Register-Failure 'specstory-build (go build produced no binary)' }
487	        } finally { Pop-Location }
488	    } catch {
489	        Write-Warning "specstory-build error: $_"
490	        Register-Failure 'specstory-build'
491	    }
492	} else {
493	    Register-Failure 'specstory-build (needs git + go; enable Extra runtimes or run: scoop install go)'
494	}
495	{{ end -}}

596	# Clink = Bash-style line editing for cmd.exe, so starship / zoxide / fzf work in
597	# the DOS prompt too (scoop main bucket). pwsh stays the default shell; this is an
598	# opt-in secondary target with prompt + navigation parity only. Our starship.lua
599	# deploys via chezmoi (AppData/Local/clink/starship.lua). The zoxide / fzf Clink
600	# bridges have no scoop/winget manifest (and zoxide has no native cmd target), so
601	# -- like herdr -- we fetch them from upstream into the Clink profile dir at apply
602	# time. Network/offline failures are collected, never fatal; starship still works.
603	Scoop-Install @('clink')
604	if (Have clink) {
605	    clink autorun install *> $null                 # HKCU AutoRun; inject into every cmd.exe (no admin)
606	    $clinkDir = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'clink'
607	    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $clinkDir | Out-Null

609	        'zoxide.lua' = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shunsambongi/clink-zoxide/master/zoxide.lua'
610	        'fzf.lua'    = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisant996/clink-fzf/master/fzf.lua'
611	    }
612	    foreach ($name in $clinkPlugins.Keys) {
613	        Info "clink plugin: $name"
614	        try { Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri $clinkPlugins[$name] -OutFile (Join-Path $clinkDir $name) }
615	        catch { Register-Failure "clink-plugin:$name" }
616	    }
617	    # fzf.default_bindings is a setting DEFINED INSIDE fzf.lua, and `clink set`
618	    # reloads the profile scripts first -- so this must run AFTER fzf.lua is
619	    # downloaded above, else the setting is unknown and the value is silently
620	    # not persisted (the *> $null swallows the "unknown setting" error).
621	    clink set fzf.default_bindings true *> $null    # Ctrl-R history / Ctrl-T files / Alt-C dir
622	} else { Register-Failure 'clink (autorun/plugins not configured)' }
```
