645	# built from source with `go install` -- the same path the parent repo takes on
646	# Linux (dot_ansible/roles/go_tools); macOS there uses the Homebrew tap.
647	# GOBIN/GOPATH mirror that unix convention: the binary lands in ~/.local/bin
648	# (already on PATH via profile.d/00_env.ps1) and the module cache in
649	# ~/.local/share/go rather than recreating ~/go.
650	#
651	# It is pure Go (modernc.org/sqlite -- no cgo) and cross-compiles cleanly for
652	# windows/amd64 and windows/arm64. The FIRST build is slow (several minutes: the
653	# embedded swagger-ui bundle + sqlite); later applies no-op via the version check
654	# below. Bump $translateVersion to upgrade -- editing it re-renders this script,
655	# which is what re-fires the run_onchange. go.mod needs go >= 1.26.4; the default
656	# GOTOOLCHAIN=auto fetches a newer toolchain if scoop's go is older.
657	$translateVersion = 'v0.5.2'
658	Scoop-Install @('go')   # self-contained: installExtraRuntimes may well be off
659	if (Have go) {
660	    $trBin  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\translate.exe'
661	    $trHave = ''
662	    # `translate --version` prints "translate version v0.5.2 ..."; a module-proxy
663	    # build carries no VCS metadata, so token 3 is exactly the module version. An
664	    # absent/unparseable answer just falls through to a reinstall, which is cheap
665	    # once the module cache is warm.
666	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin) {
667	        try { $trHave = ((& $trBin --version 2>$null) -split '\s+')[2] } catch { $trHave = '' }
668	    }
669	    if ($trHave -eq $translateVersion) {
670	        Info "translate $translateVersion already installed"
671	    } else {
672	        Info "go install translate@$translateVersion (first build takes several minutes)"
673	        $env:GOBIN  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
674	        $env:GOPATH = Join-Path $HOME '.local\share\go'
675	        go install "github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@$translateVersion" 2>&1 | Out-Host
676	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin)) {
677	            Register-Failure "go:translate@$translateVersion"
678	        }
679	    }
680	} else {
681	    Register-Failure 'translate (needs go; enable Extra runtimes or run: scoop install go)'
682	}
683	{{ end -}}
684	
685	{{ if .installInputMethod -}}
686	# Rime input method. The managed YAML under %APPDATA%\Rime is deployed by chezmoi
687	# itself (gated in .chezmoiignore); 重新部署 happens in
688	# run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1 once the files are on disk.
689	Install-Weasel
690	{{ end -}}
691	
692	if ($script:Failures.Count -gt 0) {
693	    Write-Warning ("package install: {0} item(s) failed and were skipped:" -f $script:Failures.Count)
694	    $script:Failures | ForEach-Object { Write-Warning "  - $_" }
695	    Write-Warning "This is a run_onchange script; an unchanged apply will not retry it."
696	    Write-Warning "Retry only this installer with: chezmoi state delete --bucket=entryState --key='C:/Users/{{ .chezmoi.username }}/.chezmoiscripts/10_packages.ps1'; chezmoi apply"
697	} else {
698	    Info 'package install complete — no failures'
699	}
700

2	# Guards hard invariant #1 (AGENTS.md): every init prompt in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl
3	# must have a matching non-interactive flag in .github/workflows/windows.yml.
4	#
5	# Why this exists: adding a prompt without the flag does not fail loudly at
6	# authoring time — it fails much later, on the Windows runner, as an opaque
7	#   error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF
8	# because `chezmoi init --no-tty` has no answer for the new question and hits
9	# end-of-input. That broke CI for three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds`
10	# was added. This test turns that into a local `Invoke-Pester` failure with the
11	# exact missing flag line to paste in.
12	#
13	# Matching is on the prompt's TEXT (3rd arg to promptXOnce), because that is
14	# what chezmoi's `--promptBool 'text=value'` parser keys on — not the variable
15	# name.
16

18	    $repo = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent
19	    $tomlTmpl = Join-Path $repo '.chezmoi.toml.tmpl'
20	    $workflow = Join-Path $repo '.github/workflows/windows.yml'
21	
22	    # promptBoolOnce . "varName" "Prompt text" <default>

418	    try {
419	        # Upstream install.ps1 dot-sources scripts/install-utils.ps1 relative to

428	            -OutFile $peonInstaller
429	        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
430	            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/scripts/install-utils.ps1' `
431	            -OutFile (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts\install-utils.ps1')
432	        & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $peonInstaller `
433	            -OpenPeon -Packs 'league_of_legends'
434	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping' }
435	        # The installer downloads the pack but leaves default_pack="peon" — a pack
436	        # that ships NO sounds — so a fresh install is silent ("No sound files

438	        # first install (whole block is guarded on peon.ps1 absence), so a pack the
439	        # user later switches to via `peon packs use` is never clobbered.
440	        $peonCli = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\peon.cmd'
441	        if (Test-Path $peonCli) {
442	            & $peonCli packs use league_of_legends
443	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack' }
444	        } else {
445	            Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack (peon CLI shim missing)'
446	        }
447	    } catch {
448	        Register-Failure 'peon-ping'
449	    }

452	}

646	# Linux (dot_ansible/roles/go_tools); macOS there uses the Homebrew tap.
647	# GOBIN/GOPATH mirror that unix convention: the binary lands in ~/.local/bin
648	# (already on PATH via profile.d/00_env.ps1) and the module cache in
649	# ~/.local/share/go rather than recreating ~/go.
650	#
651	# It is pure Go (modernc.org/sqlite -- no cgo) and cross-compiles cleanly for
652	# windows/amd64 and windows/arm64. The FIRST build is slow (several minutes: the
653	# embedded swagger-ui bundle + sqlite); later applies no-op via the version check
654	# below. Bump $translateVersion to upgrade -- editing it re-renders this script,
655	# which is what re-fires the run_onchange. go.mod needs go >= 1.26.4; the default
656	# GOTOOLCHAIN=auto fetches a newer toolchain if scoop's go is older.
657	$translateVersion = 'v0.5.2'
658	Scoop-Install @('go')   # self-contained: installExtraRuntimes may well be off
659	if (Have go) {
660	    $trBin  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\translate.exe'
661	    $trHave = ''
662	    # `translate --version` prints "translate version v0.5.2 ..."; a module-proxy
663	    # build carries no VCS metadata, so token 3 is exactly the module version. An
664	    # absent/unparseable answer just falls through to a reinstall, which is cheap
665	    # once the module cache is warm.
666	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin) {
667	        try { $trHave = ((& $trBin --version 2>$null) -split '\s+')[2] } catch { $trHave = '' }
668	    }
669	    if ($trHave -eq $translateVersion) {
670	        Info "translate $translateVersion already installed"
671	    } else {
672	        Info "go install translate@$translateVersion (first build takes several minutes)"
673	        $env:GOBIN  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
674	        $env:GOPATH = Join-Path $HOME '.local\share\go'
675	        go install "github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@$translateVersion" 2>&1 | Out-Host
676	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin)) {
677	            Register-Failure "go:translate@$translateVersion"

Each platform is a one-line `{{ template "rime/…" . }}` renderer: `AppData/Roaming/Rime/` here, `private_Library/Rime/` (Squirrel) and `dot_config/ibus/rime/` (ibus-rime) there. Only `weasel.custom.yaml` is Windows-specific (`style/` is Weasel's own, `app_options` keys on the EXE name vs. Squirrel's bundle ids, and `global_ascii` doesn't exist on Squirrel). Plain managed files, **not** a `modify_` overlay: Rime persists runtime state to `user.yaml`, never back into `*.custom.yaml`. Two gotchas: a bare silent winget install registers **简体** (hence `--custom '/T'` in `Install-Weasel` — see `pitfalls/weasel-silent-install-registers-simplified-chinese.md`), and config edits need a redeploy, which `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.

61	## Conventions & hard invariants
62	
63	1. **A new/renamed init prompt must update the CI flags in the same commit.** `chezmoi init --promptBool/--promptChoice "<text>=value"` matches the prompt's exact TEXT (3rd arg to `promptXOnce` in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`), used non-interactively by `.github/workflows/windows.yml`. Forget it → CI's init hangs/EOFs (`error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF`; this broke three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds` was added). Corollary: **never put `=` in a prompt's text** — the `name=value` parser splits on the first `=` (this broke the `role` prompt once). Enforced by `tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` (missing flag, stale flag, wrong flag kind, `=` in text), which CI runs *before* `chezmoi init` so the failure names the missing flag instead of EOF-ing — run `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` locally after touching either file.
64	2. **Run-scripts must never abort the apply.** The installer + editor/terminal/backup/skill scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'` (+ `PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$false`), collect failures via `Register-Failure`, print a summary, and exit 0. One bad scoop/winget manifest (e.g. btop's stale `.conf`) must not stop the rest.
65	3. **Preserve raw escapes when authoring config with control chars.** Alacritty CSI-u (`[…u`), VSCode `sendSequence`, tv `\t` — hand-typing tends to drop them. Generate via a throwaway Python script and re-parse (`tomllib` / `json`) to confirm the escape landed.
66	4. **tv channel commands are `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "…"` inside TOML literal (`'''…'''`) strings** — runs regardless of tv's shell, sidesteps nested-quote escaping; placeholders `{split: :0}` (space) / `{split:\t:0}` (tab). tv reads config from `%APPDATA%\television\` on Windows.
67	5. **Editors use a run_onchange pwsh merger, not `modify_`** (`modify_` interpreter selection is unreliable on Windows). Overlay sources live in `editors/` (chezmoi-ignored, embedded via `{{ include }}`).
68	6. **The agent skill body lives once** in `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`; both `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` and `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` render it via `{{ "{{" }} template … {{ "}}" }}` → real files at `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/`. Edit the shared template, not the two one-line renderers (no symlink/junction — those need elevation/Developer Mode on Windows).
69	7. **PSScriptAnalyzer exclusions are intentional** (`PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`): hyphenated command names, `Write-Host`, `Invoke-Expression` for tool init, no-BOM UTF-8. Don't "fix" these; do fix real Errors.
70	8. **Public package fallback is opt-in, deny-first, and single-source.** Only repo-owned npm agent operations and uv dependency resolution may use `scripts/package-source-runner.ps1`; corporate is always attempted first and public at most once. Never add public as an extra index, broaden fallback beyond timeout/transient-network/HTTP-5xx, or bypass 401/403, TLS/certificate, package-absence, policy, solver/build, or local-state failures. Go/Rust/Ruby/Scoop/winget/Git/CDN operations have no corporate source and must not use this fallback.

100	<!-- Snippet for the project's agent contract file (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md /

102	     markers; safe to re-run. -->
103	
104	### Long-term backlog → `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
105	
106	When the user surfaces an idea explicitly **not** being implemented this
107	session (signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
108	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來"), add an entry to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using
109	the priority + effort tag schema. Do **not** create new `ROADMAP.md` /
110	`IDEAS.md` / `BACKLOG.md` files — `TODO.md` is the single index.
111	
112	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates the format. Run it
113	(`scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md`) after editing so syntax
114	drift is caught immediately.
115	
116	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
117	
118	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
119	
120	   ```
121	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
122	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
123	   ```
124	
125	   Inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane and
126	   re-runs the validator. Add `--backlog` to also scaffold
127	   `backlog/<slug>.md` from the bundled template.
128	
129	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
130	
131	   ```
132	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
133	   ```
134	
135	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox", run
136	   `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`. It prompts for the missing fields per loose
137	   line and calls `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs
138	   that only formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
139	
140	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh; run
141	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
142	
143	Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` companion doc when the item meets any of:
144	
145	- carries a `P?` tag (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
146	- captures a paused troubleshooting session that you intend to fix later
147	  (preserve the error trace + root cause analysis before context evaporates)
148	- weighs multiple options (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
149	- is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)
150	
151	`[S]` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the `TODO.md` line is
152	usually enough. See [`backlog/README.md`](backlog/README.md) for the full
153	template and "when to add a doc" rules.
154	
155	When implementing a `TODO.md` item, in the same commit:
156	
157	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`
158	   to move the entry into `## Done` with the dated syntax and re-validate.
159	2. Mark the corresponding `backlog/<slug>.md` (if any) `Status: shipped`
160	   and keep it as a historical record (don't delete — future-you may
161	   revisit adjacent decisions).
162	
163	`backlog/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore); it
164	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
165	
166	### Past pitfalls → `pitfalls/`
167	
168	When you spend more than ~15 minutes debugging something that wasn't
169	googleable and the fix is non-obvious, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
170	capturing:
171	
172	1. **Verbatim symptom** — copy-paste error messages exactly, do not
173	   paraphrase (preserves grep-ability for future-you / future agent)
174	2. **Root cause** — why this happens (with source / docs / upstream issue link)
175	3. **Workaround** — copy-pasteable commands or config diff
176	4. **Prevention** — how to avoid stepping on this again
177	
178	Title the doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause (you'll search by what
179	you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned). See
180	[`pitfalls/README.md`](pitfalls/README.md) for the full template and
181	when-to-add rules.
182	
183	**Pitfall vs Hard invariant**: a pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant in
184	this file when it (a) recurs across machines/agents/sessions despite being
185	documented, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround is non-obvious
186	enough that "remember to do X" isn't safe. When graduating, leave the
187	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the new
188	invariant.
189	
190	`pitfalls/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore) and
191	**not** auto-redacted; review for secrets before committing.

 # pueue-bootstrap.ps1 — make the pueue client usable without a manual daemon
 # terminal. Included into both the package installer and the PowerShell profile.
 
 function Resolve-PueueCommand {
     param(
         [Parameter(Mandatory)]
         [ValidateSet('pueue', 'pueued')]
         [string]$Name
     )
 
     $command = Get-Command $Name -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
         Select-Object -First 1
     if ($command) { return $command.Source }
 
     # A first-time Scoop install can create the shim after this pwsh process
     # captured PATH. Resolve the stable `current` junction as a fallback.
     $scoop = Get-Command scoop -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
         Select-Object -First 1
     if (-not $scoop) { return $null }
 
     $prefixOutput = @(& $scoop.Source prefix pueue 2>$null)
     if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $prefixOutput) { return $null }
     $prefix = ([string]$prefixOutput[-1]).Trim()
     $candidate = Join-Path $prefix "$Name.exe"
     if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $candidate) { return $candidate }
     return $null
 }
 
 function Test-PueueAdministrator {
     if (-not $IsWindows) { return $false }
     try {
         $identity = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
         $principal = [Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal]$identity
         return $principal.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
     } catch {
         return $false
     }
 }

             $script:ClientCalls++

             $script:DaemonCalls.Add(($args -join ' '))

         }

1	#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Runs under pwsh via [interpreters.ps1] in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl. chezmoi pipes the
5	# CURRENT target file into stdin and takes the new contents from stdout.
6	#
7	# WHY AN OVERLAY (this replaced a plain managed dot_config/herdr/config.toml):
8	# herdr rewrites this file at runtime — the onboarding flag, in-app settings
9	# popups, [session] / [remote] / [experimental] / [update] state. A plain managed
10	# file clobbers all of that on every `chezmoi apply`, which can re-trigger
11	# onboarding. The parent (unix) repo hit this and moved create_ -> modify_ on
12	# 2026-07-06; this repo's config was added five days later and still used the
13	# plain form. Same fix, ported.
14	#
15	# MERGE MODEL — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
16	#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
17	#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
18	#   - Every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file that is NOT managed and NOT already in
19	#     the template is copied across (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
20	#     [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
21	#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins).
22	#   - FORCED single keys are re-asserted INTO a pulled-through table, so the table
23	#     keeps herdr's own bookkeeping. Windows needs exactly one: update.channel
24	#     must stay "preview" (the installer rejects "stable" on Windows builds), but
25	#     [update] also holds herdr's last-check state, which we do not want to wipe.
26	#     This sub-key merge is the one deliberate divergence from the unix overlay.
27	#
28	# WHY tomlkit (not a hand-rolled emitter): herdr's config has an array-of-tables
29	# ([[keys.command]]) and comments worth keeping; stdlib tomllib is read-only.
30	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees >=3.11 -> stdlib tomllib), fall back to
31	# system python, then to emitting the raw template (a fresh host with neither
32	# still gets a full config — note we emit the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a
33	# fresh host stdin is empty).
34	#
35	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
36	# Validate the result with `herdr server reload-config` (empty diagnostics).
37	
38	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
39	
40	# modify_ scripts run under `pwsh -NoProfile`, so the deployed 05_mirrors.ps1
41	# fragment is not loaded here. Apply the same source policy inline before uv
42	# resolves tomlkit: managed machines must use the IT-approved pull-through feed.

49	# and no BOM or trailing CRLF churn creeps into chezmoi's diff.
50	function Write-StdoutBytes {
51	    param([byte[]] $Bytes)
52	    $out = [Console]::OpenStandardOutput()
53	    $out.Write($Bytes, 0, $Bytes.Length)
54	    $out.Flush()
55	}

58	
59	$templateText = @'
60	{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
61	'@
62	
63	$liveText = [Console]::In.ReadToEnd()
64	
65	$tmpDir = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()
66	$stamp = [System.IO.Path]::GetRandomFileName()

68	$liveFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-live-$stamp.toml"

100	import sys

103	live_path = os.environ["HERDR_LIVE_FILE"]

105	
106	with open(tmpl_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
107	    template_text = fh.read()
108	
109	
110	def emit(text):
111	    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
112	        fh.write(text)
113	
114	
115	try:
116	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
117	except ModuleNotFoundError:
118	    try:
119	        import tomli as tomllib
120	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
121	        # No TOML reader -> can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is.
122	        emit(template_text)
123	        sys.exit(0)
124	
125	try:
126	    import tomlkit
127	except ModuleNotFoundError:
128	    print(

130	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
131	        file=sys.stderr,
132	    )
133	    emit(template_text)

135	
136	# Tables the template owns outright.
137	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
138	# Single keys re-asserted into an otherwise pulled-through table.
139	FORCED = {("update", "channel"): "preview"}
140	
141	with open(live_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
142	    live_text = fh.read().strip()
143	
144	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
145	try:

147	except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:

149	    print("modify_config.toml: live config is not valid TOML; enforcing template", file=sys.stderr)
150	    live = {}

152	for key, value in live.items():

154	        continue

157	        # let the template win only on the keys it actually sets.
158	        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(doc[key], dict):
159	            for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
160	                if sub_key not in doc[key]:

162	        continue
163	    doc[key] = value

165	for (table, sub_key), forced_value in FORCED.items():
166	    if table not in doc:
167	        doc[table] = tomlkit.table()
168	    doc[table][sub_key] = forced_value
169	
170	emit(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
171	'@
172	
173	    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($pyFile, $pySource, $utf8)
174	
175	    $childEnvironment = @{

177	        HERDR_LIVE_FILE = $liveFile
178	        HERDR_OUT_FILE = $outFile

185	            -AllowPublicFallback $allowPublicPackageFallback -AdditionalEnvironment $childEnvironment `
186	            -OutputMode StandardError
187	        $rc = $result.ExitCode
188	    } else {
189	        $result = Invoke-CapturedPackageProcess -Executable $exe -Arguments $rest `
190	            -Environment $childEnvironment -OutputMode StandardError
191	        $rc = $result.ExitCode
192	    }
193	
194	    if ($rc -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outFile)) {
195	        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("modify_config.toml: merge failed (exit $rc); emitting managed template")
196	        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
197	        return
198	    }
199	
200	    Write-StdoutBytes ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($outFile))
201	} finally {
202	    foreach ($f in $tmplFile, $liveFile, $pyFile, $outFile) {
203	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $f -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
204	    }
205	}

 #!/usr/bin/env bun
 // copilot-throttle-shim.js — a tiny streaming reverse proxy that sits IN FRONT
 // of the local copilot-api fork (default :4141). It provides the request
 // compatibility fixes shared by Codex/Claude Code and stops GitHub's enterprise
 // Copilot backend from 403-ing ("Forbidden") on bursts of premium requests,
 // WITHOUT adding latency to normal single-agent flow.
 //
 //   agent client ─▶ shim (:4142) ─▶ copilot-api fork (:4141) ─▶ Copilot backend
 //                    │
 //                    ├─ semaphore: at most MAX concurrent in-flight upstream
 //                    │   POSTs; a burst queues instead of hitting the backend
 //                    │   all at once (that simultaneity is what trips abuse
 //                    │   detection). Under the cap there is ZERO added latency.
 //                    │
-//                    ├─ transparent retry on 403/429/502/503/504 + network
+//                    ├─ transparent retry on 403/429/500/502/503/504 + network
 //                    │   errors, jittered backoff, BEFORE any response body is
 //                    │   streamed — so the agent never sees the transient 403
 //                    │   ("Please run /login"). GET/HEAD (health, /v1/models)
 //                    │   bypass both, so liveness checks stay instant.
 //                    │
 //                    └─ SSE keepalive + stall watchdog: an OpenAI reasoning
 //                        model produces NOTHING on the wire until its first
 //                        token, and copilot-api withholds the response headers
 //                        for that whole time, so the client socket can sit
 //                        silent for minutes. See "silent socket" below.

 # herdr — native Windows terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (preview beta).
 #
 # Windows port of the parent dotfiles repo's .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
 # It mirrors the tmux/unix keymap as closely as the Windows build allows; every
 # binding that could NOT be carried over is listed in
 # backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md with the reason.
 #
 # THIS FILE IS THE MANAGED BODY of a chezmoi modify_ overlay
 # (dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl). The overlay enforces the tables
 # below on every `chezmoi apply` and preserves the keys herdr writes back at
 # runtime (onboarding / [session] / [remote] / [experimental] / [update] state).
 # Tracking this as a PLAIN managed file — which is what this repo did before —
 # clobbers that writeback and can re-trigger onboarding.
 #
 # Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
 # Full default: `herdr --default-config`
 # Validate after editing: `herdr server reload-config` (expect empty diagnostics)
 #
 # Helper-script paths are baked ABSOLUTE at render time on purpose: `pwsh -File`
 # does NOT expand a leading `~` (verified), and herdr passes the command string
 # through without shell tilde expansion on Windows.
 #
 # Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux).
 
 [update]
-# Windows builds are preview-only; the installer rejects "stable" here.
+# This machine intentionally follows the preview channel.
 # Re-asserted by the overlay as a single key so herdr's own [update] bookkeeping
 # (last-check timestamps etc.) survives an apply.
 channel = "preview"
 
 [theme]
 name = "catppuccin"           # mocha (dark)
 auto_switch = true            # follow OS light/dark
 light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
 dark_name = "catppuccin"
 
 [ui]
 mouse_capture = true
 pane_borders = true
 pane_gaps = true
 confirm_close = true
 show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true
 
 # "auto" draws herdr's own cursor on Windows to avoid ConPTY flicker;
 # set "native" to hand the cursor to the outer terminal. Windows-only key.
 host_cursor = "auto"
 
 # Agent sidebar ordering. herdr's default is "spaces" (grouped by space);
 # "priority" turns the panel into an attention queue (blocked/waiting agents
 # float to the top). With many concurrent agent panes the queue is what you
 # actually scan. Valid values: "spaces" | "priority".
 agent_panel_sort = "priority"
 
 # Expanded Agent sidebar row layout. herdr's own default is
 #   [["state_icon", "workspace", "tab"], ["agent"]]
 # and we append the `$review` metadata token so the review-pending ⭐
 # (prefix+m / hmark) is actually VISIBLE in the sidebar.
 #
 # Required since herdr 0.7.4: `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field
 # were replaced by a namespaced token map, and unlike custom_status a token is
 # rendered ONLY where a row layout names it — set a token with no layout entry
 # and the flag silently exists in the API but shows up nowhere.
 #
 # Keep `$review` in sync with $Token in dot_config/herdr/review-mark.ps1.
 # NOTE this pins the layout: upstream changes to the default rows will NOT reach
 # us, so re-check this block against `herdr --default-config` on herdr upgrades.
 [ui.sidebar.agents]
 rows = [
   ["state_icon", "workspace", "tab", "$review"],
   ["agent"],
 ]
 
 [terminal]
 # Match the rest of this repo (WezTerm / Windows Terminal default to pwsh).
 default_shell = "pwsh"
 # CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd):
 #   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
 #   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
 # NOTE (herdr >=0.7.x): with "follow", a NEW TAB inherits the FOCUSED pane's live
 # cwd — same as a split (herdr issue #912). NO new_cwd value opens a new tab at
 # the WORKSPACE ("space") dir — for that use the prefix+C command below.
 new_cwd = "follow"
 
 # --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
 # Only existing actions can be rebound; herdr defaults are kept for everything
 # not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings, so one action can
 # carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
 [keys]
 split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
 split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
 reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
 rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup
 new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit
 
 # --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
 # switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; these add the workspace + agent
 # analogs so a number key jumps directly. "N..M" is native herdr config syntax.
 # On the unix side prefix+SHIFT+digit was found unusable (under the kitty

 #!/usr/bin/env pwsh
 # chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
 #
 # Runs under pwsh via [interpreters.ps1] in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl. chezmoi pipes the
 # CURRENT target file into stdin and takes the new contents from stdout.
 #
 # WHY AN OVERLAY (this replaced a plain managed dot_config/herdr/config.toml):
 # herdr rewrites this file at runtime — the onboarding flag, in-app settings
 # popups, [session] / [remote] / [experimental] / [update] state. A plain managed
 # file clobbers all of that on every `chezmoi apply`, which can re-trigger
 # onboarding. The parent (unix) repo hit this and moved create_ -> modify_ on
 # 2026-07-06; this repo's config was added five days later and still used the
 # plain form. Same fix, ported.
 #
 # MERGE MODEL — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
 #   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
 #     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
 #   - Every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file that is NOT managed and NOT already in
 #     the template is copied across (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
 #     [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
 #   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins).
 #   - FORCED single keys are re-asserted INTO a pulled-through table, so the table
 #     keeps herdr's own bookkeeping. Windows needs exactly one: update.channel
 #     must stay "preview" (the installer rejects "stable" on Windows builds), but
 #     [update] also holds herdr's last-check state, which we do not want to wipe.
 #     This sub-key merge is the one deliberate divergence from the unix overlay.
 #
 # WHY tomlkit (not a hand-rolled emitter): herdr's config has an array-of-tables
 # ([[keys.command]]) and comments worth keeping; stdlib tomllib is read-only.
 # Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees >=3.11 -> stdlib tomllib), fall back to
 # system python, then to emitting the raw template (a fresh host with neither
 # still gets a full config — note we emit the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a

 #

+$allowPublicPackageFallback = {{ if (get . "allowPublicPackageFallback") }}$true{{ else }}$false{{ end }}

 {{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
 '@

 import os
 import sys
 
 tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
 live_path = os.environ["HERDR_LIVE_FILE"]
 out_path = os.environ["HERDR_OUT_FILE"]

     template_text = fh.read()
 
 
 def emit(text):

         fh.write(text)

     except ModuleNotFoundError:

 MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}

 FORCED = {("update", "channel"): "preview"}

         # let the template win only on the keys it actually sets.

22	#   - FORCED single keys are re-asserted INTO a pulled-through table, so the table
23	#     keeps herdr's own bookkeeping. Windows needs exactly one: update.channel
24	#     must stay "preview" (the installer rejects "stable" on Windows builds), but
25	#     [update] also holds herdr's last-check state, which we do not want to wipe.
26	#     This sub-key merge is the one deliberate divergence from the unix overlay.
27	#
28	# WHY tomlkit (not a hand-rolled emitter): herdr's config has an array-of-tables
29	# ([[keys.command]]) and comments worth keeping; stdlib tomllib is read-only.
30	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees >=3.11 -> stdlib tomllib), fall back to
31	# system python, then to emitting the raw template (a fresh host with neither
32	# still gets a full config — note we emit the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a
33	# fresh host stdin is empty).
34	#
35	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
36	# Validate the result with `herdr server reload-config` (empty diagnostics).
37	
38	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
39	
40	# modify_ scripts run under `pwsh -NoProfile`, so the deployed 05_mirrors.ps1
41	# fragment is not loaded here. Apply the same source policy inline before uv
42	# resolves tomlkit: managed machines must use the IT-approved pull-through feed.
43	{{ template "package-sources.ps1" . }}
44	$managedMachine = {{ if .managedMachine }}$true{{ else }}$false{{ end }}
45	$allowPublicPackageFallback = {{ if (get . "allowPublicPackageFallback") }}$true{{ else }}$false{{ end }}
46	{{ include "scripts/package-source-runner.ps1" }}
47	
48	# Emit bytes verbatim so nothing re-encodes the config's ⭐ / box-drawing glyphs
49	# and no BOM or trailing CRLF churn creeps into chezmoi's diff.
50	function Write-StdoutBytes {
51	    param([byte[]] $Bytes)
52	    $out = [Console]::OpenStandardOutput()
53	    $out.Write($Bytes, 0, $Bytes.Length)
54	    $out.Flush()
55	}
56	
57	$utf8 = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)   # no BOM
58	
59	$templateText = @'
60	{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
61	'@
62	
63	$liveText = [Console]::In.ReadToEnd()
64	
65	$tmpDir = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()
66	$stamp = [System.IO.Path]::GetRandomFileName()
67	$tmplFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-tmpl-$stamp.toml"
68	$liveFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-live-$stamp.toml"
69	$pyFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-merge-$stamp.py"
70	$outFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-out-$stamp.toml"
71	
72	try {
73	    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($tmplFile, $templateText, $utf8)
74	    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($liveFile, $liveText, $utf8)
75	
76	    # Pick a Python. uv is in this repo's scoop package set; `python` is the
77	    # uv-managed default install (--default --preview creates the unversioned shim).
78	    $py = $null
79	    $pyUsesPackageRunner = $false
80	    $uvCommand = Get-Command uv -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
81	    if ($uvCommand) {
82	        $py = @($uvCommand.Source, 'run', '--no-project', '--quiet', '--with', 'tomlkit', '--python', '>=3.11', 'python')
83	        $pyUsesPackageRunner = $true
84	    } else {
85	        $pythonCommand = Get-Command python -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
86	        if (-not $pythonCommand) {
87	            $pythonCommand = Get-Command python3 -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
88	        }
89	        if ($pythonCommand) { $py = @($pythonCommand.Source) }
90	    }
91	
92	    if (-not $py) {
93	        [Console]::Error.WriteLine('modify_config.toml: no uv/python found; emitting managed template (runtime keys not preserved this run)')
94	        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
95	        return
96	    }
97	
98	    $pySource = @'
99	import os
100	import sys
101	
102	tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
103	live_path = os.environ["HERDR_LIVE_FILE"]
104	out_path = os.environ["HERDR_OUT_FILE"]
105	
106	with open(tmpl_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
107	    template_text = fh.read()
108	
109	
110	def emit(text):
111	    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
112	        fh.write(text)
113	
114	
115	try:
116	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
117	except ModuleNotFoundError:
118	    try:
119	        import tomli as tomllib
120	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
121	        # No TOML reader -> can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is.
122	        emit(template_text)
123	        sys.exit(0)
124	
125	try:
126	    import tomlkit
127	except ModuleNotFoundError:
128	    print(
129	        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
130	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
131	        file=sys.stderr,
132	    )
133	    emit(template_text)
134	    sys.exit(0)
135	
136	# Tables the template owns outright.
137	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
138	# Single keys re-asserted into an otherwise pulled-through table.
139	FORCED = {("update", "channel"): "preview"}
140	
141	with open(live_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
142	    live_text = fh.read().strip()
143	
144	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
145	try:
146	    live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
147	except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
148	    # A corrupt live file must not block the apply — enforce the template.
149	    print("modify_config.toml: live config is not valid TOML; enforcing template", file=sys.stderr)
150	    live = {}
151	
152	for key, value in live.items():
153	    if key in MANAGED:
154	        continue
155	    if key in doc:
156	        # The template also declares this table. Keep herdr's runtime keys and
157	        # let the template win only on the keys it actually sets.
158	        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(doc[key], dict):
159	            for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
160	                if sub_key not in doc[key]:
161	                    doc[key][sub_key] = sub_value
162	        continue
163	    doc[key] = value
164	
165	for (table, sub_key), forced_value in FORCED.items():
166	    if table not in doc:
167	        doc[table] = tomlkit.table()
168	    doc[table][sub_key] = forced_value
169	
170	emit(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
171	'@
172	
173	    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($pyFile, $pySource, $utf8)
174	
175	    $childEnvironment = @{
176	        HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE = $tmplFile
177	        HERDR_LIVE_FILE = $liveFile
178	        HERDR_OUT_FILE = $outFile
179	    }
180	    $exe = $py[0]
181	    $rest = if ($py.Count -gt 1) { @($py[1..($py.Count - 1)]) + @($pyFile) } else { @($pyFile) }
182	    if ($pyUsesPackageRunner) {
183	        $result = Invoke-PackageSourceCommand -Manager uv -Executable $exe -Arguments $rest `
184	            -Operation herdr-tomlkit -ManagedMachine $managedMachine `
185	            -AllowPublicFallback $allowPublicPackageFallback -AdditionalEnvironment $childEnvironment `
186	            -OutputMode StandardError
187	        $rc = $result.ExitCode
188	    } else {
189	        $result = Invoke-CapturedPackageProcess -Executable $exe -Arguments $rest `
190	            -Environment $childEnvironment -OutputMode StandardError
191	        $rc = $result.ExitCode
192	    }
193	
194	    if ($rc -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outFile)) {
195	        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("modify_config.toml: merge failed (exit $rc); emitting managed template")
196	        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
197	        return
198	    }
199	
200	    Write-StdoutBytes ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($outFile))
201	} finally {
202	    foreach ($f in $tmplFile, $liveFile, $pyFile, $outFile) {
203	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $f -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
204	    }
205	}
206

1	{{- $herdrDir := printf "%s/.config/herdr" (.chezmoi.homeDir | replace "\\" "/") -}}
2	# herdr — native Windows terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (preview beta).
3	#
4	# Windows port of the parent dotfiles repo's .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
5	# It mirrors the tmux/unix keymap as closely as the Windows build allows; every
6	# binding that could NOT be carried over is listed in
7	# backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md with the reason.
8	#
9	# THIS FILE IS THE MANAGED BODY of a chezmoi modify_ overlay
10	# (dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl). The overlay enforces the tables
11	# below on every `chezmoi apply` and preserves the keys herdr writes back at
12	# runtime (onboarding / [session] / [remote] / [experimental] / [update] state).
13	# Tracking this as a PLAIN managed file — which is what this repo did before —
14	# clobbers that writeback and can re-trigger onboarding.
15	#
16	# Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
17	# Full default: `herdr --default-config`
18	# Validate after editing: `herdr server reload-config` (expect empty diagnostics)
19	#
20	# Helper-script paths are baked ABSOLUTE at render time on purpose: `pwsh -File`
21	# does NOT expand a leading `~` (verified), and herdr passes the command string
22	# through without shell tilde expansion on Windows.
23	#
24	# Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux).
25	
26	[update]
27	# This machine intentionally follows the preview channel.
28	# Re-asserted by the overlay as a single key so herdr's own [update] bookkeeping
29	# (last-check timestamps etc.) survives an apply.
30	channel = "preview"
31	
32	[theme]
33	name = "catppuccin"           # mocha (dark)
34	auto_switch = true            # follow OS light/dark
35	light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
36	dark_name = "catppuccin"
37	
38	[ui]
39	mouse_capture = true
40	pane_borders = true
41	pane_gaps = true
42	confirm_close = true
43	show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true
44	
45	# "auto" draws herdr's own cursor on Windows to avoid ConPTY flicker;
46	# set "native" to hand the cursor to the outer terminal. Windows-only key.
47	host_cursor = "auto"
48	
49	# Agent sidebar ordering. herdr's default is "spaces" (grouped by space);
50	# "priority" turns the panel into an attention queue (blocked/waiting agents
51	# float to the top). With many concurrent agent panes the queue is what you
52	# actually scan. Valid values: "spaces" | "priority".
53	agent_panel_sort = "priority"
54	
55	# Expanded Agent sidebar row layout. herdr's own default is
56	#   [["state_icon", "workspace", "tab"], ["agent"]]
57	# and we append the `$review` metadata token so the review-pending ⭐
58	# (prefix+m / hmark) is actually VISIBLE in the sidebar.
59	#
60	# Required since herdr 0.7.4: `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field
61	# were replaced by a namespaced token map, and unlike custom_status a token is
62	# rendered ONLY where a row layout names it — set a token with no layout entry
63	# and the flag silently exists in the API but shows up nowhere.
64	#
65	# Keep `$review` in sync with $Token in dot_config/herdr/review-mark.ps1.
66	# NOTE this pins the layout: upstream changes to the default rows will NOT reach
67	# us, so re-check this block against `herdr --default-config` on herdr upgrades.
68	[ui.sidebar.agents]
69	rows = [
70	  ["state_icon", "workspace", "tab", "$review"],
71	  ["agent"],
72	]
73	
74	[terminal]
75	# Match the rest of this repo (WezTerm / Windows Terminal default to pwsh).
76	default_shell = "pwsh"
77	# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd):
78	#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
79	#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
80	# NOTE (herdr >=0.7.x): with "follow", a NEW TAB inherits the FOCUSED pane's live
81	# cwd — same as a split (herdr issue #912). NO new_cwd value opens a new tab at
82	# the WORKSPACE ("space") dir — for that use the prefix+C command below.
83	new_cwd = "follow"
84	
85	# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
86	# Only existing actions can be rebound; herdr defaults are kept for everything
87	# not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings, so one action can
88	# carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
89	[keys]
90	split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
91	split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
92	reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
93	rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup
94	new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit
95	
96	# --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
97	# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; these add the workspace + agent
98	# analogs so a number key jumps directly. "N..M" is native herdr config syntax.
99	# On the unix side prefix+SHIFT+digit was found unusable (under the kitty
100	# keyboard protocol shift+1 still carries the printable "!"), hence ctrl/alt.
101	# Whether Windows/ConPTY behaves the same is UNVERIFIED — see the backlog note.
102	switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"    # prefix+ctrl+N → workspace N
103	focus_agent = "prefix+alt+1..9"          # prefix+alt+N  → jump to agent N's pane
104	
105	# --- Workspace navigate-mode: vim j/k (entered via prefix+w) ---
106	navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
107	navigate_workspace_up = ["k", "up"]
108	
109	# --- Custom command panes (the tmux-popup recreations) ---
110	# type = "pane": a temporary pane that closes when the command exits — herdr's
111	# analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. The command runs from the focused pane's
112	# cwd and gets $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID /
113	# $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD in its environment.
114	# type = "popup" (herdr >= 0.7.4) floats ABOVE the tiled layout instead, so
115	# nothing reflows — used for the two bindings you stay inside for a while.
116	
117	[[keys.command]]
118	key = "prefix+G"
119	type = "pane"
120	command = "lazygit"
121	description = "lazygit (popup pane)"
122	
123	# btop as a floating command pane (a real PTY that closes when you quit it).
124	# Quick Actions can't host this: herdr-plus runs an action with no PTY/stdin, so
125	# an interactive TUI exits immediately.
126	# NOTE: the unix config also binds prefix+N to nvtop — deliberately NOT ported,
127	# nvtop is Linux-only. See backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md.
128	[[keys.command]]
129	key = "prefix+M"
130	type = "pane"
131	command = "btop"
132	description = "btop system monitor (popup pane)"
133	
134	# --- Scratch shell as a real floating popup (prefix+`) --- DISABLED on Windows ---
135	# type = "popup" is NOT implemented in the herdr Windows preview
136	# (0.7.5-preview.2026-07-21): the parser rejects it with
137	#   invalid keybinding config: unknown variant `popup`, expected one of
138	#   `shell`, `pane`, `plugin_action` ... keeping current
139	# and drops the binding. Left DEAD (not revived as a tiled `pane`) per preference.
140	# To restore: uncomment and keep `type = "popup"` once a Windows preview ships it,
141	# or use `type = "pane"` for a tiled fallback (drop width/height — panes ignore
142	# them). See backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md item #2.
143	# [[keys.command]]
144	# key = "prefix+`"
145	# type = "popup"
146	# command = "pwsh"
147	# width = "85%"
148	# height = "80%"
149	# description = "scratch shell (popup)"
150	
151	# --- Run an arbitrary command in a floating popup (prefix+E) --- DISABLED on Windows ---
152	# Same reason as prefix+` above: `type = "popup"` is unknown to the herdr Windows
153	# preview (0.7.5-preview.2026-07-21) and the binding is rejected. Left DEAD per
154	# preference; restore/fallback notes are on the prefix+` block above.
155	# The generalisation of prefix+G: fzf-pick or type any command, run it in the
156	# FOCUSED PANE'S cwd, and the popup closes itself when the command exits.
157	# Enter runs the highlighted history entry; Alt+Enter runs exactly what you typed.
158	# Exit behaviour: closes on success, holds on failure. Override with
159	# $env:HERDR_RUN_HOLD = 'always'|'never'.
160	# [[keys.command]]
161	# key = "prefix+E"
162	# type = "popup"
163	# command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/run-command.ps1"'
164	# width = "80%"
165	# height = "70%"
166	# description = "run a command in the pane cwd (popup)"
167	
168	# --- New tab at the workspace ("space") root dir (prefix+C) ---
169	# herdr's native new-tab (prefix+c) and the mouse "+" button follow new_cwd,
170	# which on herdr >=0.7.x means the FOCUSED pane's live cwd. This binding instead
171	# opens a new tab at the workspace ROOT dir — the lowest-numbered tab's pane cwd,
172	# i.e. what herdr uses for the space label. prefix+c keeps native behaviour.
173	[[keys.command]]
174	key = "prefix+C"
175	type = "pane"
176	command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/new-tab-at-space-root.ps1"'
177	description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"
178	
179	# URL picker (tmux prefix+u analog — joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url). Reads the focused
180	# pane, fzf-picks a URL (same rewrites: http(s)/ftp/file, www., IP, git@ remote,
181	# quoted owner/repo, npm import), opens it with the Windows shell handler.
182	# Visible screen by default; `--source recent` scans full scrollback.
183	[[keys.command]]
184	key = "prefix+u"
185	type = "pane"
186	command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/url-pick.ps1"'
187	description = "URL picker — open a URL from the pane (fzf)"
188	
189	[[keys.command]]
190	key = "prefix+T"
191	type = "pane"
192	command = "tv herdr-sesh"
193	description = "Session / workspace / dir switcher (herdr-aware tv channel)"
194	
195	[[keys.command]]
196	key = "prefix+a"
197	type = "pane"
198	command = "tv herdr-agent-panes"
199	description = "Live agent panes (herdr-aware tv channel)"
200	
201	# --- Review-pending flag (mark-unread / ⭐) ---
202	# prefix+m toggles a per-pane "I still need to review this" flag (a herdr
203	# metadata token, orthogonal to agent state — it survives the pane going idle
204	# when you peek in). prefix+i opens the flagged-panes inbox.

207	type = "pane"
208	command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/review-mark.ps1" toggle'
209	description = "toggle review-pending flag (⭐) on the current pane"
210

212	key = "prefix+i"

215	description = "Review-pending inbox — flagged panes (herdr-aware tv channel)"
216	
217	# --- Copy focused-pane facts to the clipboard (prefix+P/D/V/S) ---
218	# One helper (pane-copy.ps1) distills a pane's data and pipes it to Set-Clipboard.
219	# The SAME four ops are also herdr-plus Quick Actions. Uppercase letters resolve
220	# to prefix+shift+<letter>; P/D/V/S avoid herdr's reserved shift builtins
221	# (shift+H/J/K/L swap-pane) and this repo's shift+B / shift+R.
222	[[keys.command]]

238	description = "copy pane content (visible screen)"

244	description = "copy pane content (full scrollback)"

246	# Copy a file PATH from the pane (extrakto-style). Extracts path-like tokens;
247	# two-tier: paths that EXIST under the pane cwd (copied as resolved absolute) on
248	# top, unverified candidates below a separator. Lowercase p pairs with the

250	[[keys.command]]

202	    if (-not (Have herdr)) { return }   # herdr install failed/skipped; nothing to add to
203	    $installed = $false
204	    try { $installed = ((herdr plugin list 2>&1) -join "`n") -match 'cloudmanic\.herdr-plus' } catch { $installed = $false }
205	    if ($installed) { Info 'herdr-plus plugin already installed'; return }
206	    if (-not (Have go)) {
207	        Info 'herdr-plus: skipped — needs go to build on Windows (scoop install go, or enable Extra runtimes)'
208	        return
209	    }
210	    Info 'herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus (backs prefix+y / prefix+O)'
211	    try {
212	        herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus --yes 2>&1 | Out-Host
213	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'herdr-plus' }
214	    } catch {
215	        Write-Warning "herdr-plus install error: $_"
216	        Register-Failure 'herdr-plus'
217	    }
218	}
219	
220	# --- Rime / Weasel (小狼毫) — Traditional Chinese input method ---------------
221	# Not routed through Winget-Install because two things need overriding:
222	#
223	#  1. The manifest is machine-scope NSIS, so `--scope user` can never work and
224	#     the install always raises UAC (same class as installWsl / installSshServer).
225	#  2. winget's silent switch for nullsoft is /S, and weasel's install.nsi maps a
226	#     bare /S to `WeaselSetup.exe /s` = register the TSF service as SIMPLIFIED
227	#     Chinese. Passing /T as well makes it use /t (Traditional) instead. Silent
228	#     mode also skips the 安裝選項 dialog and auto-runs WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy.
229	#
230	# `winget list` can't be used for the installed check: the manifest's ProductCode
231	# is "Weasel" but the ARP entry is the localized display name, so we read the
232	# InstallDir the NSIS installer writes to HKLM instead — which is also how we
233	# locate WeaselSetup.exe afterwards.
234	function Install-Weasel {
235	    $key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Rime\Weasel'
236	    $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
237	    if (-not $dir) {
238	        if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel (winget unavailable)'; return }
239	        Info 'winget install Rime.Weasel (machine scope — expect a UAC prompt)'
240	        winget install --id Rime.Weasel -e --silent --custom '/T' `
241	            --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
242	        $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
243	        if (-not $dir) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel'; return }
244	    } else {
245	        Info 'Weasel already installed'
246	    }
247	    # WeaselSetup's undocumented CLI (WeaselSetup/WeaselSetup.cpp). These two
248	    # only write HKCU, so they need no elevation and are safe to re-run.
249	    #   /lt          -> Weasel's own UI in 繁體中文
250	    #   /toggleascii -> Ctrl+Space toggles ASCII rather than the whole IME,
251	    #                   which is what makes global_ascii in weasel.custom.yaml
252	    #                   behave like a single 中/英 switch.
253	    $setup = Join-Path $dir 'WeaselSetup.exe'
254	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $setup) {
255	        & $setup /lt
256	        & $setup /toggleascii
257	    } else {
258	        Register-Failure 'weasel (WeaselSetup.exe not found; UI language + Ctrl+Space unset)'
259	    }
260	}

265	# Core CLI toolset — the shell baseline, always installed.
266	Scoop-Install @(
267	    'git', 'gh', 'glab', '7zip', 'make', 'just',
268	    'starship', 'zoxide', 'fzf', 'fd', 'ripgrep', 'bat', 'eza', 'glow', 'jq',
269	    'delta', 'lazygit', 'neovim', 'yazi', 'btop', 'pueue', 'television', 'tlrc',
270	    'uv', 'gnupg',
271	    # Runtimes are NATIVE via scoop, not mise: mise's activate/shims are
272	    # unreliable on Windows and it has no windows-arm64 bun build. node + bun
273	    # here; Python via uv (below); go/rust/ruby under Extra runtimes.
274	    # copilot-proxy needs bun/bunx.
275	    'nodejs-lts', 'bun',
276	    # LazyVim pins nvim-treesitter to the `main` branch, which compiles parsers
277	    # by shelling out to `tree-sitter build`. That CLI compiles via Rust's `cc`
278	    # crate, which only knows MSVC / GCC / Clang -- NOT zig (only the retired
279	    # `master` branch accepted zig). So the parser compiler must be a real gcc on
280	    # PATH; zig here does nothing. scoop's `gcc` is nuwen MinGW-w64, amd64-only --
281	    # which also matches the amd64 nvim (native on x64, x64-emulated on ARM64), so
282	    # this ONE line covers both arches (previously gcc was ARM64-only). Plus the
283	    # tree-sitter CLI `main` requires, and win32yank so `unnamedplus` yanks reach
284	    # the Windows clipboard. (Leaner gcc alt: scoop `mingw` = niXman MinGW-w64 UCRT.)
285	    'gcc', 'tree-sitter', 'win32yank'
286	)

289	# Pueue 4's built-in Windows service (autostart at login); non-elevated applies

295	# gh-dash: GitHub PR/issue dashboard TUI (`gh dash`). It's a gh extension, not a
296	# scoop package, so it needs gh to be authenticated -- this no-ops on a fresh
297	# machine until `gh auth login`. run_onchange only re-fires when this script
298	# changes, so after authenticating, install by hand (`gh extension install
299	# dlvhdr/gh-dash`) or force a reapply (`chezmoi state delete-bucket
300	# --bucket=entryState`). gh-notify / gh-select from the Unix repo are bash-only
301	# extensions and are intentionally skipped on Windows.
302	if (Have gh) {
303	    gh auth status *> $null
304	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
305	        $ghExts = gh extension list 2>$null | Out-String
306	        if ($ghExts -notmatch 'dlvhdr/gh-dash') {
307	            Info 'gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash'
308	            gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash
309	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'gh-ext:gh-dash' }
310	        }
311	    } else {
312	        Info 'gh not authenticated -- skipping gh-dash (gh auth login, then reapply)'
313	    }
314	}

320	# (not just python3.x) in UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR (~/.local/bin, on PATH via 00_env
321	# ahead of the Store's python.exe app-alias). On uv 0.8+ `--default` lives behind
322	# preview mode, so it must be paired with `--preview` (older uv just ignored it) —
323	# without it, current uv errors: "`--default` is only available in preview mode".
324	if (Have uv) {

336	    }

338	        Set-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -InstallationPolicy Trusted -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

399	# peon-ping — game-character voice lines for agent events (CESP player; packs
400	# from the OpenPeon registry). Installed regardless of the `agentSounds` tier so
401	# `peon preview` / `peon packs list` are always available to experiment with;
402	# the tier only decides whether HOOKS get wired, and that happens in
403	# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl.
404	#
405	# `--openpeon` reroots the whole install at the tool-agnostic ~/.openpeon so the
406	# installer never touches ~/.claude/settings.json — hook wiring is ours to
407	# declare (same rule the parent repo applies to workmux's `wm setup`).
408	# NB: the PowerShell installer's param block is
409	#   param([string[]]$Packs, [switch]$All, [string]$Lang, [switch]$Local,
410	#         [switch]$Global, [switch]$OpenPeon, [switch]$InitLocalConfig)
411	# — there is NO -NoRc (that is the bash install.sh flag only), and it does not
412	# touch $PROFILE, so nothing extra is needed to keep our profile clean.
413	# Idempotent: skipped once peon.ps1 exists.
414	$peonRoot = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon'
415	$peonHook = Join-Path $peonRoot 'hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
416	if (-not (Test-Path $peonHook)) {
417	    Info 'peon-ping (agent completion sounds, ~/.openpeon root)'
418	    try {
419	        # Upstream install.ps1 dot-sources scripts/install-utils.ps1 relative to
420	        # $PSScriptRoot when run via -File; it only self-downloads that helper
421	        # when $PSScriptRoot is empty (irm|iex). So stage BOTH files preserving
422	        # the scripts/ layout in a temp dir, then run install.ps1 with -File.
423	        $peonStage = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'peon-ping-install'
424	        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts') | Out-Null
425	        $peonInstaller = Join-Path $peonStage 'install.ps1'
426	        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
427	            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/install.ps1' `
428	            -OutFile $peonInstaller
429	        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
430	            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/scripts/install-utils.ps1' `
431	            -OutFile (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts\install-utils.ps1')
432	        & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $peonInstaller `
433	            -OpenPeon -Packs 'league_of_legends'
434	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping' }
435	        # The installer downloads the pack but leaves default_pack="peon" — a pack
436	        # that ships NO sounds — so a fresh install is silent ("No sound files
437	        # found for pack 'peon'"). Activate the pack we just seeded. Runs only on
438	        # first install (whole block is guarded on peon.ps1 absence), so a pack the
439	        # user later switches to via `peon packs use` is never clobbered.
440	        $peonCli = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\peon.cmd'
441	        if (Test-Path $peonCli) {
442	            & $peonCli packs use league_of_legends
443	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack' }
444	        } else {
445	            Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack (peon CLI shim missing)'
446	        }
447	    } catch {
448	        Register-Failure 'peon-ping'
449	    }
450	} else {
451	    Info 'peon-ping already installed — skipping (upgrade: peon update)'
452	}
453	{{ end -}}

455	{{ if .installSpecstoryBuild -}}
456	# EXPERIMENTAL SpecStory Windows CLI. There is no native-Windows release yet;
457	# Windows/WSL support lives in the unmerged getspecstory PR #191. Build it from
458	# source (opt-in) and drop specstory.exe in ~/.local/bin so the Copilot module's
459	# session auto-save (claude-copilot) can pick it up. Needs git (core) + go (enable
460	# Extra runtimes, or `scoop install go`). Treat as experimental — may break until
461	# the PR lands. Tracking + revisit criteria: backlog/specstory-windows-native-cli.md.
462	if ((Have git) -and (Have go)) {
463	    try {
464	        $ssCache = Join-Path $HOME '.cache\specstory-build'
465	        $ssRepo  = Join-Path $ssCache 'getspecstory'
466	        $ssBin   = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
467	        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $ssCache, $ssBin | Out-Null
468	        if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $ssRepo '.git'))) {
469	            Info 'specstory: cloning specstoryai/getspecstory'
470	            git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory.git $ssRepo
471	        }
472	        Push-Location $ssRepo
473	        try {
474	            Info 'specstory: fetching PR #191'
475	            $ssRemoteRef = 'refs/remotes/origin/pr-191'
476	            git fetch origin "pull/191/head:$ssRemoteRef" --force
477	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'git fetch of SpecStory PR #191 failed' }
478	            # Detached checkout leaves no local branch checked out, so the next
479	            # apply can safely force-refresh the remote-tracking ref above.
480	            git checkout --detach --force $ssRemoteRef
481	            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'git checkout of SpecStory PR #191 failed' }
482	            $ssOut = Join-Path $ssBin 'specstory.exe'
483	            Push-Location (Join-Path $ssRepo 'specstory-cli')
484	            try { Info "specstory: go build -> $ssOut"; go build -o $ssOut . } finally { Pop-Location }
485	            if (Test-Path $ssOut) { Info "specstory: built $ssOut" }
486	            else { Register-Failure 'specstory-build (go build produced no binary)' }
487	        } finally { Pop-Location }
488	    } catch {
489	        Write-Warning "specstory-build error: $_"
490	        Register-Failure 'specstory-build'
491	    }
492	} else {
493	    Register-Failure 'specstory-build (needs git + go; enable Extra runtimes or run: scoop install go)'
494	}
495	{{ end -}}

598	# opt-in secondary target with prompt + navigation parity only. Our starship.lua

600	# bridges have no scoop/winget manifest (and zoxide has no native cmd target), so
601	# -- like herdr -- we fetch them from upstream into the Clink profile dir at apply
602	# time. Network/offline failures are collected, never fatal; starship still works.
603	Scoop-Install @('clink')
604	if (Have clink) {

610	        'fzf.lua'    = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisant996/clink-fzf/master/fzf.lua'
611	    }
612	    foreach ($name in $clinkPlugins.Keys) {
613	        Info "clink plugin: $name"
614	        try { Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri $clinkPlugins[$name] -OutFile (Join-Path $clinkDir $name) }
615	        catch { Register-Failure "clink-plugin:$name" }
616	    }

618	    # reloads the profile scripts first -- so this must run AFTER fzf.lua is
619	    # downloaded above, else the setting is unknown and the value is silently
620	    # not persisted (the *> $null swallows the "unknown setting" error).

643	# translate -- terminal translator CLI+TUI (github.com/daviddwlee84/translate).
644	# There is no scoop/winget manifest and no prebuilt Windows release, so it is
645	# built from source with `go install` -- the same path the parent repo takes on
646	# Linux (dot_ansible/roles/go_tools); macOS there uses the Homebrew tap.
647	# GOBIN/GOPATH mirror that unix convention: the binary lands in ~/.local/bin
648	# (already on PATH via profile.d/00_env.ps1) and the module cache in
649	# ~/.local/share/go rather than recreating ~/go.
650	#
651	# It is pure Go (modernc.org/sqlite -- no cgo) and cross-compiles cleanly for
652	# windows/amd64 and windows/arm64. The FIRST build is slow (several minutes: the
653	# embedded swagger-ui bundle + sqlite); later applies no-op via the version check
654	# below. Bump $translateVersion to upgrade -- editing it re-renders this script,
655	# which is what re-fires the run_onchange. go.mod needs go >= 1.26.4; the default
656	# GOTOOLCHAIN=auto fetches a newer toolchain if scoop's go is older.
657	$translateVersion = 'v0.5.2'

661	    $trHave = ''
662	    # `translate --version` prints "translate version v0.5.2 ..."; a module-proxy
663	    # build carries no VCS metadata, so token 3 is exactly the module version. An
664	    # absent/unparseable answer just falls through to a reinstall, which is cheap
665	    # once the module cache is warm.
666	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin) {
667	        try { $trHave = ((& $trBin --version 2>$null) -split '\s+')[2] } catch { $trHave = '' }

674	        $env:GOPATH = Join-Path $HOME '.local\share\go'
675	        go install "github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@$translateVersion" 2>&1 | Out-Host
676	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin)) {
677	            Register-Failure "go:translate@$translateVersion"
678	        }
679	    }
680	} else {

682	}
683	{{ end -}}
684

687	# itself (gated in .chezmoiignore); 重新部署 happens in
688	# run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1 once the files are on disk.
689	Install-Weasel
690	{{ end -}}

692	if ($script:Failures.Count -gt 0) {

694	    $script:Failures | ForEach-Object { Write-Warning "  - $_" }

17	#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
18	#   - Every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file that is NOT managed and NOT already in
19	#     the template is copied across (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],

21	#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins).
22	#   - FORCED single keys are re-asserted INTO a pulled-through table, so the table

```text
1	#Requires -Version 7
2	# Guards hard invariant #1 (AGENTS.md): every init prompt in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl
3	# must have a matching non-interactive flag in .github/workflows/windows.yml.
4	#
5	# Why this exists: adding a prompt without the flag does not fail loudly at
6	# authoring time — it fails much later, on the Windows runner, as an opaque
7	#   error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF
8	# because `chezmoi init --no-tty` has no answer for the new question and hits
9	# end-of-input. That broke CI for three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds`
10	# was added. This test turns that into a local `Invoke-Pester` failure with the
11	# exact missing flag line to paste in.
12	#
13	# Matching is on the prompt's TEXT (3rd arg to promptXOnce), because that is
14	# what chezmoi's `--promptBool 'text=value'` parser keys on — not the variable
15	# name.
16	
17	BeforeAll {
18	    $repo = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent
19	    $tomlTmpl = Join-Path $repo '.chezmoi.toml.tmpl'
20	    $workflow = Join-Path $repo '.github/workflows/windows.yml'
21	
22	    # promptBoolOnce . "varName" "Prompt text" <default>
23	    $script:Prompts = [regex]::Matches(
24	        (Get-Content -Raw $tomlTmpl),
25	        'prompt(?<kind>Bool|String|Choice)Once\s+\.\s+"(?<var>[^"]+)"\s+"(?<text>[^"]+)"'
26	    ) | ForEach-Object {
27	        [pscustomobject]@{
28	            Kind = $_.Groups['kind'].Value
29	            Var  = $_.Groups['var'].Value
30	            Text = $_.Groups['text'].Value
31	        }
32	    }
33	
34	    # '--promptBool','Prompt text=value'
35	    $script:Flags = [regex]::Matches(
36	        (Get-Content -Raw $workflow),
37	        "'--prompt(?<kind>Bool|String|Choice)'\s*,\s*'(?<text>[^=']+)="
38	    ) | ForEach-Object {
39	        [pscustomobject]@{
40	            Kind = $_.Groups['kind'].Value
41	            Text = $_.Groups['text'].Value
42	        }
43	    }
44	}
45	
46	# NB: no angle brackets in Describe/It names — Pester expands `<...>` in test
47	# names as a data placeholder, so a name like "prompts <-> flags" is rewritten
48	# to `$-` and the whole file dies with a bogus CommandNotFoundException.
49	Describe 'init prompts vs CI flags (invariant #1)' {
50	    It 'finds prompts in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl' {
51	        $script:Prompts.Count | Should -BeGreaterThan 10
52	    }
53	
54	    It 'finds prompt flags in windows.yml' {
55	        $script:Flags.Count | Should -BeGreaterThan 10
56	    }

58	    It 'has a CI flag for every init prompt' {
59	        $flagText = @($script:Flags.Text)
60	        $missing = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object { $flagText -notcontains $_.Text })
61	        $hint = ($missing | ForEach-Object {
62	            "            '--prompt$($_.Kind)','$($_.Text)=<value>',   # $($_.Var)"
63	        }) -join "`n"
64	        $missing.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "windows.yml is missing these flags; add to the `$flags array:`n$hint"
65	    }
66	
67	    It 'has no stale CI flag without a matching prompt' {
68	        # Catches the other half of a rename: the prompt text changed but the
69	        # flag did not. chezmoi silently ignores an unmatched flag and then
70	        # blocks on the real prompt, so this would otherwise be invisible.
71	        $promptText = @($script:Prompts.Text)
72	        $stale = @($script:Flags | Where-Object { $promptText -notcontains $_.Text })
73	        $stale.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "these windows.yml flags match no prompt: $($stale.Text -join '; ')"
74	    }
75

431	            -OutFile (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts\install-utils.ps1')
432	        & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $peonInstaller `
433	            -OpenPeon -Packs 'league_of_legends'

444	        } else {
445	            Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack (peon CLI shim missing)'
446	        }

648	# (already on PATH via profile.d/00_env.ps1) and the module cache in
649	# ~/.local/share/go rather than recreating ~/go.

657	$translateVersion = 'v0.5.2'

663	    # build carries no VCS metadata, so token 3 is exactly the module version. An
664	    # absent/unparseable answer just falls through to a reinstall, which is cheap
665	    # once the module cache is warm.
666	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin) {
667	        try { $trHave = ((& $trBin --version 2>$null) -split '\s+')[2] } catch { $trHave = '' }
668	    }
669	    if ($trHave -eq $translateVersion) {
670	        Info "translate $translateVersion already installed"
671	    } else {
672	        Info "go install translate@$translateVersion (first build takes several minutes)"
673	        $env:GOBIN  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
674	        $env:GOPATH = Join-Path $HOME '.local\share\go'
675	        go install "github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@$translateVersion" 2>&1 | Out-Host
676	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin)) {
677	            Register-Failure "go:translate@$translateVersion"
678	        }
679	    }

67	        # works in a normal console, but an ELEVATED one is refused ("Running the

69	        # passed. Some dev boxes always open the shell as admin, so detect that and

72	        $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod get.scoop.sh))

78	            & $installer

90	function Scoop-Install([string[]]$apps) {
91	    if (-not $apps) { return }
92	    # Wrap in @() so a lone survivor stays an array. Without it PowerShell
93	    # unwraps a single match to a bare string, and `scoop install @missing`
94	    # then splats it one CHARACTER per arg => "Couldn't find manifest for 'm'"
95	    # when only "mise" was missing.
96	    $missing = @($apps | Where-Object { ($_ -split '/')[-1] -notin (Get-ScoopInstalled) })
97	    if (-not $missing) { Info 'scoop: all requested tools already present'; return }
98	    Info "scoop install: $($missing -join ', ')"
99	    try { scoop install @missing } catch { Write-Warning "scoop batch error: $_" }
100	    # Anything still absent after the batch = failed (scoop keeps going past a bad one).
101	    $after = Get-ScoopInstalled
102	    foreach ($app in $missing) {
103	        $name = ($app -split '/')[-1]
104	        if ($name -notin $after) { Register-Failure "scoop:$name" }
105	    }
106	}

112	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { return }   # already installed
113	    Info "winget install $id"

120	    }

138	function Npm-InstallGlobal([string[]]$pkgs) {
139	    if (-not (Have npm)) { foreach ($p in $pkgs) { Register-Failure "npm:$p (npm unavailable)" }; return }
140	    $npmExecutable = (Get-Command npm -CommandType Application | Select-Object -First 1).Source
141	    $npmRootOutput = @(npm root -g 2>$null)
142	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $npmRootOutput) {
143	        foreach ($p in $pkgs) { Register-Failure "npm:$p (cannot resolve global npm root)" }
144	        return
145	    }
146	    $npmRoot = ([string]$npmRootOutput[-1]).Trim()
147	    $npmPrefix = Split-Path -Parent $npmRoot
148	    $npmCacheOutput = @(npm config get cache 2>$null)
149	    $npmCache = if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0 -and $npmCacheOutput) { ([string]$npmCacheOutput[-1]).Trim() } else { '' }
150	    foreach ($p in $pkgs) {
151	        # Apply is install-only. Re-running `npm install -g` as an implicit
152	        # upgrade fails with EBUSY/EPERM whenever an agent executable is live on
153	        # Windows. A package.json is a cheap, registry-independent presence test.
154	        $packageManifest = Join-Path (Join-Path $npmRoot $p) 'package.json'
155	        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $packageManifest) {
156	            Info "npm: $p already installed -- skipping (upgrade: just upgrade-npm-agents)"
157	            continue
158	        }
159	        Info "npm i -g $p"
160	        $result = Invoke-PackageSourceCommand -Manager npm -Executable $env:ComSpec `
161	            -Arguments @('/d', '/c', $npmExecutable, 'install', '-g', $p) -Operation $p `
162	            -PackageSpec $p -NpmPrefix $npmPrefix -NpmCache $npmCache `
163	            -ManagedMachine $managedMachine -AllowPublicFallback $allowPublicPackageFallback
164	        if (-not $result.Succeeded) { Register-Failure "npm:$p" }
165	    }
166	}

674	        $env:GOPATH = Join-Path $HOME '.local\share\go'
675	        go install "github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@$translateVersion" 2>&1 | Out-Host
676	        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin)) {
677	            Register-Failure "go:translate@$translateVersion"

679	    }

46	# NB: no angle brackets in Describe/It names — Pester expands `<...>` in test
47	# names as a data placeholder, so a name like "prompts <-> flags" is rewritten
48	# to `$-` and the whole file dies with a bogus CommandNotFoundException.
49	Describe 'init prompts vs CI flags (invariant #1)' {
50	    It 'finds prompts in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl' {
51	        $script:Prompts.Count | Should -BeGreaterThan 10
52	    }
53	
54	    It 'finds prompt flags in windows.yml' {
55	        $script:Flags.Count | Should -BeGreaterThan 10
56	    }
57	
58	    It 'has a CI flag for every init prompt' {
59	        $flagText = @($script:Flags.Text)
60	        $missing = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object { $flagText -notcontains $_.Text })
61	        $hint = ($missing | ForEach-Object {
62	            "            '--prompt$($_.Kind)','$($_.Text)=<value>',   # $($_.Var)"
63	        }) -join "`n"
64	        $missing.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "windows.yml is missing these flags; add to the `$flags array:`n$hint"
65	    }
66	
67	    It 'has no stale CI flag without a matching prompt' {
68	        # Catches the other half of a rename: the prompt text changed but the
69	        # flag did not. chezmoi silently ignores an unmatched flag and then
70	        # blocks on the real prompt, so this would otherwise be invisible.
71	        $promptText = @($script:Prompts.Text)
72	        $stale = @($script:Flags | Where-Object { $promptText -notcontains $_.Text })
73	        $stale.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "these windows.yml flags match no prompt: $($stale.Text -join '; ')"
74	    }
75	
76	    It 'uses the right flag kind for each prompt' {
77	        $byText = @{}
78	        foreach ($f in $script:Flags) { $byText[$f.Text] = $f.Kind }
79	        $wrong = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object {
80	            $byText.ContainsKey($_.Text) -and $byText[$_.Text] -ne $_.Kind
81	        })
82	        $wrong.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "flag kind mismatch for: $($wrong.Var -join '; ')"
83	    }
84	
85	    It 'has no "=" in any prompt text' {
86	        # Invariant #1 corollary: chezmoi's `name=value` parser splits on the
87	        # FIRST "=", so a prompt whose text contains one can never be answered
88	        # non-interactively. This already broke the `role` prompt once.
89	        $bad = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object { $_.Text -match '=' })
90	        $bad.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "prompt text may not contain '=': $($bad.Var -join '; ')"
91	    }
92	
93	    It 'keeps public package fallback explicit and default-off' {
94	        $template = Get-Content -Raw $tomlTmpl
95	        $template | Should -Match 'allowPublicPackageFallback"\s+"Allow one public PyPI/npm retry after eligible corporate feed failures"\s+false'
96	        @($script:Prompts | Where-Object Var -eq 'allowPublicPackageFallback').Count | Should -Be 1
97	    }
98	
99	    It 'describes only package ecosystems with configured China mirrors' {
100	        $prompt = $script:Prompts | Where-Object Var -eq 'useChineseMirror'
101	        $prompt.Text | Should -Match 'pip/uv, npm, RubyGems, Go, and rustup'
102	        $prompt.Text | Should -Not -Match 'Cargo|Node'
103	    }
104	}
105
